**Surah al-Ma'idah**

It has one hundred and twenty verses. It was all revealed in Medina except His words, ﴿Today I have perfected your religion for you﴾, and the verse that follows it, which were revealed at 'Arafat.

﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.﴾

It is narrated from Abu Maysarah, who said: "Allah, may He be exalted, revealed in this surah eighteen rulings that He did not reveal in any other surah. They are His words: ﴿Forbidden to you are carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, that which has been dedicated to other than Allah, the strangled, the beaten to death, the fallen, the gored, and what a wild beast has eaten, except what you have slaughtered, and what is sacrificed on stone altars, and that you seek decision by arrows﴾; ﴿And [the game caught by] trained hunting animals that you train, teaching them as Allah has taught you﴾; ﴿The food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you, and your food is lawful for them. And [lawful for you are] chaste women from among the believers and chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you﴾. The completion of the purification is in His words: ﴿When you rise to prayer﴾; ﴿As for the thief, male or female﴾; ﴿Do not kill game while you are in the state of ihram﴾, to the end of the verse; ﴿Allah did not institute [such things as] bahirah or sa'ibah or wasilah or ham﴾; and His words: ﴿The testimony between you when death approaches one of you﴾."

[Narrated by al-Firyabi, Abu 'Ubayd, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu al-Shaykh from Abu Maysarah. See al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/4.]

* *

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, fulfil [your] contracts﴾. That is, [fulfil] the covenants. Al-Zajjaj said: "They are the most binding of covenants. It is said: 'I made a contract (' aqadtu) with so-and-so and bound myself to him (' aqadtu 'alayhi),' meaning I obligated him to that with firm assurance. Its origin is the tying of one thing to another and joining it to it, just as a rope is tied to a rope [when it is joined]." [Omitted in "B".]

The scholars differed regarding these contracts. Ibn Juraij said: "This is addressed to the People of the Book, meaning: O you who have believed in the earlier Scriptures, fulfil the covenants that I made with you concerning the matter of Muhammad (ﷺ). This is His words: ﴿And [mention] when Allah took the covenant of those who were given the Scripture: 'You must make it clear to the people and not conceal it'﴾ (Surah Al 'Imran, 187)."

Others said: "It is general." Qatadah said: "It refers to the alliance they made with one another in the Jahiliyyah (the time of ignorance before Islam)." Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "They are the covenants of faith and of the Qur'an." It was also said: "They are the contracts that people make among themselves."

﴿Lawful for you is the beast of grazing livestock﴾. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: "It refers to all grazing livestock, which are camels, cattle and sheep. He intended the permission of what the people of the Jahiliyyah had forbidden to themselves from among the livestock."

Abu Zabyan narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he said: "The beast of grazing livestock is the unborn young (ajinnah)." Similarly, al-Sha'bi said: "They are the unborn young that are found dead in the wombs of their mothers when the mothers are slaughtered or sacrificed." Most of the people of knowledge held that it is lawful.

[The Shaykh, the Imam said:] "I read to Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn al-Fadl al-Kharaqi, and I said: 'It was read to Abu Sahl Muhammad ibn 'Umar ibn Tarafah while you were present,' and it was said to him: 'Abu Sulayman al-Khattabi narrated to you: Abu Bakr ibn Dasah told us: Abu Dawud al-Sijistani told us: Musaddad told us: Hushaym told us, from Mujalid, from Abu al-Waddak, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with them, who said: We said: "O Messenger of Allah, we sacrifice a she-camel, and we slaughter a cow or a sheep, and we find in its belly a fetus. Shall we throw it away or eat it?" He said: "Eat it if you wish, for its slaughter is the slaughter of its mother."'"

[Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Adahi, chapter on what has come regarding the slaughter of the fetus: 4/118; and al-Tirmidhi in al-Sayd, chapter on what has come regarding the slaughter of the fetus, with the wording: "The slaughter of the fetus is the slaughter of its mother," and he said: "A hasan (good) hadith." Also al-Daraqutni in al-Sayd wa'l-Dhaba'ih wa'l-At'imah: 4/274; Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 3/31, 45, 53; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 11/228. All of them narrated it through the chain of Mujalid, from Abu al-Waddak, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri. 'Abd al-Haqq said: "None of its chains is to be used as proof." Al-Ghazali said: "It is a sahih (sound) hadith; no doubt reaches its text and no weakness reaches its chain." Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said: "There is room for examination here. The truth is that it contains what the proof can rest upon, namely the collection of its chains and the chains of the hadith of Jabir that follows immediately after this."

See: Talkhis al-Habir: 4/156–158; Nasb al-Rayah: 4/189–192; Mukhtasar al-Mundhiri li-Sunan Abi Dawud: 4/119–121.]

It was also narrated by Abu al-Zubayr from Jabir, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "The slaughter of the fetus is the slaughter of its mother."

[Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Dahaya, chapter on what has come regarding the slaughter of the fetus: 4/119; al-Darimi in al-Adahi, chapter on the slaughter of the fetus: 2/84; and al-Daraqutni: 4/273, with the wording "The fetus in its mother's belly is [to be eaten]." It was declared sahih by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak on the condition of Muslim, and al-Dhahabi agreed: 4/114.

Al-Haythami attributed it in al-Majma' (4/35) and al-Zayla'i in Nasb al-Rayah (4/189) to Abu Ya'la in his Musnad. The author also narrated it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 11/229.

Al-Mundhiri said: "Its chain includes 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ziyad al-Makki al-Qaddah, and there is some criticism of him." Al-Haythami said: "It includes Hammad ibn Shu'ayb, who is weak." Al-Albani declared it sahih in Irwa' al-Ghalil: 8/172.]

Some of them made the ish'ar (marking of the animal) a condition. Ibn 'Umar said: "The slaughter of what is in its belly is in its slaughter, once its form is complete and its hair has grown." Similarly, it is narrated from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab.

According to Abu Hanifah, may Allah be pleased with him, it is not lawful to eat the fetus if it comes out dead after the slaughter of the mother.

Al-Kalbi said: "The beast of grazing livestock refers to its wild kind, namely gazelles and wild cattle. It was called bahimah (beast) because it is made obscure (ubhimat) from discernment, and it was said: because it has no speech." ﴿Except what is recited to you﴾, that is, what was mentioned in His words: ﴿Forbidden to you is carrion﴾ up to His words: ﴿and what is sacrificed on stone altars﴾. ﴿Not hunting while you are in the state of ihram﴾: this is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause (hal), meaning: not hunting while you are in ihram. The meaning of the verse is: "The entire beast of grazing livestock is lawful for you, except what is of it wild, for that is game, which is not lawful for you while you are in the state of ihram. This is His words, may He be exalted: ﴿while you are in the state of ihram. Indeed Allah decrees what He wills﴾."

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 5, verse 2:**

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿O you who believe, do not violate the rites (shaʿāʾir) of Allah﴾. It was revealed concerning al-Ḥuṭam, whose name was Shurayḥ ibn Ḍubayʿah al-Bakrī. He came to Madinah and left his horses outside [[in "B": (outside of)]] Madinah, and he entered alone upon the Prophet ﷺ. He said to him: "To what do you invite the people?" He replied: "To the testimony that there is no god but Allah, [[omitted in "B"]] and to the establishment of prayer and the giving of zakat." He said: "Good [[in "B": (enough for me)]], but I have chiefs whom I do not decide any matter without. Perhaps I will embrace Islam and bring them with me." The Prophet ﷺ had said to his companions: "A man from Rabiʿah will enter upon you, speaking with the tongue [[in "B": (words)]] of a devil." Then Shurayḥ left his presence. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "He entered with the face of a disbeliever and left with the back of a treacherous one, and this man is not a Muslim." He passed by the herd of livestock of Madinah, drove it off and set out. They pursued him but could not catch him. The following year he set out for the pilgrimage (ḥajj) with the pilgrims of Bakr ibn Wāʾil from al-Yamamah, and with him was a great quantity of merchandise, and he had garlanded the sacrificial animal (hady). The Muslims said to the Prophet ﷺ: "This al-Ḥuṭam has set out for pilgrimage; let us be free to deal with him." The Prophet ﷺ said: "He has garlanded the sacrificial animal." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, this is something we used to do in the Jahiliyyah." The Prophet ﷺ refused, so Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not violate the rites of Allah﴾ [[See: Tafsir al-Ṭabarī: 9/472-473; al-Durr al-Manthūr: 3/9-10; Asbāb al-Nuzūl by al-Wāḥidī p. 219; Tafsir al-Qurṭubī: 6/43.]].

Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid said: they are the rites of the Hajj. The polytheists used to perform pilgrimage and bring sacrificial animals, and the Muslims wanted to raid them, so Allah forbade them from that.

Abū ʿUbaydah said: "The rites of Allah are the marked sacrificial animals (hadāyā mushʿarah). Ishʿār (marking) derives from shiʿār, which means a sign. Its ishʿār is making it known by what identifies it as a sacrificial animal. Ishʿār here means piercing the hump of a camel with an iron implement until blood flows, so that this is a sign that it is a sacrificial animal. This is the sunnah regarding sacrificial animals when they are camels, based on what was reported to us by ʿAbd al-Wāḥid al-Mulayḥī: Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Nuʿaymī told us, Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf told us, Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl told us, Abū Nuʿaym told us, Aflaḥ told us, from al-Qāsim, from ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her), that she said: 'I braided the garlands of the Prophet's ﷺ camels with my own hands, then he garlanded them, marked them and sent them as offerings, and nothing that had been permitted to him became forbidden to him'" [[Narrated by al-Bukhārī in al-Ḥajj, chapter on whoever marks and garlands at Dhū al-Ḥulayfah: 3/542; and Muslim in al-Ḥajj, chapter on the recommendation of sending the offering to the Ḥaram...: no. (1321), 2/957; and the author in Sharḥ al-Sunnah: 7/92.]].

Al-Shāfiʿī analogized cows to camels regarding ishʿār, but sheep are not marked by cutting, because they cannot bear cutting due to their weakness. According to Abū Ḥanīfah: the offering is not marked.

ʿAṭiyyah reported from Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both): "Do not violate the rites of Allah" means that you hunt while you are in the state of iḥrām, based on the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And when you have come out of iḥrām, then hunt﴾. Al-Suddī said: He meant the sanctuary (ḥaram) of Allah. It was also said: what is meant is the prohibition of killing within the sanctuary. ʿAṭāʾ said: "The rites of Allah are the sacred things of Allah, avoiding His wrath and following His obedience."

His saying: ﴿nor the sacred month﴾, meaning by fighting in it. Ibn Zayd said: it is the postponement (nasīʾ), for they used to make it lawful in the Jahiliyyah one year and forbid it another year. ﴿nor the offering (hady)﴾, which is everything brought as an offering to the House of Allah, whether a camel, a cow or a sheep. ﴿nor the garlands (qalāʾid)﴾, meaning the garlanded offerings, meaning those possessing garlands. ʿAṭāʾ said: he meant the owners of the garlands, because in the Jahiliyyah, when they wished to leave the sanctuary, they would garland themselves and their camels with some of the bark of the trees of the sanctuary so that they would not be attacked, so the Sharīʿah forbade making lawful any part of them. Muṭarrif ibn al-Shikhkhīr said: "They are the garlands themselves, for the polytheists used to take bark from the trees of Makkah and wear it as garlands, so they were forbidden to strip its trees."

His saying the Exalted: ﴿nor those coming to the Sacred House﴾, meaning those intending the Sacred House, that is the Kaʿbah, so do not molest them. ﴿seeking﴾, meaning seeking, ﴿bounty from their Lord﴾, meaning provision through trade, ﴿and approval﴾, meaning according to their assumption, because the disbelievers have no share in the approval. Qatādah said: it is that He sets right their livelihood in this world and does not hasten punishment for them in it. It was also said: seeking bounty is general for believers and polytheists, while seeking approval is specific to believers, because Muslims and polytheists used to perform pilgrimage. This verse up to this point has been abrogated (mansūkhah, naskh) by His saying: "Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them" (Sūrat al-Tawbah, 5), and by His saying: "So let them not approach the Sacred Mosque after this year of theirs" (Sūrat al-Tawbah, 28). Thus it is not permissible for a polytheist to perform pilgrimage, nor for a disbeliever to be given security with the offering and the garlands.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And when you have come out of your iḥrām﴾, ﴿then hunt﴾. It is a command of permission (amr ibāḥah), permitting the one not in iḥrām to take game, like His saying the Exalted: ﴿And when the prayer is concluded, disperse in the land﴾ (al-Jumuʿah, 10).

﴿And do not let hatred of a people﴾. Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatādah said: "Let not ... incite you." It is said: Fulān incited me (jaramanī) to do such-and-such, meaning it drove me to it. Al-Farrāʾ said: "Let not ... earn for you", it is said: jarama meaning earned, and Fulān is the jarīmat ahlihi, meaning their earner. It was also said: "Let not ... call you." ﴿hatred﴾ meaning their animosity and enmity, and it is the verbal noun of shanaʾta (you hated). Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Bakr read shanʾān qawmin with the first nūn sukūn (sukūn on the first nūn), and the others read it with a fatḥah, and both are dialects, but the fatḥah is better, because most verbal nouns are of the pattern faʿalān with fatḥah on the ʿayn, like ḍarabān, sayalān, naslān and similar. ﴿that they barred you from the Sacred Mosque﴾: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read it with a kasrah on the alif, as a resumption (istiʾnāf), and the others read it with a fatḥah on the alif, meaning "because they barred you." The meaning of the verse: let not the enmity of a people move you to transgression because they barred you. Muḥammad ibn Jarīr said: because this surah was revealed after the incident of al-Ḥudaybiyyah, and the barring had already occurred. ﴿that you transgress﴾ against them by killing and taking their property. ﴿And cooperate﴾, meaning let some of you help one another, ﴿in righteousness and piety﴾. It was said: righteousness is following the command, and piety is avoiding the prohibition. It was also said: righteousness is Islam, and piety is the sunnah. ﴿And do not cooperate in sin and aggression﴾. It was said: sin is disbelief, and aggression is injustice. It was also said: sin is disobedience, and aggression is innovation (bidʿah).

101 Abū al-Qāsim ʿAbd al-Karīm ibn Hawāzin al-Qushayrī informed us: Abū ʿAbd Allāh Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Ṭāhir al-Daqqāq told us in Baghdad: Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Zubayr al-Qurashī informed us: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿAffān told us: Zayd ibn al-Ḥubāb told us, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Ṣāliḥ, who said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Jubayr ibn Nufayr ibn Mālik al-Ḥaḍramī narrated to me, from his father, from al-Nawwās ibn Samʿān al-Anṣārī, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about righteousness and sin, and he said: "Righteousness is good character, and sin is that which troubles your soul and you dislike that people should see it" [[Narrated by Muslim in al-Birr wa al-Ṣilah, chapter on the explanation of righteousness and sin, no. (2553), 4/1980; and the author in Sharḥ al-Sunnah: 13/76.]].

﴿And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is severe in punishment.﴾

The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 5, verse 3 (part 1 of 2):

His, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: ﴿Forbidden to you are carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than Allah﴾, i.e., that over whose slaughter the name of other than Allah the Exalted has been invoked. ﴿And the strangled animal﴾, which is the one that is strangled and dies. Ibn 'Abbas said: The people of the Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance before Islam) used to strangle the sheep, and when it died they would eat it. ﴿And the beaten animal﴾ is the one killed by a stick. Qatadah said: They used to strike it with a staff, and when it died they would eat it. ﴿And the fallen animal﴾ is the one that falls from a high place or into a well and dies. ﴿And the animal killed by goring﴾ is the one that another animal gores and it dies. The feminine ending (ha' al-ta'nith) enters the form fa'il (here fa'il is written as fa'eel) when it has the meaning of the active participle; when it has the meaning of the passive participle, the masculine and feminine are equal in it, as in 'ayn kahil (a kohl-darkened eye) and kaff khadib (a dyed hand). When you omit the noun and use the adjective alone, they add the ha', saying: ra'ayna kahilah wa khadibah (we saw a kohl-darkened [female] and a dyed [female]). Here the ha' was added because the noun did not precede it; if the ha' were dropped, one would not know whether the adjective is feminine or masculine. Similar to this are al-dhabihah (the slaughtered [female]) and al-nasikah (the sacrificed [female]), and akilat al-sabu' (the one eaten by a beast of prey). ﴿And that which a beast of prey has eaten﴾ means what remains of what a beast of prey has eaten, and the people of the Jahiliyyah used to eat it. ﴿Except what you have slaughtered (dhakkaytum)﴾, meaning: except what you have reached while its dhakah (ritual slaughter) is still possible, from among these things.

The root meaning of tadhkiyah (ritual slaughter) is completion. It is said: dhakkaytu al-nar (I completed the kindling of the fire) when you completed its ignition. Here it means completing the cutting of the two jugular veins (al-awdaj) and the flowing out of the blood. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whatever makes the blood flow and over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, eat it, except the tooth and the nail" [[Reported by al-Bukhari in Slaughter and Hunting, chapter "What causes the blood to flow of reed, flint, and iron": 9/631, and Muslim in Sacrifices, chapter "The permissibility of slaughtering with anything that makes the blood flow, except the tooth, the nail, and the rest of the bone," no. (1968): 3/1558.]].

The minimum of dhakah in an animal that can be controlled is cutting the windpipe (al-mari') and the throat (al-hulqum). It is also permissible to cut the two jugular veins along with them. Slaughter is permitted with any sharp instrument that cuts, whether of iron, reed, glass, or stone, except the tooth and the nail, for the Prophet (ﷺ) forbade slaughtering with them. An animal that has been wounded by a beast of prey and has eaten some of it is lawful only if you reach it while life remains stable in it and you slaughter it. As for an animal that, by the wound of the beast of prey, has come to the state of one already slaughtered, it has the ruling of carrion and is not lawful even if you slaughter it. Likewise, the fallen animal and the gored animal, if you reach them alive before they come to the state of the slaughtered, and slaughter them, they are lawful. If someone shoots at game in the air and hits it, and it falls to the ground and dies, it is lawful, because falling to the ground is inherent in it. But if it falls onto a mountain, a tree, or a roof and then tumbles from it and dies, it is not lawful, and it is of the category of the fallen animal, unless the arrow struck its throat in the air, in which case it is lawful wherever it falls, because the slaughter was accomplished by the arrow striking the throat.

﴿And that which is sacrificed on the nusub (stone altars)﴾. It has been said: al-nusub is a plural whose singular is nisab; it has also been said: it is a singular whose plural is anṣab, like 'unuq and a'naq, and it means the thing that is set up.

They differed about it. Mujahid and Qatadah said: Around the House there were three hundred and sixty stones set up, which the people of the Jahiliyyah worshipped, venerated, and slaughtered for; and they were not idols, for the idols are the carved and engraved images. Others said: They are the idols that were set up, and the meaning is: that which is slaughtered in the name of the nusub. Ibn Zayd said: "That which is sacrificed on the nusub" and "that which has been dedicated to other than Allah" are one and the same. Qutrub said: 'ala here has the meaning of li (for), i.e., that which is slaughtered for the sake of the nusub.

﴿And that you seek decision by the arrows (al-azlam)﴾, i.e., and forbidden to you is seeking the decision (al-istiqsam) by the arrows. Al-istiqsam is seeking a division and a ruling from the arrows. Al-azlam are the arrow-shafts (al-qidah) that have neither feathers nor head; their singular is zalm, and zulm with a fatha and a damma on the zay. Their arrows were seven shafts, straight, of shawhat wood [[Al-shawhat: a tree from which bows are made. (al-Qamus al-Muhit: 2/680). See also: al-Maysir wa al-qidah by Ibn Qutaybah, pp. 44 and following.]], kept with the custodian of the Ka'bah. On one was written "Yes," on one "No," on one "From you," on one "From other than you," on one "Attached," on one "The blood-money," and one was blank with nothing written on it. When they wanted to do something, a journey, a marriage, a circumcision, or other, or when they disputed about a lineage or differed about bearing a blood-money, they came to Hubal, which was the greatest of the idols of Quraysh in Makkah, and brought a hundred dirhams and gave them to the owner of the arrows, until he shuffled the arrows. They would say: "O our god, we intend such and such," and if "Yes" came out they did it, and if "No" came out they did not do it that year. Then they returned to the arrows a second time. If they were shuffling over a lineage, and "From you" came out, he was a middling one among them; if "From other than you" came out, he was an ally; if "Attached" came out, he remained in his rank, having neither lineage nor alliance. If they differed over a blood-money, whoever the arrow of the blood-money came out against bore it; and if the blank one came out, they shuffled again until the inscribed one came out. Allah the Mighty and Majestic forbade that and prohibited it, and said: ﴿That is ungodliness (fisq)﴾. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: The azlam are white pebbles with which they cast lots. Mujahid said: They are the dice of Persia and Rome with which they gambled. Al-Sha'bi and others said: The azlam are for the Arabs, and the kiʿab (dice) are for the non-Arabs. Sufyan ibn Waki' said: They are chess. It has been narrated to us that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Augury (al-iyafah), drawing lines (al-tarq), and omens (al-tiyarah) are from jibt (sorcery)" [[Reported by Abu Dawud in Medicine, chapter "On drawing lines and deterring birds": 5/373; Ahmad in al-Musnad: 3/477, 5/60; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 12/177. al-Mundhiri attributed it to al-Nasa'i. al-Nawawi said: its chain is good. See Fayd al-Qadir: 4/396.]]. What is meant by al-tarq is striking with pebbles.

Abu Sa'id al-Shurayhi informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us: Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Ibn al-Fadl al-Kindi informed us: al-Hasan ibn Dawud al-Khashshab informed us: Suwayd ibn Sa'id informed us: [Abu al-Mukhtar] [[In "B": Abu al-Mahyah. He is Yahya ibn Ya'la al-Taymi, trustworthy, of the eighth tabaqah. (al-Taqrib).]] from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, from Raja' ibn Haywah, from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever practises soothsaying, or seeks decision by arrows, or is deterred by an omen that turns him back from his journey, will not look upon the high degrees of Paradise on the Day of Resurrection" [[Al-Haythami attributed it to al-Tabarani in al-Awsat and said: in it is Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Abi Yazid, and he is a liar. Majma' al-Zawa'id: 1/128. Abu Nu'aym also reported it in al-Hilyah: 5/174, and said: it is strange from the hadith of al-Thawri from 'Abd al-Malik; Muhammad ibn al-Hasan alone transmitted it.]].

His, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: ﴿Today those who disbelieve have despaired of your religion﴾, meaning: that you would return to their religion as disbelievers. That is because the disbelievers used to hope that the Muslims would return to their religion; when Islam became strong, they despaired. Yaisa and ayisa have the same meaning.

﴿So fear them not, but fear Me. Today I have perfected for you your religion, completed My favour upon you, and approved for you Islam as a religion﴾. This verse was revealed on Friday, the Day of 'Arafah, after the afternoon prayer, during the Farewell Pilgrimage, while the Prophet (ﷺ) was standing at 'Arafat upon his she-camel al-'Adba'; the camel's foreleg was nearly broken from the weight, so she knelt down.

'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed me: al-Hasan ibn al-Sabah heard Ja'far ibn 'Awn inform us: Abu al-'Umays informed us: Qays ibn Muslim informed us, from Tariq ibn Shihab, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), that a man of the Jews said to him: "O Commander of the Believers, there is a verse in your Book that you recite; had it been revealed to us, the community of the Jews, we would have taken that day as a festival." He said: "Which verse?" He said: "Today I have perfected for you your religion, completed My favour upon you, and approved for you Islam as a religion." 'Umar said: We know the day and the place in which it was revealed to the Prophet (ﷺ), who was standing at 'Arafah on the day of Friday [[Reported by al-Bukhari in Tafsir, Surah al-Ma'idah, chapter "Today I have perfected for you your religion...": 8/270, and in Iman and I'tisam. Reported by Muslim in Tafsir, no. (3017): 4/2313.]]. 'Umar indicated that that day was a festival for us.

Ibn 'Abbas said: On that day there were five festivals: Friday, 'Arafah, and the festivals of the Jews, the Christians, and the Magians; and the festivals of the people of the religions have never coincided on one day before it or after it.

Harun ibn 'Antarah narrated from his father, who said: When this verse was revealed, 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) wept. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "What makes you weep, O 'Umar?" He said: "What made me weep is that we were in an increase in our religion; but when it is completed, nothing has ever been completed except that it diminished." He said: "You have spoken the truth" [[Reported by al-Tabari in Tafsir: 9/519; al-Suyuti attributed it to Ibn Abi Shaybah. See al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/18.]].

This verse was the announcement of the Prophet's (ﷺ) death; he lived after it eighty-one days, and he died on Monday, after the sun had declined, two nights having passed of the month of Rabi' al-Awwal [in the year eleven after the Hijrah; it has been said: he died on the twelfth of the month of Rabi' al-Awwal]. [[What is between the brackets is absent from "B".]] His migration was on the twelfth.

His, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: ﴿Today I have perfected for you your religion﴾, meaning: on the day this verse was revealed, I perfected for you your religion, i.e., the obligations, the sunan (recommended practices), the hudud (prescribed punishments), the jihad, the rulings, the lawful and the unlawful. Nothing lawful or unlawful was revealed after this verse, nor anything of the obligations. This is the meaning of the saying of Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with both of them). It is also narrated from him that the verse on usury (riba) was revealed after it.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Qatadah said: "I have perfected for you your religion" means that no polytheist performed the Hajj with you.

It has been said: I made your religion manifest and granted you security from the enemy.

His, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: ﴿And completed My favour upon you﴾, meaning: and I fulfilled My promise in the saying "and that I may complete My favour upon you" (Surah al-Baqarah, 150). Among the completion of His favour was that they entered Makkah secure, dominant over it, and performed the Hajj at peace, with no polytheist mixing with them. ﴿And approved for you Islam as a religion﴾. I heard 'Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi say: I heard Abu Muhammad ibn Abi Hatim say: I heard Abu Bakr al-Nisaburi say: I heard Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Musayyab al-Marwazi say: I heard Abu Hatim Muhammad ibn Idris al-Handhali say: I heard 'Abd al-Malik ibn Maslamah say: Marwan al-Misri informed me: I heard Ibrahim ibn Abi Bakr ibn al-Munkadir (may Allah be pleased with him) say: I heard my paternal uncle Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir say: I heard Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah (may Allah be pleased with him) say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Jibril (peace be upon him) said: Allah the Exalted said: This is a religion I have approved for Myself, and nothing will set it right except generosity and good character; so honour it with them as long as you keep company with it" [[Reported by al-Tabarani in al-Awsat from Jabir, and similarly from 'Imran ibn Husayn. al-Asbahani narrated it, and al-Mundhiri mentioned it in the weak form in al-Targhib wa al-Tarhib: 3/383, 406. al-Haythami said: "al-Tabarani narrated it, and in it is 'Amr ibn al-Husayn al-'Uqayli, who is abandoned" Majma' al-Zawa'id: 3/248. al-Albani mentioned it in Silsilat al-Ahadith al-Da'ifah, no. (1282): 3/441-442. See also a study titled: Inna al-Din 'inda Allah al-Islam, in Majallat al-Buhuth al-Islamiyyah, issue (16).]]

He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿But whoever is compelled by hunger﴾, meaning: whoever is driven by severe hunger (fi makhmasah), and al-makhmasah is the emptiness of the stomach of food. It is said: "a man is khamis al-batn" when he is tawi (empty-bellied) and khawi (hollow). ﴿Without inclining toward sin﴾, meaning: without being inclined to sin, which is to eat beyond satiety. Qatadah said: "without deliberately going toward disobedience in his intention." ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. There is an ellipsis here, meaning: so he eats it, for indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.

Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Marwazi informed us: Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Siraj al-Tahhan informed us: Abu Ahmad Muhammad ibn Quraysh ibn Sulayman informed us: Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Makki informed us: Abu Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Sallam informed us: Muhammad ibn Kathir informed us, from al-Awza'i, from Hassan ibn Atiyyah, from Abu Waqid al-Laythi, who said: A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, we are in a land where hunger afflicts us, so when is carrion lawful for us?" He (ﷺ) said: "As long as you have not taken a morning drink or an evening drink from it, or gathered a herb from it with your hands, then it is your affair."¹

¹ Narrated by Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad (5/218), and al-Darimi in al-Adahi, chapter on eating carrion for the one compelled (2/88). It was also narrated by al-Bayhaqi and al-Tabarani; its narrators are trustworthy, but its chain has a break, as Hassan ibn Atiyyah did not hear from Abu Waqid al-Laythi, and there is disagreement regarding Abu Waqid's companionship. The author also narrated it in Sharh al-Sunnah (11/347), and Ibn Kathir cited it with Imam Ahmad's narration and said: "It is a sound chain according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs." The phrase "tahtafi'uha baqlan" (gathering it as a herb): Abu Ubayd said: "It has reached me that it is from al-hifa' (hamzated, with a short vowel), which is the root of the white, moist papyrus, and it is eaten. He means: as long as you have not uprooted this very thing and eaten it." It was also said that the correct wording is "ma lam tahtufuha biha baqlan" (with a light fa', unhamzated), and everything that is uprooted is called ihtufiya, as in ihfa' al-sha'r (plucking hair). It is said: "ihtafa al-rajulu yahtafi" when he takes from the surface of the earth with the tips of his fingers. He said: the meaning of the hadith is: what is lawful for you of it, meaning of the carrion, is only the morning drink, which is the midday meal, or the evening drink, which is the supper; so it is not permitted for you to combine both from the carrion. They rejected this from Abu Ubayd, and said: its meaning is: if you do not find a morning drink or an evening drink, and you do not find a herb to eat, then carrion becomes lawful for you... See Sharh al-Sunnah: 11/347-348.

**Commentary on the words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿They ask you what has been made lawful for them﴾, to the end of the verse.** Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: This verse was revealed concerning 'Adi ibn Hatim and Zayd ibn al-Muhalhil al-Ta'i, who is Zayd al-Khayl, whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) named Zayd al-Khayr. They said: "O Messenger of Allah, we are a people who hunt with dogs and falcons, so what is lawful for us from them?" Then this verse was revealed. [[Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim on the authority of Sa'id ibn Jubayr. See al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/20; Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, pp. 222-223.]]

It is also said that the occasion of its revelation was that when the Prophet (ﷺ) ordered the killing of dogs, they said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is lawful for us from this community that you have ordered to be killed?" Then this verse was revealed. [[Narrated by al-Hakim on the authority of Abu Rafi', 2/311, and he declared it sound, and al-Dhahabi agreed. See Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, p. 221; al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/21.]] When it was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) permitted the keeping of dogs that are beneficial, and forbade keeping those of no benefit.

We were informed by Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Salihi: Abu al-Husayn 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Bishran informed us: Isma'il ibn Muhammad al-Saffar informed us: Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi informed us: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar informed us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Salama, on the authority of Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever keeps a dog, other than a herding dog, a hunting dog or a farming dog, his reward is reduced by one qirat every day." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Harth wa al-Muzara'a, chapter on keeping a dog for farming: 5/5, with the wording "Whoever keeps a dog, his deeds are reduced by one qirat every day, except a dog for farming or herding." Also narrated by Muslim in al-Musaqat, chapter on ordering the killing of dogs and explaining its abrogation, and the prohibition of keeping them except for hunting, farming, herding and the like (1575): 3/1203; and by the author in Sharh al-Sunna: 11/209.]]

The first opinion is more sound regarding the occasion of the revelation of this verse.

**﴿Say: Lawful for you are the good things﴾**: that is, the slaughtered animals over which the name of Allah the Exalted has been mentioned. It is also said: everything that the Arabs find good and enjoyable, provided no text from the Book or the Sunna has been revealed prohibiting it. **﴿And [those animals] which you have trained from the hunting beasts﴾**: that is, lawful for you is the game caught by the hunting beasts (al-jawarih) you have trained.

They differed concerning these hunting beasts (al-jawarih, predatory animals used for hunting). Al-Dahhak and al-Suddi said: they are dogs only, and what is caught by other than a dog is not lawful unless one reaches its ritual slaughter (dhakah). This view is not acted upon. Rather, the majority of the people of knowledge (ahl al-'ilm) hold that what is meant by al-jawarih and al-kawasib (predators that take prey) includes beasts of prey such as the leopard, the panther and the dog, and birds of prey such as the falcon, the eagle and the hawk, and the like, of whatever accepts training. Thus the game caught by all of them is lawful. They were called jarihah (from jarh, "wound" or "gain") because they gain for their owners their sustenance from game, i.e., their earnings. It is said: "So-and-so is the jarihah of his family," meaning their earner.

**﴿Trained﴾ (mukallibin)**: al-mukallib is one who incites dogs to hunt, and it is also said of one who trains them, mukallib. Al-Kallab is the owner of dogs, and it is also said of one who hunts with them, kallab. The word mukallibin is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause (hal), meaning: while you are training these beasts, i.e., inciting them to hunt. Dogs are mentioned because they are the most common and the most widespread, and what is meant is all hunting beasts.

**﴿You teach them﴾**: you train them in the manners of seizing game. **﴿From what Allah has taught you﴾**: that is, from the knowledge which Allah has taught you. Al-Suddi said: that is, as Allah has taught you, with "min" in the sense of "ka" (like).

**﴿Then eat of what they catch for you﴾**: he means that if the trained hunting beast is sent forth by its owner, then seizes the game and kills it, it is lawful. Training is established when three things are found in it: when it is sent, it goes; when it is restrained, it stops; and when it seizes the game, it holds it and does not eat it. If this is repeatedly found in it, at least three times, it is considered trained, and it is lawful to kill (game) with it when it is sent forth by its owner.

We were narrated to by 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Musa ibn Isma'il informed us: Thabit ibn Zayd informed us, on the authority of 'Asim, on the authority of al-Sha'bi, on the authority of 'Adi ibn Hatim, on the authority of the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "If you send forth your trained dog and mention the name of Allah, and it holds [the game] and kills it, then eat. If it eats [from it], then do not eat, for it has only held it for itself. If it mixes with dogs over which the name of Allah was not mentioned, and they hold and kill, then do not eat, for you do not know which of them killed it. If you shoot at game and find it after a day or two with no trace but the mark of your arrow, then eat. If it falls into water, do not eat." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Dhaba'ih wa al-Sayd, chapter on game that is absent for two or three days: 9/610; and by Muslim in al-Sayd wa al-Dhaba'ih, chapter on hunting with trained dogs, no. (1929): 3/1531, with similar wording; and by the author in Sharh al-Sunna: 11/191-192.]]

They differed concerning the case where the (trained) beast seizes game and eats some of it. Most of the people of knowledge held that it is forbidden. This is related from Ibn 'Abbas, and it is the view of 'Ata', Tawus and al-Sha'bi. It is also the view of al-Thawri, Ibn al-Mubarak and the companions of opinion (ashab al-ra'y), and it is the sounder of the two positions of al-Shafi'i, because of the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying: "If it eats, then do not eat, for it has only held it for itself."

Some scholars permitted eating it. This is related from Ibn 'Umar, Salman al-Farisi and Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, and Malik also held this view, based on what is related from Abu Tha'laba al-Khushani, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If you send your dog and mention the name of Allah the Exalted, then eat, even if it has eaten from it." [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Dahaya, chapter on game: 4/136; and by the author in Sharh al-Sunna: 11/195.

Al-Mundhiri said in Mukhtasar al-Sunan: "Its chain includes Dawud ibn 'Amr al-Awdi al-Dimashqi, governor of Wasit. Yahya ibn Ma'in declared him trustworthy. Imam Ahmad said: 'A hadith that is close (to sound).' Abu Zur'a said: 'There is no harm in him.' ... Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-'Ijli said: 'He is not strong.'"]]

As for a hunting beast other than a trained one that seizes game, or a trained one that goes forth without its owner's sending, and it seizes and kills, then it is not lawful unless its owner reaches it alive and slaughters it, in which case it becomes lawful.

We were informed by 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: 'Abd Allah ibn Yazid informed us: Haywa informed us: Rabi'a ibn Yazid al-Dimashqi informed me, on the authority of Abu Idris, on the authority of Abu Tha'laba al-Khushani, who said: I said: "O Prophet of Allah, we are in the land of a people of the Book; shall we eat from their vessels? We are also in a land of game, where I hunt with my bow and with my dog that is not trained, and with my trained dog; what is permitted for me?" He said: "As for what you mention of the vessels of the People of the Book: if you find others, do not eat in them; and if you do not find others, then wash them and eat in them. What you hunt with your bow and mention the name of Allah over, eat. What you hunt with your trained dog and mention the name of Allah over, eat. What you hunt with your dog that is not trained, but you reach its ritual slaughter, eat." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Dhaba'ih wa al-Sayd, chapter on hunting with a bow: 9/604-605; chapter on what has come concerning hunting: 9/612; chapter on the vessels of the Magians: 9/622; and by Muslim in al-Sayd wa al-Dhaba'ih, chapter on hunting with trained dogs, no. (1930): 3/1532. And by the author in Sharh al-Sunna: 11/199.]]

**Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And mention the name of Allah over it, and fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning﴾.** In it is an explanation that mentioning the name of Allah the Mighty and Majestic over the slaughtered animal is a condition at the time of slaughter, and over game at the time of sending forth the hunting beast or the arrow.

We were informed by Abu al-Hasan 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Dawudi: Abu al-Hasan 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Ulwiyya al-Jawhari informed us, saying: Abu al-'Abbas Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Athram al-Muqri narrated to us in Basra: 'Umar ibn Shayba narrated to us: Ibn Abi 'Adiyy informed us, on the authority of Sa'id, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sacrificed two white horned rams. He slaughtered them with his own hand, and he said the name of Allah and said 'Allahu Akbar'." He said: "I saw him placing his foot on their sides, slaughtering them with his hand, and saying: 'In the name of Allah, and Allah is greatest.'" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Adahi, chapter on one who slaughters with his own hand: 10/18, and in other places. And by Muslim in al-Adahi, chapter on the recommendation of sacrifice, no. (1966): 3/1556-1557; and by the author in Sharh al-Sunna: 4/334.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 5, verse 5:

His words, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿Today the good things have been made lawful for you﴾, meaning: the slaughtered animals over which the name of Allah, mighty and majestic is He, has been mentioned. ﴿And the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you﴾, meaning: the slaughtered animals of the Jews and the Christians, and of whoever entered their religion from among the other nations before the sending of the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), are lawful for you. As for whoever entered their religion after the sending of Muhammad (ﷺ), his slaughtered animal is not lawful. And if a Jew or a Christian slaughters upon the name of other than Allah, such as the Christian who slaughters in the name of the Messiah, they differ concerning it. ʿUmar [in the version "B": Ibn ʿUmar] said: it is not lawful, and this is the view of Rabiʿah. But most of the scholars (ahl al-ʿilm) went to the view that it is lawful, and this is the view of al-Shaʿbi, ʿAta', al-Zuhri and Makhul. Al-Shaʿbi and Makhul were asked about the Christian who slaughters in the name of the Messiah, and they both said: it is lawful, for Allah, exalted is He, has made their slaughtered animals lawful, and He knows what they say. Al-Hasan said: if a Jew or a Christian slaughters and mentions the name of other than Allah while you are listening, do not eat it; but if he is out of your sight, eat, for Allah has made it lawful for you.

His words, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿And your food is lawful for them﴾. If it is said: how was the lawfulness of our food prescribed for them when they are disbelievers and not people of the law? Al-Zajjaj said: its meaning is that it is lawful for you to feed them, so the address of lawfulness is to the Muslims. It was also said: because He mentioned after it the ruling on women, and did not mention the lawfulness of Muslim women for them, it is as if He said: it is lawful for you to feed them, and it is forbidden for you to marry them.

His words, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿And the chaste women from among the believers, and the chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you﴾. This refers back to the first and is separate from His words: "And your food is lawful for them".

They differed concerning the meaning of "al-muhsanat" (the chaste women). Most of the scholars went to the view that what is meant by them is the free women, and they permitted marriage to every free woman, whether believing or from the People of the Book, unchaste or chaste; this is the view of Mujahid. These said: it is not permissible for a Muslim to marry a slave woman from the People of the Book, based on the words of Allah, exalted is He: "of what your right hands possess from your believing young women" (Surat al-Nisa', 25), which permitted marrying a slave woman on condition that she be a believer. Most of them permitted marrying a slave woman from the People of the Book who is at war, while Ibn ʿAbbas said: it is not permitted. He recited "Fight those who do not believe in Allah" up to His words "until they give the jizya with willing submission and they are humbled" (al-Tawbah, 29). So whoever gives the jizya, his women are lawful for us, and whoever does not give it, his women are not lawful for us.

Another group went to the view that what is meant by "al-muhsanat" in the verse is the chaste women of both groups, whether free or slaves, and they permitted marrying a slave woman from the People of the Book, and they forbade the unchaste women among the believers and the People of the Book. This is the view of al-Hasan. Al-Shaʿbi said: the chastity of a Christian woman is that she abstains from fornication and performs ghusl from sexual impurity.

﴿When you have given them their wages﴾, meaning their dowries, ﴿being chaste, not committing illicit intercourse openly﴾, meaning not openly committing fornication, ﴿nor taking secret lovers﴾, meaning those who commit fornication in secret. Al-Zajjaj said: Allah forbade intercourse in the manner of illicit unions and in the manner of taking a lover, and He made it lawful in the manner of chastity, which is marriage.

﴿And whoever disbelieves in the faith, his deed has become void, and he is in the Hereafter among the losers﴾. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: He says: the Muslims' chastity of them is not what takes them out of disbelief, nor does it avail them anything; and it is general for people: "And whoever disbelieves in the faith, his deed has become void, and he is in the Hereafter among the losers."

Ibn ʿAbbas and Mujahid said regarding the meaning of His words, exalted is He: ﴿whoever disbelieves in the faith﴾, meaning: in Allah, in whom belief is obligatory.

Al-Kalbi said: "by the faith" means: by the word of monotheism, which is the testimony that there is no god but Allah.

Muqatil said: "by what was revealed to Muhammad (ﷺ)", which is the Qur'an. It was also said: "whoever disbelieves in the faith" means: he who makes lawful what is forbidden and forbids what is lawful, his deed has become void, and he is in the Hereafter among the losers. Ibn ʿAbbas said: he lost the reward.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 5, verse 6 (part 1 of 2):

His, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: ﴿O you who have believed, when you rise to prayer﴾, meaning: when you intend to rise to prayer, like His, the Exalted, saying: ﴿So when you recite the Qur'an, seek refuge in Allah﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 98), meaning: when you intend to recite.

The apparent meaning of the verse requires wudu' (ablution) each time one intends to rise to prayer. But we were informed, through the explanation of the Sunnah and the practice of the Prophet (ﷺ), that the intended meaning of the verse is: "When you rise to prayer" while you are not in a state of purity. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Allah does not accept the prayer of any one of you when he has broken wind until he performs wudu'." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Wudu', chapter "The prayer is not accepted without purity," 1/234, and in al-Hiyal, chapter on prayer, 12/329; and Muslim in Taharah, chapter on the obligation of purity for prayer, no. (225), 1/204, with the wording "The prayer of one of you is not accepted when he has broken wind..."; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah, 1/328.]]

The Prophet (ﷺ) combined four prayers on the day of the Trench with a single wudu'. Abu al-Qasim Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Hanifi informed us: Abu al-Harith Tahir ibn Muhammad al-Tahiri informed us: Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Halim informed us: Abu al-Muwajjih Muhammad ibn Amr ibn al-Muwajjih informed us: Abdan informed us: Sufyan informed us, from Alqamah ibn Martad, from Sulayman ibn Buraydah, from his father, that the Prophet (ﷺ) prayed the prayers on the day of the Conquest of Makkah with a single wudu', and wiped over his khuffs (leather socks). [[Narrated by Muslim in Taharah, chapter on the permissibility of performing all prayers with one wudu', no. (277); and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah, 1/448.]]

Zayd ibn Aslam said: The meaning of the verse is "when you rise to prayer from sleep."

Some scholars said: It is a command in the manner of recommendation (nadb), recommending that one who rises to prayer renew his purity for it even if he is already in a state of purity. Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, related that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever performs wudu' while in a state of purity, Allah records for him ten good deeds." [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in Taharah, chapter on a man renewing wudu' without having broken it, 1/46; and al-Tirmidhi in Taharah, chapter on what has been related about wudu' for every prayer, 1/192, and he said: "...its isnad is weak." It was also narrated by Ibn Majah in Taharah, chapter on wudu' upon wudu', no. (512), 1/171. In al-Zawa'id it is said: the hadith revolves around Abd al-Rahman ibn Ziyad al-Ifriqi, who is weak, and despite his weakness he was a mudallis (one who conceals defects in his narration). The author also declared it weak in Sharh al-Sunnah, 1/449.]]

It is related from Abdullah ibn Handhalah ibn Amir that "the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded wudu' for every prayer, whether one was in a state of purity or not. When that became difficult for him, he commanded the use of the siwak (tooth-stick) for every prayer." [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in Taharah, chapter on the siwak, 1/40; al-Mundhiri said: its isnad contains Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar, and the imams differed regarding the use of his narrations as proof. Also narrated by al-Darimi in Wudu', 1/168, and Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad, 5/225.]]

Some scholars said: This is a notification from Allah, glorified and exalted is He, to His Messenger (ﷺ) that he had no obligation of wudu' except when he rose to prayer, and not for other actions. So He permitted him to do, after a breach of wudu', whatever other actions he wished, apart from prayer. Abu al-Qasim al-Hanifi informed us: Abu al-Harith al-Tahiri informed us: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Halim informed us: Abu al-Muwajjih informed us: Sadaqah informed us: Ibn Uyaynah informed us, from Amr ibn Dinar, who heard Sa'id ibn al-Huwayrith, who heard Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, say: "We were with the Prophet (ﷺ) when he returned from the toilet (al-ghait). Food was brought to him, and it was said to him: 'Will you not perform wudu'?' He said: 'Why? Am I going to pray so that I perform wudu'?'" [[Narrated by Muslim in Hayd, chapter on the permissibility of a person in a state of minor impurity eating food, no. (374), 1/283; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah, 2/40.]]

His, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: ﴿then wash your faces﴾. The limit of the face is from the hairline to the end of the chin in length, and what lies between the two ears in width. All of it must be washed in wudu'. It is also obligatory to make the water reach what lies beneath the two eyebrows, the eyelashes, the moustache, the sideburns (al-'idhar), or the goatee (al-'anfaqah), even if it is thick. As for the cheek hair and the beard: if it is thick such that the skin beneath it cannot be seen, it is not obligatory to wash its underside in wudu', but it is obligatory to wash its outer surface.

Is it obligatory to let water flow over the outer surface of the beard that hangs down beyond the chin? On this there are two opinions:

The first: It is not obligatory. This is the view of Abu Hanifa, because hair that hangs beyond the limit of the head does not take the ruling of the head regarding the permissibility of wiping over it; likewise, hair that hangs beyond the limit of the face does not take the ruling of the face regarding the obligation of washing it.

The second opinion: It is obligatory to let water flow over its outer surface, because Allah, the Exalted, commanded the washing of the face, and the face is that part with which one faces (al-muwajahah) others. In the language it is said: "The face of so-and-so has grown" (baqala wajhu fulan) and "his face has come out" (kharaja wajhuhu) when his beard has grown.

His, the Exalted, saying: ﴿and your hands up to the elbows﴾. Meaning: "along with the elbows," like His saying: ﴿and do not consume their wealth along with your wealth﴾ (Surah al-Nisa', 2), meaning: along with your wealth; and His saying: ﴿Who are my helpers in (the cause of) Allah?﴾ (Surah Al 'Imran, 52, and Surah al-Saff, 14), meaning: for Allah.

Most scholars hold that it is obligatory to wash both elbows, and for the feet it is obligatory to wash both ankles (al-ka'bayn). Al-Sha'bi and Muhammad ibn Jarir said: it is not obligatory to wash the elbows and ankles when washing the hands and feet, because the particle "ila" (up to) indicates the limit and the boundary, so what follows it does not enter into what is bounded.

We say: This is not a limit, but it carries the meaning of "ma'a" (along with), as we have mentioned. It has also been said: When something is limited up to its own kind, the limit enters into it; but when it is limited up to something other than its kind, the limit does not enter. Like His saying: ﴿Then complete the fast until the night﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 187): the night does not enter into it, because it is not of the same kind as the day.

His, the Exalted, saying: ﴿and wipe your heads﴾. The scholars differed regarding the amount of wiping of the head that is obligatory. Malik said: it is obligatory to wipe the whole head, just as it is obligatory to wipe the whole face in tayammum (dry ablution). Abu Hanifa said: it is obligatory to wipe a quarter of the head. According to al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him: it is obligatory to wipe the amount to which the term "wiping" (mash) applies.

Those who permitted wiping only part of the head argued with what was informed to us by Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib: Abd al-Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal informed us: Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm informed us: al-Rabi' informed us: al-Shafi'i informed us: Yahya ibn Hassan informed us, from Hammad ibn Zayd and Ibn Ulayyah, from Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani, from Ibn Sirin, from Amr ibn Wahb al-Thaqafi, from al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah, that "the Prophet (ﷺ) performed wudu' and wiped his forelock (nasiyah) and over his turban and his two khuffs." [[Narrated by Muslim in Taharah, chapter on wiping the forelock and the turban, no. (275), 1/231; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah, 1/451.]] Some scholars permitted wiping over the turban on the basis of this hadith, and this was the view of al-Awza'i, Ahmad and Ishaq.

Most scholars did not permit wiping over the turban as a substitute for wiping the head. They said: In the hadith of al-Mughirah, the obligation of wiping was dropped by wiping the forelock, and in it is evidence that wiping the whole head is not obligatory.

His, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: ﴿and your feet up to the ankles﴾. Nafi', Ibn Amir, al-Kisa'i, Ya'qub and Hafs read "wa-arjulakum" with a fatha on the lam (naṣb), and the others read "wa-arjulikum" with a kasra (khafd). Whoever read "wa-arjulakum" with the fatha, it is coordinated (ma'tuf) on His saying: "wash your faces and your hands," meaning: and wash your feet. Whoever read with the kasra, a few scholars held that one wipes over the two feet. It is related from Ibn Abbas that he said: "Wudu' is two washings and two wipings." This is also related from Ikrimah and Qatadah. Al-Sha'bi said: Jibril descended with wiping, and said: "Do you not see that the one performing tayammum wipes what is washing and cancels what is wiping?"

Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari said: The one performing wudu' may choose between wiping over the khuffs and washing the two feet.

The majority of scholars, from among the Companions, the Successors and others, held that washing the two feet is obligatory, and they said: the kasra on the lam in "al-arjul" is due to the proximity of the wording (mujawarat al-lafz), not due to agreement in the ruling, as He, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿the punishment of a painful day﴾, where "painful" (alim) is an attribute of "punishment," but it took the case-ending (i'rab) of "day" because of proximity. And as they say: "A ruined lizard burrow (juhr dabb kharib)," where "ruined" (kharib) is an attribute of "burrow," but it took the case-ending of "lizard" (dabb) because of proximity.

The evidence for the obligation of washing the two feet is what was informed to us by Abu Sa'id Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Abbas al-Humaydi, the preacher (al-Khatib): Abu Abdullah al-Hafiz informed us: Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Ya'qub informed us: Yahya ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya informed us: al-Hajabi and Musaddad said: Abu Awanah informed us, from Abu Bishr, from Yusuf ibn Mahak, from Abdullah ibn Amr who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) lagged behind us on a journey we were making. He caught up with us when the prayer of 'Asr had become pressing for us, and we were performing wudu', and we began wiping over our feet. He called out to us in his loudest voice: 'Woe to the heels from the Fire!'" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-'Ilm, chapter on one who repeats a hadith three times so that it is understood from him, 1/189; and Muslim in Taharah, chapter on the obligation of washing the two feet completely, no. (241/214); and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah, 1/428.]]

Abdul-Wahid al-Mulayhi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Abdan informed us: Abdullah informed us: Ma'mar informed us: al-Zuhri informed me, from Ata' ibn Yazid, from Humran, the freedman of Uthman, who said: "I saw Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, perform wudu'. He poured water over his hands three times, then rinsed his mouth, sniffed water into his nose and blew it out. Then he washed his face three times, then washed his right hand up to the elbow three times, then washed his left hand up to the elbow three times, then wiped his head, then washed his right foot three times, then the left three times. Then he said: 'I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) perform wudu' similar to this wudu' of mine, then he said: Whoever performs wudu' like this wudu' of mine, then prays two rak'ahs without speaking to himself during them, Allah will forgive him his previous sins.'" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Wudu', chapter on performing wudu' three times, 1/259; and in al-Sawm, chapter on the siwak with fresh and dry wood, 4/158; and Muslim in Taharah, chapter on the manner and completeness of wudu', no. (226), 1/205.]]

Some scholars said: By His saying "﴿and your feet﴾" He meant wiping over the khuffs, as it is related that "the Prophet (ﷺ), when he bowed, placed his hands on his knees." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Adhan, chapter on the sunnah of sitting in the tashahhud, 2/305; see also Muslim in Masajid, chapter on the recommendation of placing the hands on the knees in bowing and the abrogation of application (tatbiq), nos. (534-535), 1/379-380.]] The intended meaning is not that there was no barrier between them. It is said: "So-and-so kissed the ruler's head and hand," even though the turban is on his head and his hand is in his sleeve.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 5, verse 6 (part 2 of 2):**

Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi informed us that Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us that Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us that Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us that Abu Nu'aym informed us that Zakariyya reported from Amir, from Urwah ibn al-Mughirah, from his father, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "I was with the Prophet (ﷺ) one night on a journey, and he said, 'Do you have water with you?' I said, 'Yes.' So he dismounted from his mount and walked until he disappeared from me in the darkness of the night. Then he came back, and I poured water on him from the waterskin, and he washed his face and his hands, and he was wearing a woollen cloak. He could not get his forearms out of it until he brought them out from beneath the cloak, and he washed his forearms. Then he wiped his head. Then I bent down to take off his leather socks, and he said, 'Leave them, for I put them on in a state of purity.' So he wiped over them." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Libas, chapter on wearing a woollen cloak in battle: 10/268-269; and by Muslim in Taharah, chapter on wiping over the leather socks, no. (274): 1/230. The author also narrates it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/455.]]

The words of the Exalted: ﴿to the ankles﴾. The ankles (al-Ka'bayn) are the two protruding bones on either side of the feet, and they are the joint where the shin meets the foot. Therefore it is obligatory to wash them along with the feet, as we mentioned concerning the elbows.

The obligatory acts (fara'id) of wudu' are: washing the three body parts as Allah the Exalted mentioned, and wiping the head. The scholars differed concerning the obligation of intention (niyyah). Most of them held that it is obligatory, because wudu' requires intention like all other acts of worship. Some held that it is not obligatory; this is the view of al-Thawri and the people of opinion (ashab al-ra'y).

They also differed concerning the obligation of sequence (tartib), which is that one washes the limbs in succession (al-wala'), as Allah the Blessed and Exalted mentioned. A group held that it is obligatory; this is the view of Malik, al-Shafi'i, Ahmad and Ishaq, may Allah have mercy on them. This is also related from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.

Al-Shafi'i argued with the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 158). The Prophet (ﷺ) began with al-Safa and said, "We begin with what Allah began with." [[Narrated by Muslim in Hajj, chapter on the Hajj of the Prophet (ﷺ), no. (1218): 2/886-888. It is a portion of the long hadith of Jabir on the description of the Prophet's Hajj, with the wording "I begin with what Allah began with..." The author also narrates it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 7/136.]] Likewise here, Allah the Exalted began by mentioning the washing of the face, so it is obligatory for us to begin in action with what Allah the Exalted began with in mention.

A group held that sequence is a sunnah (prophetic practice), and they said: the conjunctions (waw) mentioned in the verse indicate togetherness, not sequence, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, the charities are only for the poor and the needy﴾ (Surah al-Tawbah, 60), and so on. They agreed that observing sequence is not obligatory in distributing charity to its eight categories of recipients. As for those who make sequence obligatory, they answered that it is not reported from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he observed sequence among the categories of recipients, whereas in wudu' it is not reported that he performed it except in sequence as Allah mentioned, and the clarification of the Book is taken from the Sunnah, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿O you who have believed, bow and prostrate﴾ (Surah al-Hajj, 77), where He mentioned bowing before prostration. It is not reported from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he did it except in that order, so observing sequence in it is obligatory; similarly, sequence here.

The words of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And if you are in a state of janabah, then purify yourselves﴾, i.e., perform ghusl (full bath). Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us that Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us that Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us that Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Hisham ibn Urwah, from his father, from Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that "when the Prophet (ﷺ) performed ghusl from janabah, he would begin by washing his hands, then perform wudu' as he does for prayer, then he would put his fingers in the water and run them through the roots of his hair, then he would pour water over his head three times with his hands, then he would let the water flow over his whole skin." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Ghusl, chapter on wudu' before ghusl: 1/360; and by Muslim in Hayd, chapter on the manner of ghusl from janabah, no. (316): 1/253-254. The author also narrates it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 2/10.]]

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And if you are ill, or on a journey, or one of you comes from the place of relieving oneself, or you have touched women, and you find no water, then take clean earth (sa'id) and wipe your faces and your hands with it.﴾ In it is evidence that wiping the face and the two hands with the sa'id, which is dust, is obligatory. ﴿Allah does not intend to place upon you﴾ by what He has enjoined upon you of wudu', ghusl and tayammum, ﴿any hardship﴾, meaning narrowness, ﴿but He intends to purify you﴾ from minor and major impurities and sins, ﴿and to complete His favor upon you that you may be grateful.﴾ Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: The completion of the favor is the expiation of sins through wudu', as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿That Allah may forgive you what preceded of your sin and what follows﴾ (Surah al-Fath, 2), so He made the completion of His favor the forgiveness of his sins.

Abu al-Hasan Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Kisa'i informed us that Abd al-Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal informed us that Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm informed us that al-Rabi' informed us that al-Shafi'i informed us that Sufyan informed us, from Hisham ibn Urwah, from his father, from Humran: that Uthman performed wudu' at al-Maqa'id three times three times, then he said, "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say, 'Whoever performs wudu' like this wudu' of mine, his sins will come out from his face, his hands and his feet.'" [[Narrated in this wording by al-Shafi'i in al-Musnad: 1/31 (Tartib al-Musnad). Al-Bukhari narrates in Wudu', chapter on performing wudu' three times three times: 1/259, with the wording "Whoever performs wudu' like this wudu' of mine, then prays two rak'ahs without speaking to himself in them, will be forgiven what preceded of his sin." Muslim narrates in Taharah, chapter on the sins coming out with the water of wudu', no. (245): 1/216, with the wording: "Whoever performs wudu' and does it well, his sins will come out of his body until they come out from under his nails." The author also narrates it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/324.]].

Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us that Zahir ibn Ahmad, Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us that Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Hisham ibn Urwah, from his father, from Humran, the freedman of Uthman: that Uthman ibn Affan, may Allah be pleased with him, sat on the maqa'id one day, and the muezzin came to him and informed him of the time of the Asr prayer. He asked for water and performed wudu'. Then he said, "By Allah, I will narrate to you a hadith which, were it not for a verse in the Book of Allah, I would not have narrated to you. I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'No Muslim [man] [[Not found in "B".]] performs wudu' and does it well, then prays the prayer, except that he is forgiven what is between it and the next prayer until he prays it.'" Malik said: "I think he meant this verse: ﴿And establish prayer for My remembrance﴾." [[Narrated by Malik in al-Muwatta', Kitab al-Taharah, chapter on comprehensive wudu': 1/30-31.]] Ibn Shihab narrated it, and Urwah said the verse is: ﴿Indeed, those who conceal what We have sent down of clear proofs﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 159). [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Wudu', chapter on performing wudu' three times three times: 1/206; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/325.]]

Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi informed us that Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us that Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us that Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us that Yahya ibn Bukayr informed us that al-Layth informed us, from Khalid, from Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal, from Nu'aym al-Mujammar, who said: "I ascended the roof of the mosque with Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, and he performed wudu'. He said: 'I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "On the Day of Resurrection, my ummah will be called with bright faces and white limbs from the traces of wudu'. So whoever among you can prolong his brightness, let him do so."'" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Wudu', chapter on the virtue of wudu' and the bright faces and white limbs from the traces of wudu': 1/235; and by Muslim in Taharah, chapter on the recommendation of prolonging the brightness and whiteness in wudu', no. (246): 1/216; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/425.]]

The Almighty's saying: ﴿Remember the favour of God upon you﴾, meaning all the favours; ﴿and His covenant with which He bound you﴾, meaning His pledge which He made with you, O believers, ﴿when you said, "We hear and we obey."﴾ This was when they pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to hear and obey, in what they liked and what they disliked. This is the view of most of the exegetes (mufassirun). Mujahid and Muqatil said: it means the covenant that was taken from them when He brought them forth from the loins of Adam (peace be upon him). ﴿And fear God. Indeed, God is Knowing of what is in the breasts﴾, meaning of what is in the hearts, of good and evil.

The Almighty's saying: ﴿O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm for God, witnesses in justice﴾, that is: be those who stand firmly with justice [qawwalin] [In "b": (qa'ilin)] with truthfulness. He commanded them to be just and truthful in their actions and their words. ﴿And do not let the hatred of a people prevent you from being just﴾, meaning do not let it compel you, ﴿hatred of a people﴾, meaning the enmity of a people, ﴿prevent you from being just﴾, that is: from abandoning justice toward them because of their enmity. Then He said: ﴿Be just; that is nearer to righteousness﴾, meaning in regard to your allies and your enemies, ﴿that is nearer to righteousness﴾, meaning nearer to piety. ﴿And fear God. Indeed, God is Acquainted with what you do.﴾

The Almighty's saying: ﴿God has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds that for them is forgiveness and a great reward.﴾ This is in the accusative position (nasb), because the verb of promising governs the forgiveness; its nominative form (raf') is possible on the basis of an implied construction, meaning: "He said to them, forgiveness and a great reward."

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 5, verses 10–11:**

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿O you who believe, remember the favour of Allah upon you﴾, by warding off [harm] from you, ﴿when a people resolved to stretch out their hands against you﴾ with killing.

Qatadah said: This verse was revealed while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in Batn Nakhl. The Banu Tha'labah and the Banu Muharib intended to ambush him and his Companions while they were occupied with the prayer. Allah, blessed and exalted is He, informed His Prophet of this, and Allah revealed the prayer of fear (salat al-khawf).[[Narrated by al-Tabari from Qatadah: 6/146 (Halabi edition). al-Suyuti also attributed it to Abd ibn Humayd. See al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/38.]]

Al-Hasan said: The Prophet ﷺ was besieging Ghatafan at Nakhl. A man from the polytheists said: "Shall I kill Muhammad for you?" They said: "How would you kill him?" He said: "I will ambush him." They said: "We wish you would do that." So he came to the Prophet ﷺ while the Prophet ﷺ was wearing his sword. The man said: "O Muhammad, show me your sword." So he gave it to him. The man began to brandish the sword, looking once at the sword and once at the Prophet ﷺ, and said: "O Muhammad, who will protect you from me?" He said: "Allah." The Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ threatened him, so he sheathed the sword and departed. Then Allah, exalted is He, revealed this verse.[[See: al-Tabari: 6/146; Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi, pp. 223–224; Sirah of Ibn Hisham: 3/205–206; al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/36.]]

Mujahid, Ikrimah, al-Kalbi, and Ibn Yasar, on the authority of his men, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent al-Mundhir ibn Amr al-Sa'idi, who was one of the nuqaba' (chieftains) on the night of al-Aqabah, with thirty riders from the Muhajirun and the Ansar to the Banu Amir ibn Sa'sa'ah. They set out and met Amir ibn al-Tufayl at Bi'r Ma'unah, which was one of the watering places of the Banu Amir, and they fought. Al-Mundhir ibn Amr and his Companions were killed, except for three men who had gone in search of a lost animal of theirs. One of them was Amr ibn Umayyah al-Damri. They were alarmed only by birds circling in the sky, from whose beaks clots of blood were falling. One of the three said: "Our companions have been killed." Then he turned and ran until he met a man, and they exchanged two blows. When the blow reached him, he lifted his head toward the sky, opened his eyes, and said: "Allahu Akbar! Paradise and the Lord of the worlds!" His two companions returned and met two men from the Banu Sulaym, between whom and the Prophet ﷺ and their people there was a truce. They claimed to be from the Banu Amir, and they killed the two men. Their people came to the Prophet ﷺ seeking blood money. He went out, accompanied by Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali, Talhah, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, may Allah be pleased with them all, until they came to Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf and the Banu al-Nadir, seeking their help regarding the blood money for the two men. They had made a pact with the Prophet ﷺ to refrain from fighting and to assist him in paying blood money. They said: "Yes, O Abu al-Qasim, it is time for you to come to us and ask us for something. Sit down until we feed you and give you what you asked." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions sat down. Some of them withdrew from the others and said: "You will never find Muhammad closer to you than he is now. Who will climb onto this house and drop a stone on him, so that he will relieve us of him?" Umar ibn Jahhash said: "I will." He came to a large millstone to drop it on him, but Allah, exalted is He, held back his hand.
