**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 5, verses 10–11:**

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿O you who believe, remember the favour of Allah upon you﴾, by warding off [harm] from you, ﴿when a people resolved to stretch out their hands against you﴾ with killing.

Qatadah said: This verse was revealed while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in Batn Nakhl. The Banu Tha'labah and the Banu Muharib intended to ambush him and his Companions while they were occupied with the prayer. Allah, blessed and exalted is He, informed His Prophet of this, and Allah revealed the prayer of fear (salat al-khawf).[[Narrated by al-Tabari from Qatadah: 6/146 (Halabi edition). al-Suyuti also attributed it to Abd ibn Humayd. See al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/38.]]

Al-Hasan said: The Prophet ﷺ was besieging Ghatafan at Nakhl. A man from the polytheists said: "Shall I kill Muhammad for you?" They said: "How would you kill him?" He said: "I will ambush him." They said: "We wish you would do that." So he came to the Prophet ﷺ while the Prophet ﷺ was wearing his sword. The man said: "O Muhammad, show me your sword." So he gave it to him. The man began to brandish the sword, looking once at the sword and once at the Prophet ﷺ, and said: "O Muhammad, who will protect you from me?" He said: "Allah." The Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ threatened him, so he sheathed the sword and departed. Then Allah, exalted is He, revealed this verse.[[See: al-Tabari: 6/146; Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi, pp. 223–224; Sirah of Ibn Hisham: 3/205–206; al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/36.]]

Mujahid, Ikrimah, al-Kalbi, and Ibn Yasar, on the authority of his men, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent al-Mundhir ibn Amr al-Sa'idi, who was one of the nuqaba' (chieftains) on the night of al-Aqabah, with thirty riders from the Muhajirun and the Ansar to the Banu Amir ibn Sa'sa'ah. They set out and met Amir ibn al-Tufayl at Bi'r Ma'unah, which was one of the watering places of the Banu Amir, and they fought. Al-Mundhir ibn Amr and his Companions were killed, except for three men who had gone in search of a lost animal of theirs. One of them was Amr ibn Umayyah al-Damri. They were alarmed only by birds circling in the sky, from whose beaks clots of blood were falling. One of the three said: "Our companions have been killed." Then he turned and ran until he met a man, and they exchanged two blows. When the blow reached him, he lifted his head toward the sky, opened his eyes, and said: "Allahu Akbar! Paradise and the Lord of the worlds!" His two companions returned and met two men from the Banu Sulaym, between whom and the Prophet ﷺ and their people there was a truce. They claimed to be from the Banu Amir, and they killed the two men. Their people came to the Prophet ﷺ seeking blood money. He went out, accompanied by Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali, Talhah, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, may Allah be pleased with them all, until they came to Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf and the Banu al-Nadir, seeking their help regarding the blood money for the two men. They had made a pact with the Prophet ﷺ to refrain from fighting and to assist him in paying blood money. They said: "Yes, O Abu al-Qasim, it is time for you to come to us and ask us for something. Sit down until we feed you and give you what you asked." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions sat down. Some of them withdrew from the others and said: "You will never find Muhammad closer to you than he is now. Who will climb onto this house and drop a stone on him, so that he will relieve us of him?" Umar ibn Jahhash said: "I will." He came to a large millstone to drop it on him, but Allah, exalted is He, held back his hand. Jibril came and informed him, so the Prophet ﷺ rose and returned to Madinah. Then he summoned Ali and said: "Do not leave your place. If any of my Companions comes out to you and asks you about me, say: 'He has gone toward Madinah.'" Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, did so until they came to him, and then they followed him. Then Allah, exalted is He, revealed this verse and said: ﴿So He withheld their hands from you, and fear Allah; and upon Allah let the believers rely.﴾[[See: Tafsir al-Tabari: 6/145 (Halabi edition); Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi, pp. 224–225; al-Durr al-Manthur of al-Suyuti: 3/37–38; Sirah of Ibn Hisham: 2/563.]]

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 5, verse 12:**

His saying, may He be Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And Allah had certainly taken the covenant of the Children of Israel, and We raised among them twelve leaders﴾. The reason for this is that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, had promised Moses, peace be upon him, that He would make him and his people inherit the Holy Land, which is al-Sham (Greater Syria). The Canaanites, who were tyrants, lived there. When the Children of Israel had settled in Egypt, Allah the Exalted commanded them to march to Ariha (Jericho) in the land of al-Sham, which is the Holy Land. It had a thousand villages, and in each village a thousand orchards. He said: "O Moses, I have written it for you as a dwelling and a lasting abode. Go forth to it and fight those of the enemy who are in it, for I will give you victory over them. And take from your people twelve leaders, one leader from each tribe, who will stand as surety over his people for their fulfilment of what they have been commanded." So Moses chose the leaders. Moses set out with the Children of Israel until they drew near to Ariha, and he sent these leaders to spy out the news for him and to learn its condition.

A man of the tyrants met them, called Uj ibn Unuq. His height was three thousand, three hundred and thirty-three cubits and a third of a cubit. He would take hold of the clouds and drink from them, and he would reach for a fish from the bottom of the sea and roast it by the sun's heat, lifting it up to the sun and then eating it. It is related that the water rose over everything on the earth except the mountains, and it did not reach beyond the knees of Uj. He lived three thousand years until Allah destroyed him at the hands of Moses, peace be upon him. That came about because he came and tore out [and uprooted] [[In "A": (wa-qawwara).]] a rock from the mountain, the size of Moses' army, which was a farsakh by a farsakh (a parasang by a parasang). He carried it to drop it upon them. Then Allah sent the hoopoe, which hollowed out the rock with its beak, so it fell onto his neck and felled him. Moses, peace be upon him, came while he was prostrate and killed him. His mother [Unuq] [[Addition from "B".]] was one of the daughters of Adam, and her seat was [a jarib] [[Addition from "B":]] of land. When Uj met the leaders, he had a bundle of firewood on his head. He took the twelve, put them in his waistband, and set off with them to his wife. He said: "Look at these people who claim they want to fight us." He threw them down before her and said: "Shall I not crush them under my foot?" His wife said: "No, rather release them until they inform their people of what they have seen." So he did that. [[The story of Uj ibn Unuq: al-Imam al-Tabari in his tafsir (6/174–175, Halabi edition), al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (3/48–49), and other exegetes. It is among the Israelite narrations and fables that enemies of Islam slipped in and promoted. Al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, transmitted it from al-Tabari and said: "There is doubt about this chain." Then he quoted the narration of Ibn Abi Hatim and said: "This is something one is ashamed to mention. Moreover, it contradicts what is established in the two Sahihs, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Allah created Adam and his height was sixty cubits. Then creation continued to diminish until now.' They also mention that this man was a disbeliever, that he was born of fornication, that he refused to board Noah's ark, and that the flood did not reach his knees. This is a lie and a fabrication. Allah the Exalted mentioned that Noah prayed against the disbelievers of the earth, saying: 'My Lord, do not leave upon the earth any of the disbelievers as a dweller' (71:26). Allah the Exalted said: 'So We saved him and those with him in the laden ship, then We drowned the rest' (26:119–120). He also said: 'There is no protector today from the command of Allah, except for him on whom He has mercy' (11:43). If the disbelieving son of Noah drowned, how could Uj ibn Unuq remain, while he was a disbeliever and born of fornication? This is not permissible by reason or by the Sharia. Moreover, the existence of a man called Uj ibn Unuq is doubtful, and Allah knows best." Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 2/39, Dar al-Fikr edition, 1400 AH. Ibn al-Qayyim al-Jawziyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, cited this narration as an example of a report for which sound evidence establishes its falsehood. Then he said: "It is no wonder that this liar dared against Allah. The wonder is at those who include this narration in books of knowledge, such as tafsir and others, without clarifying its status. They hold that this man is not one of Noah's offspring, yet Allah the Exalted said: 'And We made his offspring the survivors' (37:77). He thus informed that everyone who remained on the face of the earth was of Noah's offspring. So if this Uj had existed, he would not have survived after Noah... Also, between the heaven and the earth is a distance of five hundred years' journey, and the thickness of the heavens is likewise. If the sun is in the fourth heaven, and between us and it lies this great distance, how could a man of three thousand cubits reach it, so that a fish is roasted in its heat? There is no doubt that this and similar things are the fabrication of the heretics among the People of the Book, who intended to mock and ridicule the messengers and their followers." Naqd al-Manqul aw al-Manar al-Munif by Ibn al-Qayyim, pp. (44–45). See also: Ruh al-Ma'ani by al-Alusi: 6/86–87; al-Fatawa al-Hadithiyyah by Ibn Hajar al-Haytami, p. (188); al-Isra'iliyyat wal-Mawdu'at fi Kutub al-Tafsir by Shaykh Muhammad Abu Shahbah, pp. (259–262); al-Bidayah wal-Nihayah by Ibn Kathir: 1/278.]].

It is also narrated that he put them in his sleeve and brought them to the king, and he threw them down before him. The king said: "Go back and inform them of what you have seen." He would not carry a single bunch of their grapes except that five men were on a pole, and a half of a pomegranate, once its seeds were removed, could hold five men. The leaders returned and began to inquire into their conditions. Some of them said to others: "O people, if you inform the Children of Israel of the news of the people, they will turn back from the Prophet of Allah. But keep it secret, and inform Moses and Aaron, so that they may consider their opinion." Some of them took a covenant from others to this effect. Then they broke the covenant, and each one of them began to forbid his tribe from fighting them and informed them of what he had seen, except for two men. This is the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And Allah had certainly taken the covenant of the Children of Israel, and We raised among them twelve leaders﴾.

﴿And Allah said: "Indeed, I am with you"﴾, meaning, your helper against your enemy. Then He began speech, saying: ﴿"If you establish prayer"﴾, O assembly of the Children of Israel, ﴿"and give zakah and believe in My messengers and support them"﴾, meaning, help them. It was said: and honour and magnify them. ﴿"And lend Allah a goodly loan"﴾. It was said: this is giving zakah, and it was said: it is spending on one's family. ﴿"I will surely remove from you your misdeeds"﴾, meaning, I will surely erase your misdeeds from you. ﴿"And I will surely admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow. But whoever among you disbelieves after that has certainly strayed from the sound way"﴾, that is, he has missed the right course of the path. The path meant is the way of [the truth] [[In "B": (the Garden).]]. And "sawa'" (the middle) of everything is its centre.

﴿So for their breaking of their covenant﴾, meaning: because of their breaking (*naqḍihim*). The word "mā" here is *ṣilah* (a redundant particle that adds no meaning). ﴿We cursed them﴾. Qatadah said: "They broke it in several ways, because they denied the messengers who came after Musa, killed the prophets of Allah, cast away His Book, and neglected its obligations." ʿAṭāʾ [in B: Qatadah] said: "We distanced them from Our mercy." Al-Hasan and Muqatil said: "We punished them by transforming them." ﴿And We made their hearts hard﴾. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read *qasiyyah* with a shaddah on the yā' and without an alif, and both forms are dialectal variants, like *al-dhākiyah* and *al-dhakiyyah*. Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: *qāsiyah* means dry. It was also said: it means thick and unyielding. And it was said that the meaning is: their hearts are not purely devoted to faith; rather, their faith is mixed with disbelief and hypocrisy. From this comes the expression *al-darāhim al-qāsiyah*, meaning debased, adulterated coins.

﴿They distort words from their places﴾. It was said: this refers to their altering the description of the Prophet (ﷺ). It was also said: it refers to their distortion through false interpretation. ﴿And they forgot a portion of what they were reminded of﴾, meaning: they abandoned their share of what they were commanded, namely belief in Muhammad (ﷺ) and clarifying his description. ﴿And you will not cease to discover [O Muhammad] [omitted in B] treachery from them﴾, meaning: a betrayal. The form *khā'inah* is used in the sense of a verbal noun, like *al-kādhibah* and *al-lāghiyah*. It was also said that it is used in the sense of the agent, and the *hā'* is for emphasis, as in *rawiyah*, *nassābah*, *ʿallāmah*, and *ḥassābah*. It was also said: [it means] a treacherous group. Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: "*ʿAlā khā'innah*" means "upon disobedience." Their treachery consisted of breaking the covenant, supporting the polytheists in fighting the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), their plot to kill him and to poison him, and similar betrayals that became evident. ﴿Except a few of them﴾, who did not betray and did not break the covenant; they are those among the People of the Book who embraced Islam. ﴿So pardon them and overlook﴾, meaning: turn away from them and do not confront them. ﴿Indeed, Allah loves the doers of good﴾.

This verse is said to be abrogated by the Verse of the Sword. (This statement is transmitted from Qatadah; see al-Tabari, *Tafsir*, 10/135. He then rejected the claim of abrogation with a valuable discussion, in which he said: "What Qatadah said is not impossible; however, the abrogating ruling that is beyond doubt is that which negates all meanings of its opposite that preceded it. As for what does not negate its entirety, there is no way to know that it abrogates except by a report from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, or from His Messenger (ﷺ). In His saying, 'Fight those who do not believe in Allah or the Last Day, and do not forbid what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, and do not follow the religion of truth from among those given the Scripture, until they give the jizyah willingly while they are humbled' (al-Tawbah), there is no indication of commanding the negation of forgiveness and pardon toward the Jews. Even if that is the case, and it was permissible, while they acknowledge their humiliation and pay the jizyah after fighting, to command pardon for a treachery they intended or a breach they resolved upon, as long as they do not commit hostilities without paying the jizyah and refuse the obligatory rulings upon them, it would not be necessary to judge that His saying, 'Fight those who do not believe in Allah or the Last Day...' (the verse), abrogates His saying, 'So pardon them and overlook; indeed, Allah loves the doers of good.'" Al-Zarkashi, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his book *al-Burhan fi ʿUlum al-Qur'an*: "What many exegetes have insisted upon, that the verses commanding leniency are abrogated by the Verse of the Sword, is a weak view. It belongs to *al-munsaʾ* (with a *ḍammah* on the *mīm*), meaning that every command that is required to be obeyed at a certain time, due to a cause that necessitates that ruling, then shifts with the shifting of that cause to another ruling; this is not abrogation. Abrogation is removal, such that it is never permissible to act upon it again... The ruling of warfare does not abrogate the ruling of peace; rather, each of them must be acted upon at its proper time." See al-Burhan of al-Zarkashi, 2/43–44; *ʿUlum al-Qur'an* by Dr. ʿAdnan Muhammad Zarzur, pp. 210–212.)

The saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And among those who say, "We are Christians," We took their covenant﴾. It was said: He meant by them the Jews and the Christians, and He mentioned only one of them. The sound view is that the verse refers to the Christians specifically, since the Jews have already been mentioned. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 5, verse 15–17:

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿O People of the Book﴾ means: O People of the Two Books (ahl al-kitabayn), ﴿Our Messenger has certainly come to you, making clear to you much of what you used to conceal from the Scripture﴾

That is: from the Torah and the Gospel, such as the description of Muhammad (ﷺ), the verse of stoning (ayat al-rajm), and other things. ﴿And he pardons much﴾ means: he overlooks much of what you have concealed, so he does not confront it and does not hold you accountable for it. ﴿There has certainly come to you from Allah a light﴾ meaning: Muhammad (ﷺ). It was also said: Islam. ﴿And a clear Book﴾ meaning: clear. It was also said: "clear" (mubin) refers to the Qur'an.

﴿By it Allah guides those who follow His pleasure (ridwanahu)﴾ meaning: His approval, ﴿to the paths of peace (subul al-salam)﴾. It was said: al-Salam is Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and His path is His religion which He legislated for His servants and sent His messengers with. It was also said: al-Salam is safety (al-salamah), like al-ladhadh and al-ladhadhah, which have one meaning; and what is meant is the ways of safety. ﴿And He brings them out from darknesses into the light﴾ meaning: from the darknesses of disbelief into the light of faith, ﴿by His permission﴾ by His enabling and His guidance, ﴿and guides them to a straight path﴾ 104 which is Islam.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Certainly, they have disbelieved who say, "Indeed, Allah is the Messiah, the son of Mary."﴾ They are the Ya'qubiyyah among the Christians, who say the Messiah is Allah, exalted is He. ﴿Say, "Then who could prevent Allah at all if He wished to destroy the Messiah, the son of Mary, and his mother and everyone on the earth entirely?"﴾ meaning: who is able to repel any of Allah's decree once He has ordained it? ﴿And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them. He creates what He wills, and Allah is over all things competent.﴾

He creates what He wills, and Allah is over all things competent.﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 5, verse 15–17:

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿O People of the Book﴾ means: O People of the Two Books (ahl al-kitabayn), ﴿Our Messenger has certainly come to you, making clear to you much of what you used to conceal from the Scripture﴾

That is: from the Torah and the Gospel, such as the description of Muhammad (ﷺ), the verse of stoning (ayat al-rajm), and other things. ﴿And he pardons much﴾ means: he overlooks much of what you have concealed, so he does not confront it and does not hold you accountable for it. ﴿There has certainly come to you from Allah a light﴾ meaning: Muhammad (ﷺ). It was also said: Islam. ﴿And a clear Book﴾ meaning: clear. It was also said: "clear" (mubin) refers to the Qur'an.

﴿By it Allah guides those who follow His pleasure (ridwanahu)﴾ meaning: His approval, ﴿to the paths of peace (subul al-salam)﴾. It was said: al-Salam is Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and His path is His religion which He legislated for His servants and sent His messengers with. The Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 5, verse 18:

His statement, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿The Jews and the Christians said: "We are the children of God and His beloved."﴾ It was said: they meant that God, exalted is He, is to us like a father in tenderness and compassion, and we are like children to Him in nearness and station. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: The Jews found in the Torah, "O children of my rabbis (ahbar)," but they altered it to "O children of my firstborn (abkar)," and from this they said, "We are the children of God." It was also said: its meaning is, "We are the children of God's messengers."

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Say: "Why then does He punish you for your sins?"﴾ He means: if the matter is as you claim, that you are His children and His beloved, then a father does not punish his child, and a beloved does not punish his beloved, yet you acknowledge that He punishes you? It was also said: "Why then does He punish you," that is: why did He punish those before you for their sins, transforming them into apes and swine? ﴿Rather, you are human beings among those He has created﴾, like the rest of the children of Adam, recompensed for evil and for good. ﴿He forgives whom He wills﴾ by grace, ﴿and punishes whom He wills﴾ by justice. ﴿To God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, and to Him is the final return.﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (*Ma'alim al-Tanzil*) on surah 5, verses 19–20:

﴿O People of the Scripture, there has certainly come to you Our Messenger﴾ Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿making clear to you﴾ the signs of guidance and the laws of the religion, ﴿after a interval in the messengers﴾, that is, a break in the sending of messengers.

They differed concerning the length of the *fatra* (the interval, a period in which no messenger was sent) between ʿIsa (Jesus, peace be upon him) and Muhammad (ﷺ). Abu ʿUthman al-Nahdi said: six hundred years. Qatadah said: five hundred and sixty years. Maʿmar and al-Kalbi said: five hundred and forty years. [[Al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir, may God have mercy on him, said in his *Tafsir* (2/36), after mentioning something similar to what al-Baghawi said: "...Al-Dahhak said: four hundred and some thirty years. Ibn ʿAsakir mentioned in the biography of ʿIsa, peace be upon him, from al-Shaʿbi, that he said: From the raising of the Messiah to the Hijrah of the Prophet (ﷺ) is nine hundred and thirty-three years. The well-known view is the first opinion, namely that it is six hundred years. Some say six hundred and twenty years. There is no contradiction between them; the first speaker meant six hundred solar years, and the other meant lunar years, and between every hundred solar years and the lunar years there are about three years. For this reason God, exalted is He, said in the story of the People of the Cave: 'And they remained in their cave three hundred years and added nine' — that is, lunar years, to complete the three hundred solar years which were known to the People of the Scripture. The interval between ʿIsa son of Maryam, the last of the prophets of the Children of Israel, and Muhammad, the Seal of the Prophets absolutely, was as established in the Sahih of al-Bukhari." That is, the period of the *fatra*, the time span in which no messenger was sent, is what lies between ʿIsa and the mission of Muhammad (ﷺ).]] It was called a *fatra* because messengers had been coming in succession after Musa (Moses, peace be upon him) without interruption until the time of ʿIsa (peace be upon him), and after ʿIsa (peace be upon him) there was none but our Messenger (ﷺ).

﴿Lest you should say﴾, meaning so that you would not say, ﴿"There came to us no bringer of good news nor warner. But there has come to you a bringer of good news and a warner. And God is over all things competent."﴾

His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿And [mention] when Musa said to his people, "O my people, remember the favor of God upon you when He appointed among you prophets﴾ [that is, from among you prophets] [[Omitted from "B".]] ﴿and made you kings﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: meaning owners of servants and retinues. Qatadah said: they were the first to possess servants, and there were no servants for those before them. It was narrated from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When one of the Children of Israel had a servant, a wife and a mount, he would be recorded as a king." [[Al-Suyuti attributed it to Ibn Abi Hatim from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri (*al-Durr al-Manthur* 3/46), and Al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir mentioned it in the *Tafsir* (2/38) and said: "A strange hadith from this route." In the chain there is Ibn Lahiʿah: truthful, of the seventh tier, who became confused after his books were burned; and Darraj ibn Abi al-Samh: truthful in his narrations from Abu al-Haytham, but weak. (*al-Taqrib*).]]

Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Hubuli said: I heard ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs, and a man asked him, "Are we not among the poor of the emigrants?" ʿAbdullah said to him: "Do you have a wife to whom you retreat?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Do you have a dwelling in which you live?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then you are among the wealthy." He said: "But I have a servant." He said: "Then you are among the kings." [[Narrated by Muslim in *al-Zuhd wa al-Raqa'iq*, no. (2979), 4/2285.]]

Al-Suddi said: and He made you kings, free men who control the affairs of your own selves, after you had been under the hands of the Copts who enslaved you. Al-Dahhak said: their dwellings were spacious, with flowing water in them, so whoever had a spacious dwelling with flowing water in it was a king. ﴿And He gave you what He had not given anyone among the worlds﴾, meaning the worlds of your time. Mujahid said: meaning the manna and the quails, the stone, and the shading of the clouds.

The Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 5, verses 21–22:

Concerning Allah's words: ﴿O my people, enter the Holy Land which Allah has prescribed for you﴾, the scholars differed about the Holy Land (al-Ard al-Muqaddasah). Mujahid said: it is Mount Sinai (al-Tur) and what surrounds it. Al-Dahhak said: it is Iliya and Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem). Ikrimah and al-Suddi said: it is Arihaa (Jericho). Al-Kalbi said: it is Damascus, Palestine, and part of Jordan. Qatadah said: it is all of al-Sham (Greater Syria). Ka'b said: "I found in the Book of Allah that was revealed that al-Sham is the treasure of Allah in His earth, and in it is the most treasured of His servants."

His words, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿which Allah has prescribed for you﴾ mean: He wrote it in the al-Lawh al-Mahfuz (the Preserved Tablet) that it would be your dwelling. Ibn Ishaq said: Allah granted it to you. It was also said: He made it for you. Al-Suddi said: Allah commanded you to enter it. Qatadah said: they were commanded to it just as they were commanded to prayer, meaning it was obligated upon you.

﴿And do not turn back on your heels﴾, meaning, do not retreat, contrary to the command of Allah, ﴿for you would turn about as losers﴾. Al-Kalbi said: Ibrahim, peace be upon him, ascended Mount Lebanon, and it was said to him: "Look. Whatever your sight reaches is sacred, and it is an inheritance for your offspring."

﴿They said: O Musa, indeed in it are a people of great strength (jabbarin)﴾. This is because the chieftains (nuqaba', pl. of naqib) who went out to spy on the news, when they returned to Musa and informed him of what they had witnessed, Musa said to them: "Conceal their situation and do not inform anyone of the army, lest they become weak." Yet each one of them informed his close relative and cousin, except two men who fulfilled what Musa had told them. One of them was Yusha' ibn Nun ibn Afra'im ibn Yusuf, peace be upon them, the servant of Musa. The other was Kalib ibn Yufuna, the brother-in-law of Musa, peace be upon him, through his sister Maryam daughter of Imran, and he was of the tribe of Yahudha. These two were among the chieftains. A group of the Children of Israel learned of this, raised their voices weeping, and said: "Would that we had died in the land of Egypt! Would that we had died in this wilderness! Allah will not bring us into their land, so that our women, our children and our belongings become spoils for them." A man would say to his companion: "Come, let us appoint a leader over ourselves and return to Egypt." This is the meaning of Allah's words, relating about them: ﴿They said: O Musa, indeed in it are a people of great strength, and we will never enter it until they leave it. But if they leave it, then we will indeed enter﴾.

The root of jabbar is the one who magnifies himself and refuses to be subdued. It is said: "a jabbarah palm tree" when it is tall and out of reach of hands. Those people were called jabbarin because of their refusal (to be overcome), by their height and the strength of their bodies. They were of the 'Amaliqah and the remnant of the people of 'Ad. When the Children of Israel said what they said and resolved to turn back to Egypt, Musa and Harun fell down prostrate, and Yusha' and Kalib tore their garments. These are the two whom Allah, Exalted is He, mentioned in His words: ﴿Two men from among those who feared (Allah) said﴾.

These are the two whom Allah, Exalted is He, mentioned in His words: ﴿Two men from among those who feared (Allah) said﴾.

Said two men from among those who feared (God). That is, those who feared God Most High. Sa'id ibn Jubayr read "yukhafun" (with a dammah on the yā'), and said: The two men were among the giants (al-jabbarin), then they embraced Islam and followed Musa. ﴿God had bestowed His favour upon them﴾ with success and protection. They said: ﴿Enter upon them through the gate﴾, meaning: the city of the giants. ﴿When you have entered it, you will surely be victorious﴾, because God Most High fulfils His promise, and although we have seen them, their bodies are huge but their hearts are weak, so do not fear them. ﴿And upon God rely, if you are [truly] believers﴾. But the Children of Israel wanted to stone them with rocks, and they disobeyed them.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 5, verses 24–26:

﴿They said: "O Musa, we will never enter it as long as they are in it. So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we will sit right here."﴾ Abdul-Wahid al-Mulayhi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il (al-Bukhari) informed us: Abu Nu'aym informed us: Isra'il informed us, from Mukhariq, from Tariq ibn Shihab, who said: I heard Ibn Mas'ud say: "I witnessed from al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad a stand that I would rather have been part of than anything else that was weighed against it. He came to the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was supplicating against the polytheists, and he said: 'We will not say what the people of Musa said: "Go, you and your Lord, and fight." Rather, we will fight on your right, on your left, in front of you, and behind you.' I saw the face of the Prophet (ﷺ) brighten, and what he said pleased him." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Maghazi, chapter on the words of Allah, "When you were seeking help from your Lord..." 7/287.]] When the Children of Israel did what they did, by disobeying the command of their Lord and intending to harm Yusha' and Kalib, Musa (peace be upon him) became angry and invoked curses upon them.

﴿He said: "My Lord, I have power over no one except myself and my brother."﴾ [It has been said: its meaning is, "and my brother has power over no one except himself." It has also been said: its meaning is, "none obeys me except myself and my brother."] [[Omitted from manuscript B.]] ﴿So part us﴾: separate us; ﴿from the defiantly disobedient people﴾: the rebellious ones.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, it is forbidden for them﴾. It has been said: the sentence ends here, and its meaning is: that land is forbidden to them forever. He did not intend a prohibition of worship (taʿabbud), but rather a prohibition of barring them (man'). So Allah revealed to Musa: "By Me, you have sworn [[Addition from manuscript B.]]: I will certainly forbid them from entering the holy land, except for My two servants, Yusha' and Kalib. And I will make them wander in this wilderness ﴿for forty years﴾ [[Omitted from manuscript B: they will wander]] — for every day of the days you were detained there, one year — and I will cast their corpses into these deserts. As for their sons, who did not know evil, they will enter it." That is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, it is forbidden for them for forty years﴾. ﴿They will wander﴾: they will be bewildered, ﴿in the land. So do not grieve over the defiantly disobedient people﴾: that is, do not sorrow over such a people. So they remained for forty years in a region of six farsakhs, and they were six hundred thousand fighting men. Every day they would travel onward, but when evening came they would find themselves at the very place they had set out from.

It has been said that Musa and Harun (peace be upon them both) were not among them. The more correct view is that they were among them, but they did not receive the punishment; the punishment was only for those people. Every person who had entered the wandering (al-tih) who was over twenty years of age died in it, except Yusha' and Kalib. None of those who said "We will never enter it" entered Ariha. When they had died and the forty years had ended, and the young ones among their offspring had grown up, they marched to fight the giants (al-jabbarin).

They differed about who led that war and at whose hands the conquest took place. A group said: Musa conquered Ariha, and Yusha' was at its vanguard. Musa (peace be upon him) then went toward them with those among the Children of Israel who remained, and Yusha' entered it and fought the tyrants. Then Musa (peace be upon him) entered it and remained there as long as Allah willed. Then Allah took him to Himself, and no one knows his grave. This is the most sound of the opinions, because the scholars agree that Uj ibn Unuq was killed by Musa (peace be upon him).

Others said: Only Yusha' fought the giants, and he did not march toward them until after the death of Musa (peace be upon him). [They said: Musa] [[Omitted from manuscript B.]] and Harun both died together in the wandering.

The story of the death of Harun

Al-Suddi said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Musa: "I am going to cause Harun to die, so bring him to such-and-such a mountain." Musa and Harun (peace be upon them both) set out toward that mountain, and suddenly they saw a tree the like of which had never been seen, and suddenly there was a built house, in which was a couch with bedding, and in it there was a pleasant fragrance. When Harun saw that, it pleased him, and he said: "O Musa, I would love to sleep on this couch." He said: "Then sleep on it." He said: "I fear that the owner of this house will come and become angry with me." Musa said to him: "Do not be afraid, I will take care of the matter with the owner of this house, so sleep." He said: "O Musa, you sleep with me, for if the owner of the house comes, he will be angry with both of us." When they both slept, death seized Harun. When he felt his death, he said: "O Musa, you have deceived me." When he was taken, the house was lifted, that tree was gone, and the couch was raised with him to the sky. When Musa returned to the Children of Israel without Harun, they said: "Musa has killed Harun, and he envied him because the Children of Israel loved him." Musa (peace be upon him) said: "Woe to you! He was my brother, so how could I kill him?" When they insisted against him, he stood and prayed two rak'ahs, then called upon Allah, and the couch descended until they saw him between the sky and the earth, and they believed him.

From Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: Musa and Harun (peace be upon them both) climbed the mountain, and Harun died while Musa remained. The Children of Israel said to Musa (peace be upon him): "You killed him," and they harmed him. So Allah commanded the angels, and they carried him until they passed by him over the Children of Israel, and the angels spoke of his death until the Children of Israel knew that he had died. Then Allah cleared him of what they had said. Then the angels carried him and buried him, and no one came to know the place of his grave except the vulture (al-rakham), so Allah made it deaf and mute.

Amr ibn Maymun said: Harun died before Musa (peace be upon him) in the wandering. They had both gone out to some caves, and Harun died, and Musa buried him and returned to the Children of Israel, and they said: "You killed him out of our love for him," for he was beloved among the Children of Israel. So Musa (peace be upon him) humbly pleaded to his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, and Allah revealed to him: "Set out with them to his grave, for I will resurrect him." So he took them to his grave [[In manuscript B: "So he called out: 'O Harun!'"]], and he came out of his grave shaking his head, and said: "Did I kill you?" He said: "No, but I died." He said: "Return to your resting place." Then they departed.

He asked the sun to stand still and the moon to remain until he took vengeance upon the enemies of Allah, the Exalted, before the Sabbath began. So the sun was returned to him and added to the day by an hour, until he had killed them all. He pursued the kings of Syria and seized from them thirty-one kings, until he prevailed over all the land of Syria, and all of Syria became the Children of Israel's. He distributed his officials across its regions and gathered the spoils, but the fire did not descend [to consume them]. So Allah revealed to Yusha' that there was embezzlement among them, so he commanded them to pledge allegiance, and they pledged allegiance to him. The hand of a man among them stuck to his hand, and he said: "Bring what you have." So the man brought him the head of a golden ox, adorned with rubies and jewels, which he had embezzled. He placed it in the offering, and he placed the man with it. Then the fire came and consumed the man and the offering. Then Yusha' died and was buried on Mount Ephraim. His age was one hundred and twenty-six years, and his management of the affairs of the Children of Israel after Musa (peace be upon him) lasted twenty-seven years.

**The Almighty's words: ﴿And recite to them the news of the two sons of Adam, in truth﴾**, and they are Habil and Qabil. [[The naming of the sons of Adam as "Qabil" and "Habil" is only what scholars have related from the People of the Scripture (Ahl al-Kitab). No text about it has come in the Qur'an, nor in an authentic Sunnah, as far as we know. So we need not affirm it or favour it; it is only a reported opinion. See: ʿUmdat al-Tafsir by Shaykh Ahmad Shakir: 4/123.]] He is also called Qabin. **﴿When they both offered an offering﴾**. The reason for their offering, as the scholars have mentioned, was that Hawwa' (Eve) used to bear a boy and a girl to Adam (peace be upon him) with every pregnancy. All that she bore came to forty children in twenty pregnancies. The first of them was Qabil and his twin sister Aqlima, and the last was Abd al-Mughith and his twin sister Amat al-Mughith. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, blessed the offspring of Adam (peace be upon him). Ibn ʿAbbas said: Adam did not die until his descendants and the descendants of his descendants reached forty thousand.

The scholars differed about the birth of Qabil and Habil. Some of them said: Adam had intercourse with Hawwa' a hundred years after they descended to the earth, and she bore Qabil and his twin Aqlima in one womb, then she bore Habil and his twin Labuda in another.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, on the authority of some of the People of the Previous Scripture: Adam used to have intercourse with Hawwa' in Paradise before he committed the sin. She conceived Qabil and his twin Aqlima there, and she did not experience during it any pregnancy cravings (wahm), pain (wasab), or labour pains (talq) until she gave birth to them, and she did not see any blood with them. When he descended to the earth, he had intercourse with her again, and she conceived Habil and his twin. She experienced with them the pregnancy cravings, the pain, the labour pains and the bleeding. When his children grew up, Adam would marry a boy from one womb to a girl from another womb. So a man among them could marry whichever of his sisters he wished, except his twin who was born with him, because at that time there were no women except their sisters. When Qabil and his twin Aqlima were born, and then Habil and his twin Labuda, and there was a gap of two years between them according to al-Kalbi's statement, and they reached maturity, Allah, Exalted is He, commanded Adam (peace be upon him) to marry Qabil to Labuda, the sister of Habil, and to marry Habil to Aqlima, the sister of Qabil. Qabil's sister was more beautiful than Habil's sister. Adam mentioned this to his sons. Habil was pleased, but Qabil was angry and said: "She is my sister, and I have more right to her." He said: "We are from the offspring [of] Paradise and they are from the offspring [of] the earth." His father said to him: "She is not lawful to you." He refused to accept this and said: "Allah did not command him with this; it is only from his own opinion." Adam (peace be upon him) said to them both: "Offer an offering, and whichever of you has his offering accepted, he has more right to her." The offerings, when they were accepted, a white fire would descend from the sky and consume them. When they were not accepted, the fire would not descend and birds and beasts would eat them. So they both went out to offer an offering. Qabil was a farmer. He offered a heap of food from the worst of his crops, and he concealed in himself: "I do not care whether it is accepted from me or not, but he shall never marry my sister." Habil was a shepherd. He chose the best ram from his flock and offered it, and he concealed in himself the pleasure of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. They placed their offerings on top of the mountain. Then Adam (peace be upon him) prayed, and a fire descended from the sky and consumed the offering of Habil, and did not consume the offering of Qabil. [[This story was narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir: 6/188 (Halabi edition). Ibn Kathir related several narrations on this that agree in meaning: 2/42–44. Shaykh Ahmad Muhammad Shakir said in ʿUmdat al-Tafsir: 4/124: "This is from the stories of the People of the Scripture; it has no authentic basis. Then the Hafiz Ibn Kathir related reports with this meaning, with which the books of the commentators are filled," and he commented on al-Tabari's narration that Ibn Kathir related, saying: "It is a report which, as you see, is not from the Prophetic Sunnah; rather its apparent meaning shows that it is from what Ibn ʿAbbas took from the books of the People of the Scripture."]] This is the saying of the Almighty: **﴿So it was accepted from one of them﴾** [meaning Habil] **﴿and was not accepted from the other﴾**, meaning Qabil. They returned from the mountain, and Qabil was angry because his offering was rejected, and he concealed envy in himself until Adam came to Makkah to visit the House. When Adam had gone, Qabil came to Habil while he was with his flock. **﴿He said: "I will surely kill you."﴾** He said: "Why?" He said: "Because Allah accepted your offering and rejected mine, and you marry my beautiful sister and I marry your ugly sister. People will say that you are better than me, and your offspring will boast over my offspring." **﴿He said﴾** Habil said: "What is my fault? **﴿Indeed, Allah accepts only from the righteous.﴾**"

**﴿If you stretch out your hand against me to kill me, I will not stretch out my hand against you to kill you; indeed I fear Allah, the Lord of the worlds.﴾** [The verb] "baṣaṭta" means "madadta," you extended.

ʿAbdullah ibn ʿUmar said: "By Allah, the one who was killed was indeed the stronger of the two men, but his scrupulousness prevented him from extending his hand against his brother." In the Sharia (ʿurf al-sharīʿa, the religious law), this is permissible for one who is intended to be killed: that he submit and surrender, seeking reward, as ʿUthman (may Allah be pleased with him) did. Mujahid said: "It was prescribed for them at that time that when a man intended to kill another, he should not resist but should be patient."

**﴿I intend that you bear﴾**, i.e., return, and it was said: bear the burden of, **﴿my sin and your sin﴾**, meaning: the sin of killing me, added to your sin, i.e., the sins of your disobedience which you committed before. This is the statement of most of the commentators (mufassirūn, scholars of tafsir). Ibn Abi Najih narrated from Mujahid: "Its meaning is: I want that my sin which I would have committed, if you killed me, and your sin, be upon you, so you bear both my sin and my blood together." It was also said: its meaning is that you return with the sin of killing me and the sin of your disobedience, for which your offering was not accepted.

If it is asked: how could he say "I intend that you bear my sin and your sin," when intending to kill or to disobey is not permissible? It is answered: this is not a true intention, but when he knew that the other would kill him without doubt, he resolved himself to submission, seeking reward; so it was as if he became one who intends his killing in a figurative sense (majāz), though he did not truly intend it. It was also said: its meaning is "I want you to bear the punishment for killing me," so this is a correct intention, because it accords with the command of Allah, mighty and majestic; thus this is not an intention to kill, but to the necessary consequence of killing, namely sin and punishment. **﴿So you will be among the companions of the Fire, and that is the recompense of the wrongdoers.﴾**

His statement, mighty and majestic is He: **﴿So his soul made the killing of his brother seem easy to him﴾**, i.e., it obeyed him, supported him and aided him, **﴿the killing of his brother﴾**, i.e., in killing his brother. [Mujahid said: it encouraged him. Qatadah said: his soul adorned it for him. Yaman said: his soul made that easy for him, i.e., made it smooth.] [[Omitted in manuscript B.]] Its sense is: his soul portrayed to him that killing his brother was made easy and smooth for him, so he killed him. When Qabil intended to kill Habil, he did not know how to kill him. Ibn Jurayj said: Iblis (Satan) appeared to him, took a bird, placed its head on a rock, and crushed its head with another rock, while Qabil watched him; so he taught him killing. Qabil then crushed the head of Habil between two rocks. [See: al-Tabari, 6/195 (Halabi edition); Tafsir Ibn Kathir, 2/46.] It was said: he was killed while submitting, and it was said: he ambushed him while he was asleep and crushed his head and killed him. This is the saying of the Exalted: **﴿So he killed him, and became one of the losers﴾**. Habil was twenty years old when he was killed.

They differed about the place of his killing. [It was said: in Basra, at the site of the Great Mosque; the killer's body turned black, and Adam (peace be upon him) asked him about his brother, and he said: "I was not a guardian over him." He said: "Rather, you killed him, and that is why your body has turned black." Adam remained a hundred years without ever laughing since he killed him.] [[Omitted in manuscript B.]]

Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: it was on the mountain of [Thawr] [[In manuscript B: (Fawd).]]. It was said: at the pass of Hira. When he killed him, he left him in the open and did not know what to do with him, because he was the first dead person on the face of the earth from the children of Adam. Wild beasts approached him, so he carried him on his back in a sack for forty days; Ibn Abbas said: a year, until he rotted. The birds and beasts gathered around him, waiting to see when he would be thrown so they could eat him. Then Allah sent two ravens, which fought, and one of them killed the other. Then it dug a grave for it with its beak and feet until it made a place for it, then it threw it into the pit and covered it, while Qabil watched. This is the saying of the Exalted: **﴿Then Allah sent a raven scratching in the earth to show him how to conceal the nakedness of his brother﴾**. 105/b

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 5, verse 31:

﴿Then God sent a crow, scratching in the earth, to show him how to conceal his brother's corpse.﴾ When Qabil saw that, he said, "Woe is me!", an expression of regret. It was said that when he saw the crow burying, he realised that it had more knowledge than he did, and that what he had done was ignorance, so he regretted it and was filled with remorse. ﴿He said, "Woe is me! Am I unable to be like this crow and conceal my brother's corpse?"﴾ That is, his carcass. It was also said that it means his nakedness, because he had stripped off his clothes. ﴿So he became one of those who regretted it.﴾ That is, regretting having to carry him on his shoulders, not regretting having killed him. It was also said he regretted being separated from his brother. It was also said he regretted the little benefit gained from killing him, since it angered his parents, and he gained nothing from the killing. His regret was not for the killing itself or for committing the sin.

ʿAbd al-Muttalib ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Hanṭab said: When the son of Adam killed his brother, the earth, with everything on it, became parched for seven days. Then the earth drank his blood as water is drunk. Adam called out to him, "Where is your brother Habil?" He said, "I do not know. I was not a guardian over him." God, exalted is He, said, "The blood of your brother cries out to Me from the earth. Why did you kill your brother?" He said, "Where is his blood, if I did kill him?" So God, mighty and majestic, forbade the earth from that day onward ever to drink blood again.

Muqatil ibn Sulayman related from al-Dahhak, from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: When Qabil killed Habil while Adam, upon him be peace, was in Makkah, the trees withered, the foods changed, the fruits turned sour, the water became bitter, and the earth grew dusty. Adam, upon him be peace, said, "Something has happened on the earth." He went to Hind, and there found that Qabil had killed Habil. Then he composed verses, and he was the first to compose poetry. He said:

*The lands have changed, and whoever is upon them;*
*the face of the earth is dusty and ugly.*
*Every thing that had colour and taste has changed,*
*and the brightness of the lovely face has diminished.*

It is also related as "al-Malih" (the lovely).

It is related from Maymun ibn Mihran, from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: Whoever says that Adam, upon him be peace, composed poetry has lied. Muhammad (ﷺ) and all the prophets, peace be upon them, are equal in prohibition regarding poetry. However, when Qabil killed Habil, Adam lamented him, and he was Syriac-speaking. When Adam had composed his lament, he said to Shith, "My son, you are his successor; keep these words so that they may be inherited and people may be moved by them." They continued to be transmitted until they reached Yaʿrub ibn Qahtan. He spoke Arabic and Syriac, and he was the first to write in Arabic, and he used to compose poetry. He examined the lament, moved its earlier parts to the later and the later to the earlier, made it metrical as poetry, and added verses, among them:

*And why should I not generously pour out tears,*
*while Habil is enclosed in the grave?*
*I see the length of life as a grief to me;*
*so am I at rest from my life?*

When one hundred and thirty years of Adam's life, upon him be peace, had passed, which was five years after the killing of Habil, Hawwa bore him Shith. Its meaning is "gift of God." That is, he was a replacement for Habil. God, exalted is He, taught him the hours of night and day and taught him the worship of creation in each hour of them. He sent down to him fifty scrolls, and he became the successor and heir-designate of Adam. As for Qabil, he was told, "Go, a fugitive and wanderer, terrified and frightened, and you shall be safe from no one who sees you." He took his sister Iqlima by the hand and fled with her to ʿAdan in the land of Yemen. Iblis came to him and said, "The fire consumed Habil's offering only because he worshipped fire. So set up a fire for yourself as well, which will be for you and your descendants." He built a house for fire, and he was the first to worship fire. Whoever passed by it, he would throw him into it. A blind son of his approached with a son of his own, and his son said, "This is your father, Qabil," and the blind man's son shot his father and killed him. The blind man said, "Did you kill your father?" He raised his hand and slapped his son, and the son died. The blind man said, "Woe is me! I killed my father with my shot, and I killed my son with my slap."

Mujahid said: One of Qabil's legs became stuck to his thigh and shin, and from that day until the Day of Resurrection it has been stuck, and his face is turned to the sun wherever it turns. In summer he is in an enclosure of fire, and in winter in an enclosure of ice.

He said: The descendants of Qabil devised instruments of amusement, such as reed pipes, drums, flutes, lutes and tanburs. They became absorbed in amusement, drinking wine, worshipping fire, adultery and vile deeds, until God drowned them in the Flood in the days of Nuh, upon him be peace. The descendants of Shith remained.

ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi informed us: Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: ʿUmar ibn Hafs ibn Ghiyath informed us: my father informed us: al-Aʿmash informed us: ʿAbd Allah ibn Murrah narrated to me, from Masruq, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No soul is killed unjustly except that the first son of Adam bears a share of its blood, because he was the first to establish killing." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in the chapter on the Prophets, "The creation of Adam, upon him be peace, and his offspring": 6/364, and in the chapters on blood money and on holding fast to the Sunnah. Also narrated by Muslim in the chapter on the Qasamah, "Explaining who established killing," no. (1677), 3/1303-1304, and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/234.]

**The Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 5, Verse 32**

His saying, may He be glorified and exalted: ﴿Because of that﴾. Abu Ja'far (a reciter of the Qur'an) read *مِنِ اجْلِ ذَلِكَ* with a kasra on the nun and the words joined, whereas the common reading (*qira'at al-'ammah*) has the nun with a sukun (*bi-jazm al-nun*). The meaning is: *min jarra'i dhalika al-qatil wa jinayatihi*, that is, because of that killer and his crime. It is said: *ajala yu'jalu ajalan* when he committed a crime (*idha jana*), like *akhadha yakhudhu akhdhan*.

﴿We prescribed for the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul unless for a soul or for corruption [done] in the land﴾ (he kills it), so he is to be subjected to retaliation (*yuqad minhu*, *qisas*, equal retribution). ﴿Or for corruption in the land﴾: he means, unless for a soul or for corruption in the land, such as disbelief (*kufr*), fornication (*zina*), highway robbery (*qat' al-tariq*), or the like. ﴿It is as if he had slain mankind entirely﴾. The scholars differed concerning its interpretation.

Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said, in the narration of Ikrimah: whoever kills a prophet or a just leader, it is as if he had slain mankind entirely, and whoever supports a prophet or a just leader, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely.

Mujahid said: whoever kills a forbidden soul will enter the Fire for killing it, just as he would enter it had he killed mankind entirely. ﴿And whoever saves it﴾: whoever is spared from killing it, it is as if he had been spared from killing mankind entirely.

Qatadah said: Allah magnified its reward and magnified its burden. The meaning is: whoever deems the killing of a Muslim lawful without right, it is as if he had slain mankind entirely in sin, because they are not safe from him. ﴿And whoever saves it﴾ and refrains from killing it, ﴿it is as if he had saved mankind entirely﴾ [in reward, because they are safe from him]. Al-Hasan said: ﴿it is as if he had slain mankind entirely﴾. He means that the retaliation (*qisas*) due upon him for killing it is like that which would be due upon him had he killed mankind entirely. ﴿And whoever saves it﴾: that is, he pardons the one who is owed retaliation (*qisas*) and does not kill him, so it is as if he had saved mankind entirely.

Sulayman ibn 'Ali said: I said to al-Hasan, "O Abu Sa'id, is it (this ruling) for us as it was for the Children of Israel?" He said: "Indeed, by Him besides whom there is no god, the blood of the Children of Israel was not more honoured by Allah than our blood."

﴿And certainly Our messengers came to them with clear evidences. Then indeed many of them after that throughout the land were transgressors﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 5, verse 33:

﴿Indeed, the penalty for those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and strive upon the earth in corruption﴾ ... [the verse continues]. Al-Dahhak said: It was revealed concerning a people of the People of the Book who had a covenant with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. They broke the covenant, cut off the road, and spread corruption on the earth [[Recorded by al-Tabari from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Some of the People of the Book had a covenant with the Prophet..." And he recorded from al-Dahhak, who said: "A people had a covenant with the Messenger of Allah," without mentioning that they were People of the Book. Tafsir al-Tabari: 6/206 (Halabi edition). al-Suyuti also attributed it to Abd ibn Humayd: al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/69.]].

Al-Kalbi said: It was revealed concerning the people of Hilal ibn Uwaymir. The Prophet ﷺ had made a pact with Hilal ibn Uwaymir, who was Abu Burda al-Aslami, that he would not aid anyone against him and no one would aid anyone against him, and whoever passed by Hilal ibn Uwaymir on the way to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was safe and not to be harmed. Then a group from Banu Kinana passed, intending to embrace Islam, with some people from Aslam of the people of Hilal ibn Uwaymir. Hilal was not present, so [they attacked them] [[In "B": "they guided them against them" (fahadaw ilayhim).]], killed them, and took their property. Then Jibril ('alayhi al-salam) descended with the ruling concerning them.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: It was revealed concerning some people from 'Uraynah and 'Ukl who came to the Prophet ﷺ and pledged allegiance to him for Islam, while they were liars. The Prophet ﷺ sent them to the camels of charity (sadaqah), and they apostatized, killed the herdsman, and drove off the camels.

[Ahbarana 'Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi: Ana Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi: Ana Muhammad ibn Yusuf: Tha Muhammad ibn Isma'il: Tha 'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah: Tha al-Walid ibn Muslim: Tha al-Awza'i: Haddathani Yahya ibn Abi Kathir: Haddathani Abu Qilaba al-Jarmi] [[The isnad is missing from this point to the end of folio (106) of the Zahiriyya manuscript.]] from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: A group from 'Ukl came to the Prophet ﷺ and embraced Islam, but the climate of Madinah did not agree with them. So the Prophet [ﷺ] [[Omitted in "B".]] ordered them to go to the camels of charity and drink from their urine and milk. They did so and recovered, then they apostatized, killed their herdsmen, and drove off the camels. The Prophet ﷺ sent after them, and they were brought back. He cut off their hands and feet, branded their eyes with hot iron, and did not cauterize them until they died.

And Ayyub narrated from Abu Qilaba, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: He cut off their hands and feet, then ordered nails [heated] and branded their eyes with them, and they were thrown in al-Harrah, asking for water, but they were not given water until they died. Abu Qilaba said: They had killed, stolen, waged war against Allah and His Messenger, and strove upon the earth in corruption [[Recorded by al-Bukhari in al-Maghazi, chapter on the story of 'Ukl and 'Uraynah: 7/458, and in al-Hudud; and Muslim in al-Qasamah, chapter on the ruling for those who wage war and apostates, no. (1671): 3/1296-1297. The author also in Sharh al-Sunnah: 10/256-257.]]. [This is what is meant by the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿and strive upon the earth in corruption﴾] [[Omitted from "B".]].

They differed concerning the ruling on these 'Uraynis. Some said: this ruling is abrogated (mansukhah) because mutilation (muthlah) is not permitted. Others said: the ruling stands, except for the branding of the eyes [and mutilation] [[Omitted from "B".]]. Qatadah narrated from Ibn Sirin that this happened before [the hadd punishment was revealed] [[In "B": "the hudud were revealed."]]. Abu al-Zinad said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did that to them, Allah revealed the hudud and forbade mutilation, and he did not return to it.

From Qatadah, who said: We have been told that after that, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to urge charity and forbid mutilation [[See: al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Maghazi: 7/458.]]. Sulayman al-Taymi narrated from Anas: The Prophet ﷺ only branded the eyes of those people because they had branded the eyes of the herdsmen. Al-Layth ibn Sa'd said: This verse was revealed rebuking the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and teaching him their punishment; it said: Their penalty is this, not mutilation. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ never stood to deliver a sermon without forbidding mutilation.

They differed concerning the warring robbers (muharibin) who deserve this hadd. Some people said: they are those who cut off the road and carry weapons, and those who commit armed robbery in the cities. This is the opinion of al-Awza'i, Malik, al-Layth ibn Sa'd and al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on them.

Others said: those who commit armed robbery in the cities do not have the status of muharibin in deserving these hudud. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, may Allah be pleased with him.

The punishment of the muharibin is what Allah, glorified and exalted, mentioned: ﴿that they be killed, or crucified, or have their hands and feet cut off on alternate sides, or be banished from the land﴾. Some people held that the imam has a choice regarding the muharibin among killing, cutting, crucifixion, [and banishment] [[Omitted from "B".]], as the apparent meaning of the verse indicates. This is the view of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, al-Hasan, al-Nakha'i and Mujahid.

Most scholars held that these punishments are arranged according to the crimes, not as a matter of choice. [Because 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib informed us: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal informed us: Abu al-'Abbas al-Asamm informed us: al-Rabi' informed us: al-Shafi'i informed us: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad informed us, from Salih, mawla al-Tawamah] [[What is between the parentheses is omitted from "A".]], from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, concerning highway robbers: if they killed and took property, they are killed and crucified; if they killed and did not take property, they are killed and not crucified; if they took property and did not kill, their hands and feet are cut off on alternate sides; if they terrified the road and took no property, they are banished from the land [[Recorded by al-Shafi'i in al-Musnad: 2/86 (Tartib al-Musnad). In its chain is Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Yahya al-Aslami, who is abandoned (matruk) (al-Taqrib). And Salih, mawla al-Tawamah, is Salih ibn Nabhan, truthful but he became confused in his later years (Taqrib).]].

This is also the opinion of Qatadah, al-Awza'i, al-Shafi'i and the people of opinion (ashab al-ra'y), may Allah the Exalted have mercy on them.

[If a highway robber kills, he is killed] [[Addition from "B".]] definitively, so that the sentence is not dropped by the pardon of the victim's heir. If he takes property amounting to a nisab, which is a quarter dinar, his right hand and left foot are cut off. If he kills and takes property, he is killed and crucified.

They differed about the manner of it: The apparent position of al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, is that he is killed and then crucified. It was also said: he is crucified alive and then stabbed until he dies on the cross. This is the opinion of al-Layth ibn Sa'd. It was also said: he is crucified alive for three days, then taken down and killed. If he terrifies the road, he is banished.

They differed about banishment (nafy). Some people held that the imam pursues him, and wherever he is found he is banished from it. This is the view of Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz. It was also said: he is pursued so that the hudud may be carried out on him. This is the view of Ibn Abbas and al-Layth ibn Sa'd, and al-Shafi'i also said so. The people of Kufah said: banishment is imprisonment, and it is a banishment from the land. Muhammad ibn Jarir [al-Tabari] said: he is banished from his town to another and imprisoned in the prison of the place to which he was banished, until his repentance appears. Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, was the first to imprison people in prisons [[Omitted from "B".]], and he said: I imprison him until I know his repentance from him, and I do not banish him to a town where he would harm its people.

﴿That﴾, the punishment I have mentioned, ﴿is a disgrace for them﴾, meaning punishment, humiliation and exposure, ﴿in this world, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 5, verse 34:

﴿Except for those who repent before you have power over them; so know that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. As for the one who holds that the verse was revealed concerning the disbelievers, he says its meaning is: except for those who repent of their polytheism and embrace Islam before you gain power over them, for then there is no punishment (sabil) against them with any of the hudud (prescribed penalties), and no liability (tabi'ah) for them regarding what they inflicted during the state of disbelief, whether blood or property. As for Muslims who wage war (al-muharibun), whoever of them repents [[In "B": died.]] before power over him is gained, that is, before the imam (ruler) has seized him, every penalty that is due as a right of Allah drops from him; but what is a right of the servants (huquq al-'ibad) does not drop. If he has killed during highway robbery (qat' al-tariq), the obligation of the mandatory execution (tahattum al-qatl) drops from him by repenting before power over him is gained, but retaliation (qisas) remains for the victim's heir (wali al-qatil): if he wishes he may pardon him, and if he wishes he may exact it in full. If he has taken property, the amputation (al-qat') drops from him [[Added from "B".]]. If he has combined both, the obligation of mandatory execution and crucifixion (salb) drops from him, and liability for the property is required. This is the view of al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him.

Some of them said: if he comes repentant before power over him is gained, no one has any liability upon him regarding blood or property, except that if a particular item of property is found with him, he returns it to its owner.

It is related from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, concerning Harithah ibn Yazid, who went out as a highway robber, shed blood and took property, then came repentant before he was captured, that 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, did not impose upon him any liability [regarding blood or property, except that if property was found with him, it is returned to its owner]. [[What is between the brackets is an addition from "B"; see al-Tabari: 6/221, al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/70.]] As for one who repents after power over him is gained, nothing of these penalties drops from him.

It is also said: every penalty that is due as a right of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, among the penalties for highway robbery, theft (qat' al-sariqah), the hadd for fornication (zina) and for drinking wine, drops by repentance in every case; but most scholars hold that it does not drop.

﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and seek the means of nearness to Him﴾ — seek (اطْلُبُوا). ﴿Al-wasilah﴾ means nearness (الْقُرْبَةَ). It is of the pattern فَعِيلَة, from "tawassala ila fulan bi kadha," meaning he drew near to him by such-and-such. Its plural is wasa'il. ﴿And strive in His cause that you may prosper﴾ [Its summary: obey the command of Allah, and you will be saved] [[The words in brackets are omitted from manuscript "A".]].

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve — if they had whatever is on the earth entirely and the like of it with it, to ransom themselves therewith from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, it would not be accepted from them﴾. He informs that if the disbeliever owned the whole world and the like of it besides, and then ransomed himself with all of it from the punishment, that ransom would not be accepted from him. ﴿And for them is a painful punishment.﴾

﴿They will wish to exit from the Fire, but they will not be ones who exit from it﴾. There are two views on this. The first: they intend and seek a way out of it, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Every time they wish to come out of it﴾ [al-Hajj: 22]. The second: they wish for that in their hearts, as Allah the Exalted says, reporting about them: "Our Lord, bring us out of it" [al-Mu'minun: 107]. ﴿And for them is a lasting punishment.﴾

﴿As for the thief, male and female, cut off their hands﴾. He meant by it their right hands (أَيْمَانَهُمَا). Likewise it is in the codex of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him.

Its ruling: whoever steals a nisab (the minimum amount of property for which the hand is cut) from property kept in a secured place (hirz), in which he has no claim of right (shubhah), his right hand is cut off at the wrist. There is no requirement to cut for stealing less than the nisab, according to the majority of scholars. It is reported from Ibn al-Zubayr that he used to cut for a small amount, but the majority of scholars differ with him.

They differed regarding the amount for which the hand is cut. Most of them held that it is not cut for less than a quarter of a dinar. If he steals a quarter of a dinar, or goods whose value is a quarter of a dinar, the hand is cut. This is the view of Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman and Ali, may Allah be pleased with them all, and it was said by Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, al-Awza'i and al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on them, based on what was related to us by Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Kisa'i: Abd al-'Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal informed us: Abu al-'Abbas al-Asamm informed us: al-Rabi' informed us: al-Shafi'i informed us: Ibn 'Uyaynah informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from Urwah, from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The cutting is for a quarter of a dinar or more." [[Reported by al-Shafi'i in al-Musnad: 2/83; al-Bukhari in Hudud, chapter on the saying of Allah, "And the thief, male and female, cut off their hands," and on how much is cut: 12/96; Muslim in Hudud, chapter on the penalty for theft and its nisab, no. (1684): 3/1312; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 10/312.]]

Abu al-Hasan al-Shirazi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Nafi', from Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ cut off a thief for a shield (mijann) whose price was three dirhams. [[Reported by al-Bukhari, in the same place: 12/97; Muslim, in the same place, no. (1686): 3/1313; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 10/313.]]

It is reported from Uthman that he cut off a thief for a citron (utrujjah) valued at three dirhams, by the exchange rate of twelve dirhams to a dinar. This is the view of Malik, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him, that the hand is cut for three dirhams.

A group held that it is not cut for less than a dinar or ten dirhams. This is reported from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him, and Sufyan al-Thawri and the people of opinion (ashab al-ra'y) followed this view.

Another group said it is cut only for five dirhams. This is reported from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, and Ibn Abi Layla said it too. Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Umar ibn Hafs ibn Ghiyath informed us: my father informed me: al-A'mash informed us, saying: I heard Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "May Allah curse the thief who steals an egg and so his hand is cut off, and who steals a rope and so his hand is cut off." [[Reported by al-Bukhari in Hudud, chapter on the curse of the thief when he is not named: 12/81; Muslim in the same place, no. (1687): 3/1314; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 10/314.]] Al-A'mash said: They used to think that it meant the eggs of iron and the rope, which some of them are worth dirhams.

Whoever holds the cutting for a small amount argues by this hadith, but according to most scholars it is to be understood in light of what al-A'mash said, and in light of the hadith of Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her: "And if he steals something from an unsecured place, such as fruit in an orchard with no guard, or an animal in the open wilderness with no keeper, or goods in a house cut off from the houses, there is no cutting upon him." [[Bracketed text is an addition from manuscript "B".]] 106/b

It is reported from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: "There is no cutting for hanging fruit, nor for an animal of the mountain pasture (harisat jabal). But when the enclosure (murah) or the drying-place (jarin) shelters it, then the cutting is for what reaches the value of a shield." [[Reported by Imam Malik in al-Muwatta', Book of Hudud, chapter on what requires cutting: 2/831. Ibn Abd al-Barr said: "The transmitters of the Muwatta' did not differ in its being mursal, and its meaning is connected through the hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr and others." It was connected by al-Nasa'i from Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, in the chapter on the theft of hanging fruit, and in the chapter on fruit stolen after it has been sheltered in the drying-place: 8/84-86; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 10/319.]]

It is reported from Ibn Jurayj, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "There is no cutting for the embezzler, nor for the plunderer, nor for the one who snatches." [[Reported by Abu Dawud in Hudud, chapter on cutting for snatching and embezzlement: 6/224-225; al-Tirmidhi in Hudud, chapter on what has come concerning the embezzler and the snatcher: 5/8-9, and he said: this is a hasan sahih hadith; al-Nasa'i in the chapter on what carries no cutting: 8/89; Ibn Majah in Hudud, chapter on the embezzler, the plunderer and the snatcher: 2/864; and al-Darimi in the chapter on what is not cut from thieves: 2/175. Ibn Hibban authenticated it, no. (1502, 1503), from Mawarid al-Zam'an. Al-Zayla'i said in Nasb al-Rayah: 3/364: "Abd al-Haqq was silent about it in his Ahkam, and Ibn al-Qattan after him, so it is sahih according to both of them." See also Sharh al-Sunnah: 10/321-322.]]

If he steals property in which he has a claim of right (shubhah), such as a slave stealing from his master's property, or a child stealing from his father's property, or a father stealing from his child's property, or one of two partners stealing something from the common property, there is no cutting upon him.

If a thief steals for the first time, his right hand is cut off at the wrist. Then if he steals a second time, his left foot is cut off at the ankle joint.

They differed regarding if he steals a third time. Most of them held that his left hand is cut off; then if he steals a fourth time, his right foot is cut off; then if after that he steals anything, he is disciplined (yu'azzar) and imprisoned until his repentance becomes apparent. This is what is related from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, and it is the view of Qatadah, and Malik and al-Shafi'i said it, based on what is related from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Concerning the thief who steals: if he steals, cut off his hand; then if he steals, cut off his foot; then if he steals, cut off his hand; then if he steals, cut off his foot." [[Reported by al-Daraqutni in al-Sunan: 3/181; al-Tabarani and al-Shafi'i (Majma' al-Zawa'id: 6/275; Talkhis al-Habir: 4/68). Ibn Hajar said: its isnad is weak, and al-Albani authenticated it with its corroborating reports in Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i and al-Bayhaqi. See Irwa' al-Ghalil: 8/86-89.]]

A group held that if he steals a third time after his right hand and left foot have been cut off, he is not cut but imprisoned. This is reported from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "Indeed I am ashamed not to leave him a hand with which to cleanse himself, nor a foot with which to walk." [[Reported by Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf: 9/509; and Ibn al-Turkmani mentioned it in al-Jawhar al-Naqi in refutation of al-Bayhaqi, printed with the Sunan: 8/274.]] This is the view of al-Sha'bi and al-Nakha'i, and al-Awza'i, Ahmad and the people of opinion said it too.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿A recompense for what they earned﴾ is in the accusative as a circumstantial and as a cause (naṣb 'ala al-hal wa al-qat'). Similarly: ﴿a deterrent﴾, meaning a punishment, ﴿from Allah. And Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.﴾

﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and seek the means of nearness to Him﴾ — seek (اطْلُبُوا). ﴿Al-wasilah﴾ means nearness (الْقُرْبَةَ). It is of the pattern فَعِيلَة, from "tawassala ila fulan bi kadha," meaning he drew near to him by such-and-such. Its plural is wasa'il. ﴿And strive in His cause that you may prosper﴾ [Its summary: obey the command of Allah, and you will be saved] [[The words in brackets are omitted from manuscript "A".]].

The first: they intend and seek a way out of it, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Every time they wish to come out of it﴾ [al-Hajj: 22]. The second: they wish for that in their hearts, as Allah the Exalted says, reporting about them: "Our Lord, bring us out of it" [al-Mu'minun: 107]. ﴿And for them is a lasting punishment.﴾

[[Reported by al-Shafi'i in al-Musnad: 2/83; al-Bukhari in Hudud, chapter on the saying of Allah, "And the thief, male and female, cut off their hands," and on how much is cut: 12/96; Muslim in Hudud, chapter on the penalty for theft and its nisab, no. (1684): 3/1312; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 10/312.]]
