﴿So whoever repents after his wrongdoing﴾, that is, after his theft, ﴿and makes amends﴾ in his deeds, ﴿indeed Allah will turn to him in forgiveness. Indeed Allah is Forgiving, Merciful﴾. This applies to what is between him and Allah the Exalted. As for the amputation, it does not fall away by repentance according to most scholars. Mujahid said: "The amputation of the thief is his repentance; once his hand is cut off, repentance is achieved." The sound view is that the amputation is a requital for the crime, as Allah says: ﴿a recompense for what they had earned﴾. Therefore repentance is still required afterward, and his repentance consists of regret for what has passed and resolve not to return to it in the future. When the thief's hand is cut off, he is obligated, according to the majority of scholars, to repay the value of what he stole. Sufyan al-Thawri and the people of opinion (ashab al-ra'y, the Hanafi school) said: "He has no obligation to repay." By consensus, if the stolen property is still in his possession, it is recovered, and his hand is cut off, because the amputation is the right of Allah the Exalted and the repayment is the right of the servant; neither prevents the other, like the recovery of the item itself.

His saying the Exalted: ﴿Do you not know that to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth?﴾ The address is to the Prophet ﷺ, and what is meant is everyone. It is also said: the meaning is "Do you not know, O human being," so it is an address to every person. ﴿He punishes whom He wills and forgives whom He wills﴾. Al-Suddi and al-Kalbi said: "He punishes whom He wills" refers to those who die upon their disbelief, and "forgives whom He wills" refers to those who repent from their disbelief [the grave sin]. Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "He punishes whom He wills for a minor sin, and forgives whom He wills for a major sin." ﴿And Allah is over all things Competent﴾.

His saying the Exalted: ﴿O Messenger, let not those grieve you who hasten into disbelief﴾, that is, in allying themselves with the disbelievers, ﴿for they cannot harm Allah at all﴾, ﴿among those who say with their mouths "We believe" but their hearts have not believed﴾, and they are the hypocrites. ﴿And among those who are Jews﴾, meaning the Jews, ﴿are listeners to falsehood﴾, that is, a people who listen to falsehood, ﴿who are listeners to falsehood﴾, meaning those who speak falsehood, like the one praying who says "Sami' Allahu liman hamidah" (Allah hears whoever praises Him), meaning Allah accepts. It is also said: they listen to falsehood for its sake, that is, they listen to you in order to lie about you. That is because they would hear from the Messenger ﷺ, then go out and say, "We heard from him such-and-such," though they had not heard that from him. ﴿Listeners for another people who have not come to you﴾, that is, they are spies for another people, meaning the Banu Qurayzah on behalf of another people, who are the people of Khaybar.

The matter was that a man and a woman of the nobles of Khaybar committed adultery, and both were married. Their punishment in the Torah was stoning, but the Jews disliked stoning them because of their nobility. They said: "This man in Yathrib does not have stoning in his book, but only flogging. So send to your brothers, the Banu Qurayzah, for they are his neighbors and allies; let them ask him about this." The Prophet ﷺ commanded that the two be stoned at the gate of his mosque, and said: "O Allah, I am the first to revive Your command after they had caused it to die." Then Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿O Messenger, let not those grieve you who hasten into disbelief﴾ [see: Tafsir al-Tabari 6/232, al-Durr al-Manthur 3/78, Ibn Kathir 2/60-61].

Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Nafi', from Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them, who said: The Jews came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and mentioned to him that a man and a woman from among them had committed adultery. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them: "What do you find in the Torah concerning the matter of stoning?" They said: "We expose them and they are flogged." Abdullah ibn Salam said: "You have lied; indeed in it is the verse of stoning." So they brought the Torah and spread it open, and one of them placed his hand over the verse of stoning, reading what was before it and after it. Abdullah said to him: "Lift your hand." He lifted his hand, and there was the verse of stoning. They said: "He has spoken truly, O Muhammad, in it is the verse of stoning." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered them stoned, and Abdullah ibn Umar said: "I saw the man bending over the woman, shielding her from the stones" [narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Manaqib, chapter "They recognize him as they recognize their sons..." 6/631, and in al-Tafsir and al-Tawhid, and the wording is his; and Muslim in al-Hudud, chapter on the stoning of Jews, dhimmis, for adultery, no. 1699, 3/1326].

It is also said: the occasion of revelation of this verse was retaliation (qisas, the law of equal retribution). The Banu al-Nadir had superiority over the Banu Qurayzah, so the Banu Qurayzah said: "O Muhammad, our brothers, the Banu al-Nadir, have the same father, the same religion, and the same prophet as us. When they kill one of us, they do not retaliate against them, and they give us a blood-money (diyah) of seventy wasq of dates. When we kill one of them, they kill the killer and take from us double: one hundred and forty wasq of dates. If the victim is a woman, they kill a man of ours for her, and for a man of theirs they kill two men of ours, and for a free man of theirs they kill a slave of ours. Our wounds are doubled compared to their wounds. Judge between us and them." So Allah, the Exalted, revealed this verse [see: Tafsir al-Tabari 6/243, al-Durr al-Manthur 3/78, Ibn Kathir 2/61-62].

The first view is more sound, because the verse concerns stoning.

His saying: ﴿And among those who are Jews, listeners to falsehood﴾. It is said: the lam here means "to" (ila). It is also said: it is the lam of purpose, meaning: they listen in order that they may lie about you. The lam in His saying ﴿for another people﴾ means: for the sake of another people ﴿who have not come to you﴾, and they are the people of Khaybar. ﴿They distort the words [plural of kalimah] ﴿from their places﴾, meaning: after their placement in their places. He mentioned the pronoun in response to the word "kalim" (words). ﴿They say: If you are given this, then take it﴾, meaning: if Muhammad ﷺ has given you a ruling of flogging and tahmim, then accept it. ﴿And if you are not given it, then beware.﴾ ﴿And whoever Allah intends for a trial﴾, meaning his disbelief and misguidance. Al-Dahhak said: his destruction. Qatadah said: his punishment. ﴿You will not possess for him anything from Allah﴾, meaning you will not be able to repel the command of Allah concerning him. ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah did not intend to purify their hearts﴾. This contains a refutation of those who deny divine decree. ﴿For them in this world is disgrace﴾, that is, for the hypocrites and the Jews. The disgrace of the hypocrites is exposure and the tearing away of their veil by the manifestation of their hypocrisy. The disgrace of the Jews is the jizyah (poll tax), killing, captivity, and exile, and what they see from Muhammad ﷺ and his companions of what they dislike. ﴿And for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment﴾, which is eternal abiding in the Fire.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 5, verse 42:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They are listeners to falsehood, devourers of what is unlawful (suht)﴾. Ibn Kathir, Abu Ja'far, the people of Basra, and al-Kisa'i read "لِلسُّحُتِ" with a damma on the ḥāʾ, while the others read it with a sukūn. It means what is forbidden (ḥarām), and its root meaning is destruction and severity. Allah, may He be exalted, says: ﴿So He will destroy you with a punishment﴾ (Ta-Ha, 61). It was revealed concerning the Jewish judges, such as Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf and those like him, who used to accept bribes and judge in favour of whoever bribed them.

Al-Hasan said: When one of them was approached by someone with a bribe, the judge would put it in his sleeve, show it to him, and speak about his need, and he would listen to him without looking at his opponent. So he hears falsehood and eats the bribe.

He also said: That applies to the ruler when you bribe him so that he makes falsehood right for you, or nullifies a right for you. As for a man giving a ruler whom he fears for his injustice in order to ward off harm from himself, there is no harm in that. So suht is the bribe in judgment according to the saying of al-Hasan, Muqatil, Qatadah, and al-Dahhak. Ibn Mas'ud said: It is a bribe in everything. Ibn Mas'ud also said: Whoever intercedes in order to restore a right or to repel an injustice (a falsehood) and is then given a gift and accepts it, that is suht. It was said to him: "O Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, we did not think that this was anything but taking payment for judgment." He said: "Taking payment for judgment is disbelief."[[Al-Tabari: 6 / 240.]] Allah, may He be exalted, says: ﴿Whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, they are the disbelievers﴾ (Surat al-Ma'idah, 44).

We were informed by ʿAbd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Shurayh informed us: Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi related to us: ʿAli ibn al-Ja'd related to us: Ibn Abi Dhi'b informed us, from al-Harith ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, from Abu Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah has cursed the one who gives a bribe and the one who takes a bribe."[[Related by Abu Dawud in al-Aqdiyah, chapter on the disapproval of bribery: 5 / 207; al-Tirmidhi in al-Ahkam, chapter on what has been related about the one who gives and the one who takes a bribe in judgment: 4 / 567, and he said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith"; and Ibn Majah in al-Ahkam, chapter on severity regarding injustice and bribery: 2 / 775. Al-Hakim authenticated it: 4 / 102-103, and al-Dhahabi agreed. The author also related it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 10 / 87-88.]]

And suht is every earning that is not lawful.

His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿So if they come to you, judge between them or turn away from them. And if you turn away from them, they cannot harm you at all﴾. Allah, may He be exalted, gave His Messenger (ﷺ) the choice regarding judging between them: if he wished he would judge, and if he wished he would leave it.

They differed concerning the ruling of this verse today: is the judge free to choose whether to judge between the protected non-Muslims (ahl al-dhimmah, those under the protection of the Muslim state) when they bring their case to us? Most scholars said: It is a binding ruling, and there is nothing abrogated in Surat al-Ma'idah. The rulers of the Muslims have the choice in judging between the People of the Book: if they wish they judge, and if they wish they do not judge; and if they do judge, they judge by the ruling of Islam. This is the view of al-Nakha'i, al-Sha'bi, ʿAta', and Qatadah.

Others said: It is obligatory upon the ruler of the Muslims to judge between them, and the verse is abrogated. It was abrogated by His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And judge between them by what Allah has revealed﴾ (Surat al-Ma'idah, 49). This is the view of Mujahid and ʿIkrimah, and it is related from Ibn ʿAbbas,[[See: Al-Tabari: 6 / 744-747; al-Nasikh wa al-Mansukh by Abu al-Qasim Hibat Allah ibn Salamah, pp. 41-42; Ahkam al-Qur'an by al-Jassas: 4 / 87-89.]] who said: "Only two verses of al-Ma'idah have been abrogated: His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿Do not violate the sacred symbols of Allah﴾, which was abrogated by His saying, may He be exalted, 'Kill the polytheists'; and His saying: ﴿So if they come to you, judge between them or turn away from them﴾, which was abrogated by His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And judge between them by what Allah has revealed﴾." As for when a Muslim and a dhimmi bring their dispute to us, it is obligatory for us to judge between them, and there is no difference of opinion on this, because it is not permissible for a Muslim to submit to the judgment of the people of the dhimmah.

His saying: ﴿And if you judge, judge between them with justice﴾, that is, with fairness; ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly﴾, that is, those who are fair. We have related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Those who act justly will be with Allah upon pulpits of light."[[Related by Muslim in al-Imarah, chapter on the virtue of the just ruler, no. (1827): 3 / 1458; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 10 / 63-64.]]

قَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَكَيْفَ يُحَكِّمُونَكَ وَعِنْدَهُمُ التَّوْرَاةُ﴾ هَذَا تَعْجِيبٌ لِلنَّبِيِّ ﷺ، وَفِيهِ اخْتِصَارٌ، أَيْ: كَيْفَ يَجْعَلُونَكَ حَكَمًا بَيْنَهُمْ فَيَرْضَوْنَ بِحُكْمِكَ وَعِنْدَهُمُ التَّوْرَاةُ؟ ﴿فِيهَا حُكْمُ اللَّهِ﴾ وَهُوَ الرَّجْمُ، ﴿ثُمَّ يَتَوَلَّوْنَ مِنْ بَعْدِ ذَلِكَ وَمَا أُولَئِكَ بِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ أَيْ بِمُصَدِّقِينَ لَكَ.

قَوْلُهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: ﴿إِنَّا أَنْزَلْنَا التَّوْرَاةَ فِيهَا هُدًى وَنُورٌ يَحْكُمُ بِهَا النَّبِيُّونَ الَّذِينَ أَسْلَمُوا﴾ أَيْ: أَسْلَمُوا وَانْقَادُوا [لِأَمْرِ] [[في "ب": (لحكم).]] اللَّهِ تَعَالَى، كَمَا أَخْبَرَ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: "إِذْ قَالَ لَهُ رَبُّهُ أَسْلِمْ قَالَ أَسْلَمْتُ لِرَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ" (سُورَةُ الْبَقَرَةِ، ١٣١)، وَكَمَا قَالَ: "وَلَهُ أَسْلَمَ مَنْ فِي السَّمَوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ" (سُورَةُ آلِ عِمْرَانَ، ٨٣)، وَأَرَادَ بِهِمُ النَّبِيِّينَ الَّذِينَ بُعِثُوا مِنْ بَعْدِ مُوسَى عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ لِيَحْكُمُوا بِمَا فِي التَّوْرَاةِ، وَقَدْ أَسْلَمُوا لِحُكْمِ التَّوْرَاةِ وَحَكَمُوا بِهَا، فَإِنَّ مِنَ النَّبِيِّينَ مَنْ لَمْ يُؤْمَرْ بِحُكْمِ التَّوْرَاةِ مِنْهُمْ عِيسَى عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ، قَالَ اللَّهُ سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى: ﴿لِكُلٍّ جَعَلْنَا مِنْكُمْ شِرْعَةً وَمِنْهَاجًا﴾ (سُورَةُ الْمَائِدَةِ، ٤٨).

وَقَالَ الْحَسَنُ وَالسُّدِّيُّ: أَرَادَ بِهِ مُحَمَّدًا ﷺ حَكَمَ عَلَى الْيَهُودِ بِالرَّجْمِ، ذُكِرَ بِلَفْظِ الْجَمْعِ كَمَا قَالَ: "إِنَّ إِبْرَاهِيمَ كَانَ أُمَّةً قَانِتًا" (سُورَةُ النَّحْلِ، ١٢٠).

وَقَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿لِلَّذِينَ هَادُوا﴾ فِيهِ تَقْدِيمٌ وَتَأْخِيرٌ، تَقْدِيرُهُ: فِيهَا هُدًى وَنُورٌ لِلَّذِينَ هَادُوا. ثُمَّ قَالَ: يَحْكُمُ بِهَا النَّبِيُّونَ الَّذِينَ أَسْلَمُوا وَالرَّبَّانِيُّونَ، وَقِيلَ: هُوَ عَلَى مَوْضِعِهِ، وَمَعْنَاهُ: يَحْكُمُ بِهَا النَّبِيُّونَ الَّذِينَ أَسْلَمُوا عَلَى الَّذِينَ هَادُوا، كَمَا قَالَ: "وَإِنْ أَسَأْتُمْ فَلَهَا" (سُورَةُ الْإِسْرَاءِ، ٧) أَيْ: فَعَلَيْهَا، وَقَالَ: "أُولَئِكَ لَهُمُ اللَّعْنَةُ" (سُورَةُ الرَّعْدِ، ٢٥) أَيْ: عَلَيْهِمْ، وَقِيلَ: فِيهِ حَذْفٌ، كَأَنَّهُ قَالَ: لِلَّذِينَ هَادُوا وَعَلَى الَّذِينَ هَادُوا فَحَذَفَ أَحَدَهُمَا اخْتِصَارًا.

﴿وَالرَّبَّانِيُّونَ وَالْأَحْبَارُ﴾ يَعْنِي الْعُلَمَاءَ: وَاحِدُهُمْ حَبْرٌ، وَحِبْرٌ بِفَتْحِ الْحَاءِ وَكَسْرِهَا، وَالْكَسْرُ أَفْصَحُ، وَهُوَ الْعَالِمُ الْمُحْكِمُ لِلشَّيْءِ. قَالَ الْكِسَائِيُّ وَأَبُو عُبَيْدٍ: هُوَ مِنَ الْحِبْرِ الَّذِي يُكْتَبُ بِهِ. وَقَالَ قُطْرُبٌ: هُوَ مِنَ الْحِبْرِ الَّذِي هُوَ بِمَعْنَى الْجَمَالِ بِفَتْحِ الْحَاءِ وَكَسْرِهَا، وَفِي الْحَدِيثِ: "يُخْرَجُ مِنَ النَّارِ رَجُلٌ قَدْ ذَهَبَ حَبْرُهُ وَسَبْرُهُ" [[ذكره الزمخشري في الفائق: ١ / ٢٥١، وابن الأثير في النهاية: ١ / ٣٢٧.]] أَيْ: حُسْنُهُ وَهَيْئَتُهُ، وَمِنْهُ التَّحْبِيرُ وَهُوَ التَّحْسِينُ، فَسُمِّيَ الْعَالِمُ حِبْرًا لِمَا عَلَيْهِ مِنْ جَمَالِ الْعِلْمِ وَبَهَائِهِ. وَقِيلَ: الرَّبَّانِيُّونَ هَاهُنَا مِنَ النَّصَارَى، وَالْأَحْبَارُ مِنَ الْيَهُودِ، وَقِيلَ: كِلَاهُمَا مِنَ الْيَهُودِ.

قَوْلُهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: ﴿بِمَا اسْتُحْفِظُوا مِنْ كِتَابِ اللَّهِ﴾ أَيِ: اسْتُودِعُوا مِنْ كِتَابِ اللَّهِ، ﴿وَكَانُوا عَلَيْهِ شُهَدَاءَ﴾ أَنَّهُ كَذَلِكَ.

﴿فَلَا تَخْشَوُا النَّاسَ وَاخْشَوْنِ وَلَا تَشْتَرُوا بِآيَاتِي ثَمَنًا قَلِيلًا وَمَنْ لَمْ يَحْكُمْ بِمَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْكَافِرُونَ﴾ قَالَ قَتَادَةُ وَالضَّحَّاكُ: نَزَلَتْ هَذِهِ الْآيَاتُ الثَّلَاثُ فِي الْيَهُودِ دُونَ مَنْ أَسَاءَ مِنْ هَذِهِ الْأُمَّةِ. وَرُوِيَ عَنِ الْبَرَاءِ بْنِ عَازِبٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ فِي قَوْلِهِ: ﴿وَمَنْ لَمْ يَحْكُمْ بِمَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْكَافِرُونَ﴾ وَالظَّالِمُونَ وَالْفَاسِقُونَ كُلُّهَا فِي الْكَافِرِينَ. وَقِيلَ: هِيَ عَلَى النَّاسِ كُلِّهِمْ.

وَقَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ [[أخرجه الحاكم في المستدرك: ٢ / ٣١٣ وصححه على شرط الشيخين.]] وَطَاوُوسٌ: لَيْسَ بِكُفْرٍ يَنْقُلُ عَنِ الْمِلَّةِ، بَلْ إِذَا فَعَلَهُ فَهُوَ بِهِ [كَافِرٌ] [[في "ب": (كفر).]] وَلَيْسَ كَمَنْ كَفَرَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ.

قَالَ عَطَاءٌ: هُوَ كُفْرٌ دُونَ كُفْرٍ، وَظُلْمٌ دُونَ ظُلْمٍ، وَفِسْقٌ دُونَ فِسْقٍ. وَقَالَ عِكْرِمَةُ: مَعْنَاهُ: وَمَنْ لَمْ يَحْكُمْ بِمَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ جَاحِدًا بِهِ فَقَدْ كَفَرَ، وَمَنْ أَقَرَّ بِهِ وَلَمْ يَحْكُمْ بِهِ فَهُوَ ظَالِمٌ فَاسِقٌ.

وَسُئِلَ عَبْدُ الْعَزِيزِ بْنُ يَحْيَى الْكِنَانِيُّ عَنْ هَذِهِ الْآيَاتِ، فَقَالَ: إِنَّهَا تَقَعُ عَلَى جَمِيعِ مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ لَا عَلَى بَعْضِهِ، فَكُلُّ مَنْ لَمْ يَحْكُمْ بِجَمِيعِ مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ فَهُوَ كَافِرٌ ظَالِمٌ فَاسِقٌ. فَأَمَّا مَنْ حَكَمَ بِمَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ مِنَ التَّوْحِيدِ وَتَرْكِ الشِّرْكِ، ثُمَّ لَمْ يَحْكُمْ [بِجَمِيعِ] [[في "ب": (ببعض).]] مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ مِنَ الشَّرَائِعِ لَمْ يَسْتَوْجِبْ حُكْمَ هَذِهِ الْآيَاتِ. وَقَالَ الْعُلَمَاءُ: هَذَا إِذَا رَدَّ نَصَّ حُكْمِ اللَّهِ عِيَانًا عَمْدًا، فَأَمَّا مَنْ خَفِيَ عَلَيْهِ أَوْ أَخْطَأَ فِي تَأْوِيلٍ فَلَا [[للشيخ أحمد محمد شاكر وأخيه محمود شاكر تعليق على هذه الآثار، في عمدة التفسير وفي تفسير الطبري، عند تفسير هذه الآية، ننقله هنا بتمامه: قال الشيخ أحمد شاكر في عمدة التفسير: ٤ / ١٥٦-١٥٨ "وهذه الآثار - عن ابن عباس وغيره - مما يلعب به المضللون في عصرنا هذا، من المنتسبين للعلم، ومن غيرهم من الجرآء على الدين: يجعلونها عذرا أو إباحة للقوانين الوثنية الموضوعة، التي ضربت على بلاد الإسلام. وهناك أثر عن أبي مجلز، في جدال الإباضية إياه، فيما كان يصنع بعض الأمراء من الجور، فيحكمون في بعض قضائهم بما يخالف الشريعة، عمدا إلى الهوى، أو جهلا بالحكم. والخوارج، من مذهبهم أن مرتكب الكبيرة كافر، فهم يجادلون يريدون من أبي مجلز أن يوافقهم على ما يرون من كفر هؤلاء الأمراء، ليكون ذلك عذرا لهم فيما يرون من الخروج عليهم بالسيف. وهذان الأثران رواهما الطبري: ١٢٠٢٥، ١٢٠٢٦. وكتب عليهما أخي السيد محمود محمد شاكر تعليقا نفيسا جدا، قويا صريحا. فرأيت أن أثبت هنا نص أولى روايتي الطبري، ثم تعليق أخي على الروايتين. فروى الطبري: ١٢٠٢٥، عن عمران بن حدير: قال: "أتى أبا مجلز ناس من بني عمرو بن سدوس، فقالوا: يا أبا مجلز، أرأيت قول الله "ومن لم يحكم بما أنزل الله فأولئك هم الكافرون" أحق هو؟ قال: نعم، قال: "ومن لم يحكم بما أنزل الله فأولئك هم الظالمون" أحق هو؟ قال: نعم، قالوا: "ومن لم يحكم بما أنزل فأولئك هم الفاسقون" أحق هو؟ قال: نعم. قال: فقالوا: يا أبا مجلز، فيحكم هؤلاء بما أنزل الله؟ قال: هو دينهم الذي يدينون به، وبه يقولون، وإليه يدعون. فإن هم تركوا شيئا منه عرفوا أنهم قد أصابوا ذنبا، فقالوا: لا والله، ولكنك تفرق! قال: أنتم أولى بهذا مني! لا أرى، وإنكم ترون هذا ولا تحرجون! ولكنها أنزلت في اليهود والنصارى وأهل الشرك، أو نحوا من هذا". ثم روى الطبري: ١٢٠٢٦ نحو معناه. وإسناداه صحيحان. فكتب أخي السيد محمود، بمناسبة هذين الأثرين ما نصه: اللهم إني أبرأ إليك من الضلالة. وبعد، فإن أهل الريب والفتن ممن تصدروا للكلام في زماننا هذا، قد تلمس المعذرة لأهل السلطان في ترك الحكم بما أنزل الله، وفي القضاء في الدماء والأعراض والأموال بغير شريعة الله التي أنزلها في كتابه. وفي اتخاذهم قانون أهل الكفر شريعة في بلاد الإسلام. فلما وقف على هذين الخبرين، اتخذهما رأيا يرى به صواب القضاء في الأموال والأعراض والدماء بغير ما أنزل الله، وأن مخالفة شريعة الله في القضاء العام لا تكفر الراضي بها، والعامل عليها. والناظر في هذين الخبرين لا محيص له عن معرفة السائل والمسئول، فأبو مجلز (لاحق بن حميد الشيباني السدوسي) تابعي ثقة، وكان يحب عليا رضي الله عنه. وكان قوم أبي مجلز، وهم بنو شيبان، من شيعة علي يوم الجمل وصفين. فلما كان أمر الحكمين يوم صفين، واعتزلت الخوارج، كان فيمن خرج على علي رضي الله عنه، طائفة من بني شيبان، ومن بني سدوس بن شيبان بن ذهل. وهؤلاء الذين سألوا أبا مجلز، ناس من بني عمرو بن سدوس (كما في الأثر: ١٢٠٢٥)، وهم نفر من الإباضية (كما في الأثر: ١٢٠٢٦)، والإباضية من جماعة الخوارج الحرورية، هم أصحاب عبد الله بن إباض التميمي، وهم يقولون بمقالة سائر الخوارج في التحكيم، وفي تكفير علي رضي الله عنه إذ حكم الحكمين، وأن عليا لم يحكم بما أنزل الله، في أمر التحكيم. ثم إن عبد الله بن إباض قال: إن من خالف الخوارج كافر ليس بمشرك، فخالف أصحابه، وأقام الخوارج على أن أحكام المشركين تجري على من خالفهم. ثم افترقت الإباضية بعد عبد الله بن إباض الإمام افتراقا لا ندري معه - في أمر هذين الخبرين - من أي الفرق كان هؤلاء السائلون، بيد أن الإباضية كلها يقول: إن دور مخالفيهم دور توحيد، إلا معسكر السلطان فإنه دار كفر عندهم. ثم قالوا أيضا: إن جميع ما افترض الله سبحانه على خلقه إيمان، وأن كل كبيرة فهي كفر نعمة، لا كفر شرك، وأن مرتكبي الكبائر في النار خالدون مخلدون فيها. ومن البين أن الذين سألوا أبا مجلز من الإباضية، إنما كانوا يريدون أن يلزموه الحجة في تكفير الأمراء، لأنهم في معسكر السلطان، ولأنهم ربما عصوا أو ارتكبوا بعض ما نهاهم الله عن ارتكابه. ولذلك قال لهم في الخبر الأول (رقم: ١٢٠٢٥): "فإن هم تركوا شيئا منه عرفوا أنهم قد أصابوا ذنبا"، وقال لهم في الخبر الثاني: "إنهم يعملون بما يعملون أنه ذنب". وإذن، فلم يكن سؤالهم عما احتج به مبتدعة زماننا، من القضاء في الأموال والأعراض والدماء بقانون مخالف لشريعة أهل الإسلام، ولا في إصدار قانون ملزم لأهل الإسلام، بالاحتكام إلى حكم غير حكم الله في كتابه وعلى لسان نبيه ﷺ. فهذا الفعل إعراض عن حكم الله، ورغبة عن دينه، وإيثار لأحكام أهل الكفر على حكم الله سبحانه وتعالى، وهذا كفر لا يشك أحد من أهل القبلة على اختلافهم في تكفير القائل والداعي إليه. والذي نحن فيه اليوم، هو هجر لأحكام الله عامة بلا استثناء، وإيثار أحكام غير حكمه في كتابه وسنة نبيه، وتعطيل لكل ما في شريعة الله، بل بلغ الأمر مبلغ الاحتجاج على تفضيل أحكام القانون الموضوع، على أحكام الله المنزلة، وادعاء المحتجين لذلك بأن أحكام الشريعة إنما نزلت لزمان غير زماننا، ولعلل وأسباب انقضت، فسقطت الأحكام كلها بانقضائها. فأين هذا مما بيناه من حديث أبي مجلز والنفر من الإباضية من بني عمرو بن سدوس!! ولو كان الأمر على ما ظنوا في خبر أبي مجلز، أنهم أرادوا مخالفة السلطان في حكم من أحكام الشريعة. فإنه لم يحدث في تاريخ الإسلام أن سن حاكم حكما وجعله شريعة ملزمة للقضاء بها. هذه واحدة. وأخرى، أن الحاكم الذي حكم في قضية بعينها بغير حكم الله فيها، فإنه إما أن يكون حكم بها وهو جاهل، فهذا أمره أمر الجاهل بالشريعة. وإما أن يكون حكم بها هوى ومعصية، فهذا ذنب تناله التوبة، وتلحقه المغفرة. وإما أن يكون حكم بها متأولا حكما خالف به سائر العلماء، فهذا حكمه حكم كل متأول يستمد تأويله من الإقرار بنص الكتاب، وسنة رسول الله. وأما أن يكون كان في زمن أبي مجلز أو قبله أو بعده حاكم حكم بقضاء في أمر، جاحدا لحكم من أحكام الشريعة، أو مؤثرا لأحكام أهل الكفر على أحكام أهل الإسلام، فذلك لم يكن قط. فلا يمكن صرف كلام أبي مجلز والإباضيين إليه. فمن احتج بهذين الأثرين وغيرهما في غير بابهما، وصرفهما إلى غير معناهما، رغبة في نصرة سلطان، أو احتيالا على تسويغ الحكم بغير ما أنزل الله وفرض على عباده، فحكمه في الشريعة حكم الجاحد لحكم من أحكام الله: أن يستتاب، فإن أصر وكابر وجاحد حكم الله، ورضي بتبديل الأحكام = فحكم الكافر المصر على كفره معروف لأهل هذا الدين. وكتبه محمود محمد شاكر".]].

قَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَكَيْفَ يُحَكِّمُونَكَ وَعِنْدَهُمُ التَّوْرَاةُ﴾ هَذَا تَعْجِيبٌ لِلنَّبِيِّ ﷺ، وَفِيهِ اخْتِصَارٌ، أَيْ: كَيْفَ يَجْعَلُونَكَ حَكَمًا بَيْنَهُمْ فَيَرْضَوْنَ بِحُكْمِكَ وَعِنْدَهُمُ التَّوْرَاةُ؟ ﴿فِيهَا حُكْمُ اللَّهِ﴾ وَهُوَ الرَّجْمُ، ﴿ثُمَّ يَتَوَلَّوْنَ مِنْ بَعْدِ ذَلِكَ وَمَا أُولَئِكَ بِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ أَيْ بِمُصَدِّقِينَ لَكَ.

قَوْلُهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: ﴿إِنَّا أَنْزَلْنَا التَّوْرَاةَ فِيهَا هُدًى وَنُورٌ يَحْكُمُ بِهَا النَّبِيُّونَ الَّذِينَ أَسْلَمُوا﴾ أَيْ: أَسْلَمُوا وَانْقَادُوا [لِأَمْرِ] [[في "ب": (لحكم).]] اللَّهِ تَعَالَى، كَمَا أَخْبَرَ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: "إِذْ قَالَ لَهُ رَبُّهُ أَسْلِمْ قَالَ أَسْلَمْتُ لِرَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ" (سُورَةُ الْبَقَرَةِ، ١٣١)، وَكَمَا قَالَ: "وَلَهُ أَسْلَمَ مَنْ فِي السَّمَوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ" (سُورَةُ آلِ عِمْرَانَ، ٨٣)، وَأَرَادَ بِهِمُ النَّبِيِّينَ الَّذِينَ بُعِثُوا مِنْ بَعْدِ مُوسَى عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ لِيَحْكُمُوا بِمَا فِي التَّوْرَاةِ، وَقَدْ أَسْلَمُوا لِحُكْمِ التَّوْرَاةِ وَحَكَمُوا بِهَا، فَإِنَّ مِنَ النَّبِيِّينَ مَنْ لَمْ يُؤْمَرْ بِحُكْمِ التَّوْرَاةِ مِنْهُمْ عِيسَى عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ، قَالَ اللَّهُ سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى: ﴿لِكُلٍّ جَعَلْنَا مِنْكُمْ شِرْعَةً وَمِنْهَاجًا﴾ (سُورَةُ الْمَائِدَةِ، ٤٨).

وَقَالَ الْحَسَنُ وَالسُّدِّيُّ: أَرَادَ بِهِ مُحَمَّدًا ﷺ حَكَمَ عَلَى الْيَهُودِ بِالرَّجْمِ، ذُكِرَ بِلَفْظِ الْجَمْعِ كَمَا قَالَ: "إِنَّ إِبْرَاهِيمَ كَانَ أُمَّةً قَانِتًا" (سُورَةُ النَّحْلِ، ١٢٠).

وَقَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿لِلَّذِينَ هَادُوا﴾ فِيهِ تَقْدِيمٌ وَتَأْخِيرٌ، تَقْدِيرُهُ: فِيهَا هُدًى وَنُورٌ لِلَّذِينَ هَادُوا. ثُمَّ قَالَ: يَحْكُمُ بِهَا النَّبِيُّونَ الَّذِينَ أَسْلَمُوا وَالرَّبَّانِيُّونَ، وَقِيلَ: هُوَ عَلَى مَوْضِعِهِ، وَمَعْنَاهُ: يَحْكُمُ بِهَا النَّبِيُّونَ الَّذِينَ أَسْلَمُوا عَلَى الَّذِينَ هَادُوا، كَمَا قَالَ: "وَإِنْ أَسَأْتُمْ فَلَهَا" (سُورَةُ الْإِسْرَاءِ، ٧) أَيْ: فَعَلَيْهَا، وَقَالَ: "أُولَئِكَ لَهُمُ اللَّعْنَةُ" (سُورَةُ الرَّعْدِ، ٢٥) أَيْ: عَلَيْهِمْ، وَقِيلَ: فِيهِ حَذْفٌ، كَأَنَّهُ قَالَ: لِلَّذِينَ هَادُوا وَعَلَى الَّذِينَ هَادُوا فَحَذَفَ أَحَدَهُمَا اخْتِصَارًا.

﴿وَالرَّبَّانِيُّونَ وَالْأَحْبَارُ﴾ يَعْنِي الْعُلَمَاءَ: وَاحِدُهُمْ حَبْرٌ، وَحِبْرٌ بِفَتْحِ الْحَاءِ وَكَسْرِهَا، وَالْكَسْرُ أَفْصَحُ، وَهُوَ الْعَالِمُ الْمُحْكِمُ لِلشَّيْءِ. قَالَ الْكِسَائِيُّ وَأَبُو عُبَيْدٍ: هُوَ مِنَ الْحِبْرِ الَّذِي يُكْتَبُ بِهِ. وَقَالَ قُطْرُبٌ: هُوَ مِنَ الْحِبْرِ الَّذِي هُوَ بِمَعْنَى الْجَمَالِ بِفَتْحِ الْحَاءِ وَكَسْرِهَا، وَفِي الْحَدِيثِ: "يُخْرَجُ مِنَ النَّارِ رَجُلٌ قَدْ ذَهَبَ حَبْرُهُ وَسَبْرُهُ" [[ذكره الزمخشري في الفائق: ١ / ٢٥١، وابن الأثير في النهاية: ١ / ٣٢٧.]] أَيْ: حُسْنُهُ وَهَيْئَتُهُ، وَمِنْهُ التَّحْبِيرُ وَهُوَ التَّحْسِينُ، فَسُمِّيَ الْعَالِمُ حِبْرًا لِمَا عَلَيْهِ مِنْ جَمَالِ الْعِلْمِ وَبَهَائِهِ. وَقِيلَ: الرَّبَّانِيُّونَ هَاهُنَا مِنَ النَّصَارَى، وَالْأَحْبَارُ مِنَ الْيَهُودِ، وَقِيلَ: كِلَاهُمَا مِنَ الْيَهُودِ.

قَوْلُهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: ﴿بِمَا اسْتُحْفِظُوا مِنْ كِتَابِ اللَّهِ﴾ أَيِ: اسْتُودِعُوا مِنْ كِتَابِ اللَّهِ، ﴿وَكَانُوا عَلَيْهِ شُهَدَاءَ﴾ أَنَّهُ كَذَلِكَ.

﴿فَلَا تَخْشَوُا النَّاسَ وَاخْشَوْنِ وَلَا تَشْتَرُوا بِآيَاتِي ثَمَنًا قَلِيلًا وَمَنْ لَمْ يَحْكُمْ بِمَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْكَافِرُونَ﴾ قَالَ قَتَادَةُ وَالضَّحَّاكُ: نَزَلَتْ هَذِهِ الْآيَاتُ الثَّلَاثُ فِي الْيَهُودِ دُونَ مَنْ أَسَاءَ مِنْ هَذِهِ الْأُمَّةِ. وَرُوِيَ عَنِ الْبَرَاءِ بْنِ عَازِبٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ فِي قَوْلِهِ: ﴿وَمَنْ لَمْ يَحْكُمْ بِمَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْكَافِرُونَ﴾ وَالظَّالِمُونَ وَالْفَاسِقُونَ كُلُّهَا فِي الْكَافِرِينَ. وَقِيلَ: هِيَ عَلَى النَّاسِ كُلِّهِمْ.

وَقَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ [[أخرجه الحاكم في المستدرك: ٢ / ٣١٣ وصححه على شرط الشيخين.]] وَطَاوُوسٌ: لَيْسَ بِكُفْرٍ يَنْقُلُ عَنِ الْمِلَّةِ، بَلْ إِذَا فَعَلَهُ فَهُوَ بِهِ [كَافِرٌ] [[في "ب": (كفر).]] وَلَيْسَ كَمَنْ كَفَرَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ.

قَالَ عَطَاءٌ: هُوَ كُفْرٌ دُونَ كُفْرٍ، وَظُلْمٌ دُونَ ظُلْمٍ، وَفِسْقٌ دُونَ فِسْقٍ. وَقَالَ عِكْرِمَةُ: مَعْنَاهُ: وَمَنْ لَمْ يَحْكُمْ بِمَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ جَاحِدًا بِهِ فَقَدْ كَفَرَ، وَمَنْ أَقَرَّ بِهِ وَلَمْ يَحْكُمْ بِهِ فَهُوَ ظَالِمٌ فَاسِقٌ.

وَسُئِلَ عَبْدُ الْعَزِيزِ بْنُ يَحْيَى الْكِنَانِيُّ عَنْ هَذِهِ الْآيَاتِ، فَقَالَ: إِنَّهَا تَقَعُ عَلَى جَمِيعِ مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ لَا عَلَى بَعْضِهِ، فَكُلُّ مَنْ لَمْ يَحْكُمْ بِجَمِيعِ مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ فَهُوَ كَافِرٌ ظَالِمٌ فَاسِقٌ. فَأَمَّا مَنْ حَكَمَ بِمَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ مِنَ التَّوْحِيدِ وَتَرْكِ الشِّرْكِ، ثُمَّ لَمْ يَحْكُمْ [بِجَمِيعِ] [[في "ب": (ببعض).]] مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ مِنَ الشَّرَائِعِ لَمْ يَسْتَوْجِبْ حُكْمَ هَذِهِ الْآيَاتِ. وَقَالَ الْعُلَمَاءُ: هَذَا إِذَا رَدَّ نَصَّ حُكْمِ اللَّهِ عِيَانًا عَمْدًا، فَأَمَّا مَنْ خَفِيَ عَلَيْهِ أَوْ أَخْطَأَ فِي تَأْوِيلٍ فَلَا [[للشيخ أحمد محمد شاكر وأخيه محمود شاكر تعليق على هذه الآثار، في عمدة التفسير وفي تفسير الطبري، عند تفسير هذه الآية، ننقله هنا بتمامه: قال الشيخ أحمد شاكر في عمدة التفسير: ٤ / ١٥٦-١٥٨ "وهذه الآثار - عن ابن عباس وغيره - مما يلعب به المضللون في عصرنا هذا، من المنتسبين للعلم، ومن غيرهم من الجرآء على الدين: يجعلونها عذرا أو إباحة للقوانين الوثنية الموضوعة، التي ضربت على بلاد الإسلام. وهناك أثر عن أبي مجلز، في جدال الإباضية إياه، فيما كان يصنع بعض الأمراء من الجور، فيحكمون في بعض قضائهم بما يخالف الشريعة، عمدا إلى الهوى، أو جهلا بالحكم. والخوارج، من مذهبهم أن مرتكب الكبيرة كافر، فهم يجادلون يريدون من أبي مجلز أن يوافقهم على ما يرون من كفر هؤلاء الأمراء، ليكون ذلك عذرا لهم فيما يرون من الخروج عليهم بالسيف. وهذان الأثران رواهما الطبري: ١٢٠٢٥، ١٢٠٢٦. وكتب عليهما أخي السيد محمود محمد شاكر تعليقا نفيسا جدا، قويا صريحا. فرأيت أن أثبت هنا نص أولى روايتي الطبري، ثم تعليق أخي على الروايتين. فروى الطبري: ١٢٠٢٥، عن عمران بن حدير: قال: "أتى أبا مجلز ناس من بني عمرو بن سدوس، فقالوا: يا أبا مجلز، أرأيت قول الله "ومن لم يحكم بما أنزل الله فأولئك هم الكافرون" أحق هو؟ قال: نعم، قال: "ومن لم يحكم بما أنزل الله فأولئك هم الظالمون" أحق هو؟ قال: نعم، قالوا: "ومن لم يحكم بما أنزل فأولئك هم الفاسقون" أحق هو؟ قال: نعم. قال: فقالوا: يا أبا مجلز، فيحكم هؤلاء بما أنزل الله؟ قال: هو دينهم الذي يدينون به، وبه يقولون، وإليه يدعون. فإن هم تركوا شيئا منه عرفوا أنهم قد أصابوا ذنبا، فقالوا: لا والله، ولكنك تفرق! قال: أنتم أولى بهذا مني! لا أرى، وإنكم ترون هذا ولا تحرجون! ولكنها أنزلت في اليهود والنصارى وأهل الشرك، أو نحوا من هذا". ثم روى الطبري: ١٢٠٢٦ نحو معناه. وإسناداه صحيحان. فكتب أخي السيد محمود، بمناسبة هذين الأثرين ما نصه: اللهم إني أبرأ إليك من الضلالة. وبعد، فإن أهل الريب والفتن ممن تصدروا للكلام في زماننا هذا، قد تلمس المعذرة لأهل السلطان في ترك الحكم بما أنزل الله، وفي القضاء في الدماء والأعراض والأموال بغير شريعة الله التي أنزلها في كتابه. وفي اتخاذهم قانون أهل الكفر شريعة في بلاد الإسلام. فلما وقف على هذين الخبرين، اتخذهما رأيا يرى به صواب القضاء في الأموال والأعراض والدماء بغير ما أنزل الله، وأن مخالفة شريعة الله في القضاء العام لا تكفر الراضي بها، والعامل عليها. والناظر في هذين الخبرين لا محيص له عن معرفة السائل والمسئول، فأبو مجلز (لاحق بن حميد الشيباني السدوسي) تابعي ثقة، وكان يحب عليا رضي الله عنه. وكان قوم أبي مجلز، وهم بنو شيبان، من شيعة علي يوم الجمل وصفين. فلما كان أمر الحكمين يوم صفين، واعتزلت الخوارج، كان فيمن خرج على علي رضي الله عنه، طائفة من بني شيبان، ومن بني سدوس بن شيبان بن ذهل. وهؤلاء الذين سألوا أبا مجلز، ناس من بني عمرو بن سدوس (كما في الأثر: ١٢٠٢٥)، وهم نفر من الإباضية (كما في الأثر: ١٢٠٢٦)، والإباضية من جماعة الخوارج الحرورية، هم أصحاب عبد الله بن إباض التميمي، وهم يقولون بمقالة سائر الخوارج في التحكيم، وفي تكفير علي رضي الله عنه إذ حكم الحكمين، وأن عليا لم يحكم بما أنزل الله، في أمر التحكيم. ثم إن عبد الله بن إباض قال: إن من خالف الخوارج كافر ليس بمشرك، فخالف أصحابه، وأقام الخوارج على أن أحكام المشركين تجري على من خالفهم. ثم افترقت الإباضية بعد عبد الله بن إباض الإمام افتراقا لا ندري معه - في أمر هذين الخبرين - من أي الفرق كان هؤلاء السائلون، بيد أن الإباضية كلها يقول: إن دور مخالفيهم دور توحيد، إلا معسكر السلطان فإنه دار كفر عندهم. ثم قالوا أيضا: إن جميع ما افترض الله سبحانه على خلقه إيمان، وأن كل كبيرة فهي كفر نعمة، لا كفر شرك، وأن مرتكبي الكبائر في النار خالدون مخلدون فيها. ومن البين أن الذين سألوا أبا مجلز من الإباضية، إنما كانوا يريدون أن يلزموه الحجة في تكفير الأمراء، لأنهم في معسكر السلطان، ولأنهم ربما عصوا أو ارتكبوا بعض ما نهاهم الله عن ارتكابه. ولذلك قال لهم في الخبر الأول (رقم: ١٢٠٢٥): "فإن هم تركوا شيئا منه عرفوا أنهم قد أصابوا ذنبا"، وقال لهم في الخبر الثاني: "إنهم يعملون بما يعملون أنه ذنب". وإذن، فلم يكن سؤالهم عما احتج به مبتدعة زماننا، من القضاء في الأموال والأعراض والدماء بقانون مخالف لشريعة أهل الإسلام، ولا في إصدار قانون ملزم لأهل الإسلام، بالاحتكام إلى حكم غير حكم الله في كتابه وعلى لسان نبيه ﷺ. فهذا الفعل إعراض عن حكم الله، ورغبة عن دينه، وإيثار لأحكام أهل الكفر على حكم الله سبحانه وتعالى، وهذا كفر لا يشك أحد من أهل القبلة على اختلافهم في تكفير القائل والداعي إليه. والذي نحن فيه اليوم، هو هجر لأحكام الله عامة بلا استثناء، وإيثار أحكام غير حكمه في كتابه وسنة نبيه، وتعطيل لكل ما في شريعة الله، بل بلغ الأمر مبلغ الاحتجاج على تفضيل أحكام القانون الموضوع، على أحكام الله المنزلة، وادعاء المحتجين لذلك بأن أحكام الشريعة إنما نزلت لزمان غير زماننا، ولعلل وأسباب انقضت، فسقطت الأحكام كلها بانقضائها. فأين هذا مما بيناه من حديث أبي مجلز والنفر من الإباضية من بني عمرو بن سدوس!! ولو كان الأمر على ما ظنوا في خبر أبي مجلز، أنهم أرادوا مخالفة السلطان في حكم من أحكام الشريعة. فإنه لم يحدث في تاريخ الإسلام أن سن حاكم حكما وجعله شريعة ملزمة للقضاء بها. هذه واحدة. وأخرى، أن الحاكم الذي حكم في قضية بعينها بغير حكم الله فيها، فإنه إما أن يكون حكم بها وهو جاهل، فهذا أمره أمر الجاهل بالشريعة. وإما أن يكون حكم بها هوى ومعصية، فهذا ذنب تناله التوبة، وتلحقه المغفرة. وإما أن يكون حكم بها متأولا حكما خالف به سائر العلماء، فهذا حكمه حكم كل متأول يستمد تأويله من الإقرار بنص الكتاب، وسنة رسول الله. وأما أن يكون كان في زمن أبي مجلز أو قبله أو بعده حاكم حكم بقضاء في أمر، جاحدا لحكم من أحكام الشريعة، أو مؤثرا لأحكام أهل الكفر على أحكام أهل الإسلام، فذلك لم يكن قط. فلا يمكن صرف كلام أبي مجلز والإباضيين إليه. فمن احتج بهذين الأثرين وغيرهما في غير بابهما، وصرفهما إلى غير معناهما، رغبة في نصرة سلطان، أو احتيالا على تسويغ الحكم بغير ما أنزل الله وفرض على عباده، فحكمه في الشريعة حكم الجاحد لحكم من أحكام الله: أن يستتاب، فإن أصر وكابر وجاحد حكم الله، ورضي بتبديل الأحكام = فحكم الكافر المصر على كفره معروف لأهل هذا الدين. وكتبه محمود محمد شاكر".]].

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 5, verse 45:**

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And We prescribed for them therein﴾, that is: We made it obligatory upon the Children of Israel in the Torah, ﴿that the life is for the life﴾, meaning: the killer's life is to be taken for the life of the one killed, as retribution (wafa'an) by which he is killed, ﴿and the eye for the eye﴾ to be gouged out by it, ﴿and the nose for the nose﴾ to be slit off by it, ﴿and the ear for the ear﴾ to be cut off by it. Ibn Abbas said: Allah, Exalted is He, informed of His ruling in the Torah, which is: "the life for the life," and so on to its end. "So what is the matter with them that they oppose it, killing two souls for one soul and gouging out two eyes for one eye?" Nafi' lightened al-udhn (الأذن) throughout the whole Qur'an, while the others pronounced it al-udhun (الأُذُنَ) with a damma. ﴿And the tooth for the tooth﴾ to be pulled out by it, and the rest of the limbs are analogous to these in retaliation (qisas, the law of equal retribution). ﴿And for wounds, retaliation﴾. This is a generalization after a specification, because He mentioned the eye, the nose, the ear and the tooth, and then said: ﴿And for wounds, retaliation﴾, that is, in what it is possible to exact retaliation for, such as the hand, the foot, the tongue and the like. As for what retaliation cannot be exacted for, such as breaking a bone or wounding flesh in the manner of a jaifah (جائفة, a wound penetrating to the interior of the body) and the like, there is no retaliation in it, because it is not possible to determine its limit. Al-Kisa'i read "wal-ayn" (وَالْعَيْنُ) and what follows it in the nominative (raf'), and Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir, Abu Ja'far and Abu Amr read "wal-judhuh" (وَالْجُرُوحُ) in the nominative only, while the others read all of them in the accusative (nasb), like "the life."

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿So whoever gives it in charity﴾, that is, the retaliation, ﴿it is an expiation for him﴾. It was said: the pronoun in "lahu" (لَهُ, "for him") refers to the one who was wounded and to the guardian of the one who was killed, meaning: it is an expiation for the one who gives it in charity. This is the view of Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As, al-Hasan, al-Sha'bi and Qatadah.

Abu Sa'id Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Shurayhi informed us, saying: Abu Ishaq Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Tha'labi informed us, saying: Abdullah al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Dinawari informed us, saying: Umar ibn al-Khattab informed us, saying: Abdullah ibn al-Fadl informed us, saying: Abu Khaythamah informed us, saying: Jarir related to us from Mughirah, from al-Sha'bi, from Ubadah ibn al-Samit, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever gives something of his body in charity, Allah will expiate for him from his sins to the measure of that."[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in a lengthier form from Abu al-Darda, in the chapter on blood-money, "What has come concerning pardon" (Kitab al-Diyat, Bab ma ja'a fi al-afw): 4/650, and he said: "This is a gharib hadith, and I do not know that Abu al-Safar heard from Abu al-Darda." It was also narrated by Ibn Majah in Kitab al-Diyat, Bab al-afw fi al-qisas, no. (2693): 2/898; by al-Tabari in his Tafsir: 10/368; by Ibn Abi Asim in al-Diyat; and by Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 5/316 and 6/448. Al-Mundhiri mentioned it in al-Targhib wa al-Tarhib: 3/305, from the narration of Imam Ahmad, and said: "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih." And from the narration of Ibn Majah, and said: "Its chain is hasan, were it not for the break (inqita')."]]

A group said: it is an expiation for the one who inflicts the wound and for the killer. That is: if the victim pardons the offender, then his pardon is an expiation for the offender's sin, so that he is not held accountable for it in the Hereafter, just as retaliation is an expiation for him. As for the reward of the one who pardons, it is upon Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿So whoever pardons and makes reconciliation, his reward is upon Allah﴾ [al-Shura: 40]. This was related from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, and it is the view of Ibrahim, Mujahid and Zayd ibn Aslam.

﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, then it is those who are the wrongdoers﴾.

The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 5, verses 46–48:

Allah's words: ﴿And We sent, following in their footsteps﴾, meaning: following in the footsteps of the Prophets who submitted (to Allah), ﴿Jesus, son of Mary, confirming what was before him of the Torah, and We gave him the Gospel, in which﴾

That is, in the Gospel, ﴿was guidance and light, and confirming what was before it of the Torah, and a guidance and admonition for the God-fearing﴾, meaning the Gospel.

﴿Let the People of the Gospel judge by what Allah has revealed in it﴾. Al-A'mash and Hamzah recited "wa-liyahkama" with a kasra on the lam and a fatha on the mim, meaning "so that they may judge" (the lam being a particle of purpose, li-yahkama). The others recited it with a sukun on the lam and a jazm on the mim, as a command. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: Allah commanded the rabbaniyyun (the rabbinical scholars, lit. "those devoted to the Lord") and the ahbar (rabbis) to judge by what is in the Torah, and commanded the qissisun (priests) and the ruhban (monks) to judge by what is in the Gospel. But they disbelieved and said: "Ezra is the son of Allah," and "the Messiah is the son of Allah." ﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, those are the defiantly disobedient﴾, meaning those who depart from the command of Allah the Exalted.

Allah the Glorious and Exalted said: ﴿And We have sent down to you﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿the Book﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿with the truth, confirming what was before it of the Book﴾, that is, of the scriptures revealed before it, ﴿and as a muhaymin (guardian, overseer) over it﴾. Al-Walibi related from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that it means a witness over it. This is also the view of Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Suddi and al-Kisa'i.

Hassan said:
"Indeed the Book is a muhaymin for our Prophet,
and the truth is recognised by those of understanding."

He meant: a witness and a confirmer.

Ikrimah said: a guide (dallan). Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Abu 'Ubaydah said: one entrusted over it (mu'taminan 'alayhi). Al-Hasan said: a trustworthy one (aminan). It has also been said: its original form is mu'ayminun, on the pattern of mufay'il from amin, just as they said musaytir from al-baytar (veterinarian), and the hamzah was changed to a ha', as in "aratu al-ma'a" and "haraqtuhu," and "iyhat" and "hayhat," and similar words. The meaning of the Qur'an's trusteeship, according to Ibn Jurayj, is: the Qur'an is a trustworthy witness over the books before it. So whatever the People of the Book report about their book, if it is in the Qur'an, then confirm it, and if not, then deny it. [In "B": "kutubihim" (their books).]

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib and al-Dahhak said: a judge (qadiyan). Al-Khalil said: a watcher and a guardian (raqiban wa hafizan). The meanings are close. The sense of all of them is that every book to which the Qur'an bears witness as true is the Book of Allah the Exalted, and whatever it does not so attest is not.

﴿So judge﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿between them﴾, between the People of the Book when they bring their dispute to you, ﴿by what Allah has revealed﴾, by the Qur'an, ﴿and do not follow their desires away from the truth that has come to you﴾, that is, do not turn away from the truth that has come to you and do not follow their desires.

﴿For each of you We have appointed a law (shir'ah) and a way (minhaj)﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan and Mujahid said: that is, a path and a practice. The Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 5, verses 49–50:

His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿And judge between them by what Allah has revealed, and do not follow their desires, and beware of them lest they tempt you away from some of what Allah has revealed to you.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: Ka'b ibn [Asad] [[In the original: (Usayd); the correction is from Ibn Hisham's Sirah: 2/567.]], 'Abdullah ibn [Suriya] [[In Ibn Hisham's Sirah: (Salubah).]], and Shas ibn Qays, who were among the chiefs of the Jews, said to one another: "Come, let us go to Muhammad; perhaps we can tempt him away from his religion." So they came to him and said: "O Muhammad, you know that we are the rabbis and the nobles of the Jews, and that if we follow you, the Jews will not oppose us. Between us and our people there are disputes, and we will bring them to you for judgment. Decide in our favor against them, and we will believe in you, and others will follow us." Their aim was not faith; their aim was only deception and to invite him to lean toward partiality in judgment. So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed the verse. [[Ibn Hisham's Sirah: 2/567; al-Tabari: 10/393; Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi, p. 229.]]

﴿But if they turn away﴾, that is, they turn away from faith and from judging by the Qur'an. ﴿Then know that Allah intends only to afflict them for some of their sins﴾, that is: know that their turning away is because Allah intends to hasten for them the punishment in this world for some of their sins. ﴿And indeed, many of the people﴾, meaning the Jews, ﴿are defiantly disobedient.﴾

﴿Do they seek the judgment of ignorance?﴾ [108] Ibn 'Amir read "tabghun" with a ta' (second person), while the others read it with a ya' (third person), meaning: they seek. ﴿And who is better than Allah in judgment for a people who are certain?﴾

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 5, verses 51–52:**

﴿O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies.﴾ The scholars differed concerning the occasion of revelation (asbab al-nuzul) of this verse, although its ruling is general for all believers.

Some people said: It was revealed concerning Ubadah ibn al-Samit and Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, because the two of them disputed. Ubadah said: "I have many allies among the Jews, their number is great and their might is strong, and I disavow to Allah and to His Messenger their alliance and the alliance of the Jews. I have no ally except Allah and His Messenger." Abd Allah said: "But I do not disavow the alliance of the Jews, for I fear the turns of fortune, and I cannot do without them." The Prophet ﷺ said: "O Abu al-Hubab, whatever you withhold of your alliance with the Jews in favour of Ubadah ibn al-Samit, it is yours instead of him." He said: "Then I accept." So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.

[[See: Tafsir al-Tabari: 10/395–396; al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/98–99; Asbab al-Nuzul p. 229.]]

Al-Suddi said: When the battle of Uhud took place, it grew severe upon a group of people, and they feared that the disbelievers would gain the upper hand over them. A man from among the Muslims said: "I will join so-and-so, the Jew, and take a guarantee of safety from him, for I fear that the Jews will gain the upper hand over us." Another man said: "As for me, I will join so-and-so, the Christian, from the people of Syria, and take a guarantee of safety from him." So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse forbidding them both.

[[See: Tafsir al-Tabari: 6/276 (Halabi edition); al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/99.]]

Ikrimah said: It was revealed concerning [Abu Lubabah] [[In "B" (Abu Umamah), which is an error.]] ibn Abd al-Mundhir, whom the Prophet ﷺ sent to Banu Qurayzah [when he besieged them] [[What is between the brackets is omitted from "B".]]. They consulted him about coming down (from their fortresses), and they said: "What will he do with us if we come down?" He placed his finger on his throat, meaning: "It is slaughter," that is, he will kill you. So this verse was revealed.

[[See: al-Tabari: 6/276 (Halabi edition); al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/99–100. Here we place a word of the shaykh of the exegetes, the Imam al-Tabari, may Allah have mercy on him, clarifying the correct view among these opinions. He said: "The correct position in this matter, in our view, is to say: Allah, dhikruhu, forbade all the believers to take the Jews and the Christians as helpers and allies against the people of faith in Allah and His Messenger, and He informed that whoever takes them as a helper, ally and friend besides Allah, His Messenger and the believers, then he is among them in conspiring against Allah, His Messenger and the believers, and that Allah and His Messenger are free of him. It is possible that the verse was revealed concerning Ubadah ibn al-Samit, Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul and their Jewish allies; it is possible that it was revealed concerning Abu Lubabah because of his action toward Banu Qurayzah; and it is possible that it was revealed concerning the two men whom al-Suddi mentioned, one of whom resolved to join Dahlak the Jew and the other a Christian in Syria. No report with any of these three opinions has been authenticated by a proof that establishes it, so that the statement that it was as said can be accepted as sound. Since this is so, the correct view is that the apparent sense of the revelation is taken to be general, applying to whatever it encompasses. What the people of interpretation have said on this matter is permissible, insofar as we have no knowledge contrary to it. Yet there is no doubt that the verse was revealed concerning a hypocrite who used to befriend Jews or Christians out of fear for himself from the turns of time, because the verse after it indicates that."]]

﴿Some of them are allies of others.﴾ In support and aid. And their hand is one against the Muslims. ﴿And whoever among you takes them as allies, then indeed he is one of them. Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾ [So He grants them success and helps them] [[Addition from "B".]].

﴿So you see those in whose hearts is a disease﴾ meaning: hypocrisy, referring to Abd Allah ibn Ubayy and his companions among the hypocrites who befriend the Jews, ﴿hastening toward them﴾ in aiding them and befriending them, ﴿saying: "We fear that a misfortune may strike us."﴾ A turn (dawlah) of fortune. Meaning: that time may turn a turn against us, and we will need their support for us. Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, said: its meaning is, "We fear that the affair of Muhammad will not be completed, and the matter will turn against us." And it was said: "We fear that time will turn against us with something disagreeable, such as drought and famine, and so they will not give us provisions and loans." ﴿So perhaps Allah will bring the conquest﴾. Qatadah and Muqatil said: by a decisive judgment of the victory of Muhammad ﷺ over those who opposed him. Al-Kalbi and al-Suddi said: the conquest of Makkah. Al-Dahhak said: the conquest of the Jewish settlements, such as Khaybar and Fadak. ﴿Or a command from Him﴾. It was said: by completing the affair of Muhammad ﷺ. It was said: it is a punishment for them. It was said: the expulsion of Banu al-Nadir. ﴿Then they will become﴾ meaning: these hypocrites, ﴿regretful over what they concealed within themselves﴾ of allegiance to the Jews and passing information to them.

They differed concerning who these people are. ʿAli ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him), al-Hasan and Qatadah said: they are Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) and his companions who fought the people of apostasy (ridda) and those who withheld zakah (obligatory alms). That is because when the Prophet (ﷺ) was taken in death, most of the Arabs apostatized, except the people of Makkah, Madinah, and ʿAbd al-Qays from Bahrain. Some of them withheld zakah, and Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) decided to fight them. The Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) disliked this, and ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "How can we fight the people when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'I have been commanded to fight the people until they say there is no god but Allah. Whoever says it has protected his life and property from me, except by its right, and his reckoning is with Allah, Mighty and Majestic'?" Abu Bakr said: "By Allah, I will surely fight whoever separates the prayer from zakah, for zakah is the right of wealth. By Allah, if they withheld from me even a young goat (ʿanaqan) [In manuscript B: "ʿiqālan" (a cord)] that they used to pay to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), I would fight them over withholding it." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of Zakah, chapter on the obligation of zakah, 3/262; and by Muslim in the Book of Faith, chapter on the command to fight the people until they say "There is no god but Allah," no. 20, 1/51-52; and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah, 1/66-67.]]

Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him) said: The Companions disliked fighting those who withheld zakah, and they said: "They are people of the qiblah." Then Abu Bakr girded on his sword and went out alone, so they had no choice but to go out following him.

Ibn Masʿud said: "We disliked it at the beginning, then we praised him for it in the end."

Abu Bakr ibn ʿAyyash said: I heard Abu Husayn say: "No one born after the prophets is more excellent than Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him). He stood in the position of one of the prophets in fighting the people of apostasy."

Three groups had apostatized during the lifetime of the Prophet (ﷺ):

Among them were the Banu Madhhij [In manuscript B: "Banu Madhdhah"], whose chief was Dhu al-Khimar, ʿAbhalah ibn Kaʿb al-ʿAnsi, who was called al-Aswad. He was a soothsayer and a trickster who claimed prophecy in Yemen and seized control of its lands. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wrote to Muʿadh ibn Jabal and the Muslims with him, instructing them to urge the people to hold fast to their religion and to rise up to fight al-Aswad. Then Fayruz al-Daylami killed him in his bed. Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: The news came to the Prophet (ﷺ) from heaven on the night he was killed, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Al-Aswad was killed last night; a blessed man killed him." It was asked: "Who is he?" He said: "Fayruz, [Fazfayruz] [[Omitted in manuscript B.]]." The Prophet (ﷺ) gave his Companions the good news of al-Aswad's destruction, and he (ﷺ) passed away the next day. The news of the killing of al-Ansi reached Madinah at the end of Rabiʿ al-Awwal, after Usamah had set out. That was the first conquest that came to Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him). [[See: Tarikh al-Tabari 3/227 onward; al-Bidayah wa'l-Nihayah 6/305-311; Usd al-Ghabah by Ibn al-Athir 4/371; Tafsir al-Tabari 10/424-425.]]

The second group: the Banu Hanifah in al-Yamamah, whose chief was Musaylimah al-Kadhdhab [[Omitted in manuscript B: "His name was Thumamah ibn Qays."]]. He had claimed prophecy during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at the end of the tenth year (AH), and he claimed that he was made a partner with Muhammad (ﷺ) in prophethood. He wrote to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "From Musaylimah, the Messenger of Allah, to Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah. To proceed: the earth is half mine and half yours." He sent this with two men from among his companions. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: [Do you both testify that Musaylimah is the Messenger of Allah? They said: Yes. The Prophet (ﷺ) said:] [[Added from manuscript B.]] "Were it not that messengers are not killed, I would have struck off your necks." Then he replied: "From Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, to Musaylimah the liar. To proceed: the earth belongs to Allah; He bequeaths it to whomever of His servants He wills, and the final outcome is for the righteous." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fell ill and passed away. Abu Bakr sent Khalid ibn al-Walid against Musaylimah the liar with a large army, until Allah destroyed him at the hands of Wahshi, the slave of Mutʿim ibn ʿAdi, who had killed Hamzah ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib, after a fierce battle. Wahshi used to say: "I killed the best of people in the Jahiliyyah and the worst of people in Islam." [[See: Sunan Abi Dawud, Book of Jihad, chapter on messengers, 4/64; al-Bidayah wa'l-Nihayah 5/51, 6/200; Sirah of Ibn Hisham 2/600.]]

The third group: the Banu Asad, whose chief was Tulayhah ibn Khuwaylid ibn al-Walid. Tulayhah was the last to apostatize, and he claimed prophecy during the lifetime of the Prophet (ﷺ). After the death of the Prophet (ﷺ), a great multitude apostatized during the caliphate of Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) [[Omitted in manuscript B.]], until Allah relieved the Muslims of their affair and gave victory to His religion through the hands of Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him). [[See: Hurub al-Ridda by the martyr-historian al-Kalaʿi, p. 35 onward.]]

ʿAʾishah said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed away, the Arabs apostatized, hypocrisy raised its head, and there befell Abu Bakr what, had it befallen the towering mountains, would have crushed them." [[See: al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah of Ibn Hisham 2/665; Hurub al-Ridda of al-Kalaʿi p. 35; Tarikh al-Tabari 3/225.]]

It is narrated from ʿIyad ibn Ghanm al-Ashʿari who said: When this verse was revealed, ﴿then Allah will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "They are the people of this one," and he pointed to Abu Musa al-Ashʿari. [[Narrated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak 2/313 and he declared it sound according to the conditions of Muslim; al-Tabarani narrated it and its narrators are the narrators of the sound collections (Majma' al-Zawa'id 7/16); and al-Tabari in his Tafsir 10/414-415.]] They were from Yemen.

Abu ʿAbd Allah Muhammad ibn al-Fadl al-Kharqi informed us: Abu al-Hasan al-Taysafuni informed us: Abu ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar al-Jawhari informed us: Ahmad ibn [ʿAli al-Kushmihani narrated to us: ʿAli ibn] [[Added from manuscript B and Sharh al-Sunnah.]] Hujr informed us: Isma'il ibn Ja'far informed us: Muhammad ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAlqamah informed us, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The people of Yemen have come to you; they are gentler of heart and softer of hearts. Faith is Yamani, and wisdom is Yamani." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of Maghazi, chapter on the arrival of the Ashʿariyyun and the people of Yemen, 8/98; by Muslim in the Book of Faith, chapter on the people of faith, no. 52, 1/71; and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah 14/201.]]

Al-Kalbi said: They are tribes from Yemen: two thousand from al-Nakhaʿ, five thousand from Kindah and Bajilah, and three thousand from the scattered people (afya' al-nas). They fought in the cause of Allah at the Battle of al-Qadisiyyah in the days of ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him).

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿humbled toward the believers﴾ means: tender and merciful, based on His saying, Mighty and Majestic: "And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy." It does not mean abasement; rather, it means that their side is gentle toward the believers. It was also said: it derives from dhull (submission), from the expression "a tame (dhalul) beast," meaning they are humble, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth in humility﴾. ﴿Mighty toward the disbelievers﴾ means: fierce, harsh toward the disbelievers, opposing and overcoming them, from the expression ʿazzahu, meaning he overpowered him. ʿAta' said: "Humbled toward the believers" is like a child to his father and a slave to his master; "mighty toward the disbelievers" is like a predator to its prey. Its parallel is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿fierce against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves﴾.

﴿They strive in the way of Allah and do not fear the blame of any blamer﴾ means: they do not fear the people's blame concerning Allah. That is because the hypocrites used to watch the disbelievers and fear their blame. We have been related from ʿUbadah ibn al-Samit who said: "We pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to hear and obey, and to stand up or speak the truth wherever we are, not fearing in Allah the blame of any blamer." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of Ahkam, chapter on how the imam takes the pledge from the people, 13/192, and in the Book of Fitan; by Muslim in the Book of Imarah, chapter on the obligation to obey rulers in what is not sinful, no. 1709, 3/1470; and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah 10/46.]]

﴿That is the bounty of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills﴾, meaning: their love for Allah, the gentleness of their side toward the Muslims, and their severity toward the disbelievers are all from the bounty of Allah upon them. ﴿And Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing﴾.

﴿And﴾ at that time, ﴿those who believe will say﴾ [The people of Kufa recited "wa-yaqulu" with a waw and with the raf' (nominative) vowel on the lam] [[The text within the brackets is absent from manuscript B.]] The people of Basra recited it with a waw and the nasb (accusative) on the lam, as a conjunction with ﴿an yaʾtiya﴾ (that He may bring), meaning: "and perhaps those who believe will say." Others recited it without the waw and with the raf' on the lam. It is likewise in the codices of the people of [al-ʿĀliyah] [[In manuscript B: "al-Shām" (Syria).]], dispensing with the conjunction because this verse is connected to what precedes it. The meaning is: those who believe will say at the time when Allah makes the hypocrites' hypocrisy manifest, ﴿"Are these the ones who swore by Allah﴾ (swore by Allah), ﴿with the utmost of their oaths?﴾ (that is, they swore with the most emphatic oaths), ﴿that they were surely with you?﴾ (that is, that they were believers)." The meaning is that the believers at that time will marvel at their lying and their swearing to falsehood. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Their deeds have become void﴾ (all the good they did has been nullified), ﴿and they have become losers﴾ (they lost this world through their exposure, and the Hereafter through punishment and the forfeiture of reward).

﴿Verily your guardian is Allah, and His Messenger, and those who believe﴾. It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) that it was revealed concerning ʿUbadah ibn al-Samit and ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, when ʿUbadah disavowed the Jews and said: "I take Allah and His Messenger and those who believe as my allies." [[What is between the brackets is missing from manuscript "B".]] [[See what preceded, the occasion of revelation (asbab al-nuzul) of verse 51 of the surah, and al-Tabari: 10/424.]]

[[Recorded by al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul (230), from Jabir and from Ibn ʿAbbas. al-Suyuti attributed it to Ibn Mardawayh by way of al-Kalbi from Abu Salih from Ibn ʿAbbas in similar wording, in al-Durr al-Manthur 3/105.]]

On this interpretation, by His saying: ﴿and they are bowing﴾, He meant the voluntary prayer (salat al-tatawwu') by night and by day. Ibn ʿAbbas said this.

Al-Suddi said: His saying "And those who believe, who establish the prayer and give the zakat while bowing" refers to ʿAli ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him), when a beggar passed by him while he was bowing in the mosque, and he gave him his ring. [[Recorded by al-Tabari: 10/325-326. In it, from al-Suddi: "These are all the believers, but ʿAli ibn Abi Talib was passed by a beggar while he was bowing." See also al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/104-105.]]

Abu Jaʿfar Muhammad ibn ʿAli al-Baqir said: ﴿Verily your guardian is Allah and His Messenger and those who believe﴾ was revealed concerning the believers. It was said to him: "Some people say it was revealed concerning ʿAli (may Allah be pleased with him)." He said: "He is among the believers." [[Recorded by al-Tabari: 10/425. See also al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/106.]]

Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah said: ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, our people Qurayzah and al-Nadir have shunned us, separated from us, and sworn that they will not sit with us." So this verse was revealed, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited it to him. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, we are pleased with Allah, His Messenger, and the believers as allies." [[Recorded by al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul (230), from Jabir and from Ibn ʿAbbas. al-Suyuti attributed it to Ibn Mardawayh by way of al-Kalbi from Abu Salih from Ibn ʿAbbas in similar wording, in al-Durr al-Manthur 3/105.]]

On this interpretation, by His saying: ﴿and they are bowing﴾, He meant the voluntary prayer (salat al-tatawwu') by night and by day. Ibn ʿAbbas said this.

Al-Suddi said: His saying "And those who believe, who establish the prayer and give the zakat while bowing" refers to ʿAli ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him), when a beggar passed by him while he was bowing in the mosque, and he gave him his ring. [[Recorded by al-Tabari: 10/325-326. In it, from al-Suddi: "These are all the believers, but ʿAli ibn Abi Talib was passed by a beggar while he was bowing." See also al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/104-105.]]

Juwaybir related from al-Dahhak concerning His saying: ﴿Verily your guardian is Allah and His Messenger and those who believe﴾, he said: they are the believers, some of them allies of others. Abu Jaʿfar Muhammad ibn ʿAli al-Baqir said: ﴿Verily your guardian is Allah and His Messenger and those who believe﴾ was revealed concerning the believers. It was said to him: "Some people say it was revealed concerning ʿAli (may Allah be pleased with him)." He said: "He is among the believers." [[Recorded by al-Tabari: 10/425. See also al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/106.]]

﴿And whoever takes Allah and His Messenger and those who believe as allies﴾, meaning: whoever undertakes to carry out the obedience of Allah and to support His Messenger and the believers. Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: he means the Muhajirun (emigrants) and the Ansar (helpers). ﴿Then indeed the party of Allah﴾, meaning: the helpers of the religion of Allah, ﴿they are the victorious﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 5, verses 57–59:

Allah the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take those who have taken your religion as ridicule and amusement﴾. Ibn Abbas said: Rifa'ah ibn Zayd ibn al-Tabut and Suwayd ibn al-Harith had outwardly professed Islam, then they became hypocrites, and some of the Muslims were friendly with them, so Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed this verse [[See: Sirah of Ibn Hisham: 1/568; Tafsir al-Tabari: 6/290; Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi p. 231; al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/107.]] "O you who have believed, do not take those who have taken your religion as ridicule and amusement", by their displaying that with their tongues in words while they conceal disbelief. ﴿From among those who were given the Scripture before you﴾, meaning: the Jews, ﴿and the disbelievers﴾. The people of Basra and al-Kisa'i read "al-kuffari" with a kasrah on the ra', [meaning: and from among the disbelievers] [[Omitted from "b".]] and the others read it with a fathah, meaning: do not take the disbelievers ﴿as allies﴾. ﴿And fear Allah, if you are believers﴾.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And when you call to prayer, they take it as ridicule and amusement. That is because they are a people who do not reason﴾. Al-Kalbi said: The caller of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when he called to prayer and the Muslims stood up for it, the Jews said: "They have stood up, may they not stand! They have prayed, may they not pray!" mocking, and they laughed, so Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed this verse [[See: Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, p. 231; al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/107.]].

Al-Suddi said: It was revealed concerning a man from the Christians in Medina who, whenever he heard the muezzin say, "I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah," would say: "Burn the liar." One night his servant came in with a fire while he and his family were sleeping, and a spark flew from it, so the house burned and he and his family burned with it [[See: al-Tabari: 6/291; al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/107-108; Asbab al-Nuzul p. 231; al-Bahr al-Muhit: 3/515.]].

Others said: When the disbelievers heard the adhan, they envied the Muslims, so they came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Muhammad, you have innovated something we have not heard of in the past nations. If you claim prophethood, then in what you have introduced you have opposed the prophets before you. Had there been any good in it, the most deserving of people to have it would have been the prophets. So from where do you get a cry like the cry of [the goat] [[In Asbab al-Nuzul it is "the donkey".]]? How ugly a sound and how contemptible a matter!" So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse, and He revealed "And who is better in speech than one who calls to Allah..." [[See: Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi pp. 231-232; al-Bahr al-Muhit: 3/515.]].

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Say, O People of the Scripture, do you resent us except that we have believed in Allah and what has been revealed to us and what was revealed before, and that most of you are defiantly disobedient?﴾ ... The verse. Al-Kisa'i read "hal tanqimun" with the lam of "hal" assimilated into the ta', and likewise he assimilates the lam of "hal" into the ta', tha', and nun; Hamzah agreed with him regarding the ta' and tha', and Abu Amr agreed regarding "hal tara" in two places.

Ibn Abbas said: A group of Jews came to the Prophet ﷺ, Abu Yasir ibn Akhtab, Rafi' ibn Abi Rafi', and others, and they asked him about which of the messengers he believed in. He said: "We believe in Allah and what has been revealed to us and what was revealed to Abraham and Ishmael..." up to His saying: "and to Him we are submitting." When he mentioned Jesus, peace be upon him, they denied his prophethood and said: "By Allah, we know of no people with less share in this world and the Hereafter than you, nor any religion worse than your religion." So Allah revealed this verse [[See: Sirah of Ibn Hisham: 1/567; al-Tabari: 6/292; al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/108; Asbab al-Nuzul p. 232.]]: "Say, O People of the Scripture, do you resent us," meaning: do you dislike from us, ﴿except that we have believed in Allah and what has been revealed to us and what was revealed before, and that most of you are defiantly disobedient﴾, meaning: do you dislike from us anything except our belief and your defiant disobedience? That is, you dislike our belief while you know that we are upon the truth, because you have become defiantly disobedient by remaining upon your religion out of love for leadership and love for wealth.

So He mentioned the answer in the wording of the beginning (al-ibtida'), and it is not necessarily that the beginning is worse, like the verse of the Exalted: "Shall I inform you of something worse than that? "With Allah: those whom Allah cursed," meaning: it is those whom Allah cursed, "and with whom He was angry," meaning: the Jews, "and made of them apes and swine." The apes were the people of the Sabbath, and the swine were the disbelievers of the table of Jesus, peace be upon him.

It is narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that both of the transformed groups were from the people of the Sabbath: their young men were transformed into apes and their elders were transformed into swine.

"And served the Taghut" (wa 'abada al-taghut), meaning: among them was made the one who served the Taghut, that is, who obeyed Satan in what he embellished for him. Its confirmation is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: "and those who served the Taghut." Hamzah recited "wa 'Abud" with a damma on the ba' and "al-Taghut" with a kasra on the ta', intending "al-'Abud," and both are dialects: 'abd with a sukun on the ba' and 'ubud with a damma on the ba', like sab' and subu'. It was also said that it is the plural of 'ibad. Al-Hasan recited "wa 'abada al-taghut" in the singular. "Those are worse in position and further astray from the right way," meaning: from the path of truth.
