Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 5, verse 64:

﴿The Jews say: "Allah's hand is chained up."﴾ Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ikrima, al-Dahhak and Qatada said: Allah had widened His provision for the Jews, so that they were among the wealthiest of people and the most fruitful in their land. When they disobeyed Allah concerning the matter of Muhammad (ﷺ) and denied him, Allah withheld from them the abundance He had given them. At that point Finhas ibn 'Azura said: "Allah's hand is chained up," meaning: held back and restricted from provision. They attributed to Him stinginess. Allah is exalted above that.

It is said that only Finhas said this statement. When the others did not forbid him and approved of his words, Allah made them all share in it.

al-Hasan said: its meaning is "Allah's hand is restrained from punishing us. He will not punish us except for a limited period, as much as our fathers worshipped the calf." The first interpretation is preferable because of His saying: ﴿He spends as He wills﴾.

﴿Their hands are chained﴾: that is, their hands are held back [[In manuscript "b": "Allah has restrained"]] from good things. al-Zajjaj said: Allah answered them and said: "I am the Generous, and they are the stingy. Their hands are the chained ones, the ones that hold back." It is also said: this is from the chain (ghull) in the Fire on the Day of Resurrection, as in His saying: ﴿When the shackles are around their necks and the chains﴾ (Ghafir, 71).

﴿And they are cursed﴾: they are punished, ﴿for what they said﴾. Among their curse is that they were transformed into apes and swine, and humiliation and wretchedness were struck upon them in this world, and in the Hereafter they will be in the Fire. ﴿Rather, His two hands are outstretched﴾. "Allah's hand" is one of His attributes [[In manuscript "b": "attributes of His essence"]], like hearing, sight and face. He, exalted is His remembrance, said: ﴿What I created with My two hands﴾ (Sad, 75). The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Both of His hands are right hands." [[A fragment of a hadith recorded by Imam Muslim in the Book of Leadership, chapter on the virtue of the just ruler and the punishment of the oppressor, no. (1827): 3/1458.]] Allah knows best His attributes; for the servants, the obligation regarding them is belief and submission.

The leading imams of the early generations (al-salaf) from Ahl al-Sunna (the People of the Sunna) said concerning these attributes: "Let them pass as they came, without asking how."

﴿He spends﴾: He provides, ﴿as He wills. And what has been sent down to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in rebellion and disbelief﴾: that is, every time a verse was revealed they disbelieved in it and increased in rebellion and disbelief. [[Omitted in "b".]] ﴿And We have cast among them enmity and hatred﴾: meaning among the Jews and the Christians, as said by al-Hasan and Mujahid. It is also said: among the various groups of Jews. Allah made them differ in their religion and hate one another ﴿until the Day of Resurrection. Every time they kindle a fire for war, Allah extinguishes it﴾. This refers to the Jews: they corrupted and opposed the judgment of the Torah, so Allah sent Bukhtansar (Nebuchadnezzar) against them. Then they corrupted again, so Allah sent Titus the Roman against them. Then they corrupted again, so Allah empowered the Magians (Majus) over them. Then they corrupted again, so Allah sent the Muslims against them.

It is also said: every time they resolved to corrupt the affair of Muhammad (ﷺ) and kindled the fire of war, Allah extinguished it, turned them back, subdued them, and gave victory to His Prophet and his religion. This is the meaning of al-Hasan's statement. Qatada said: this is general to every war the Jews sought; you will not encounter a Jew in a city except that you find him among the most humiliated of people. ﴿And they strive upon the earth in corruption, and Allah does not love the corrupters﴾.

**Verses 65–67 of Surah al-Ma'idah**

﴿And if the People of the Scripture had believed﴾ in Muhammad ﷺ, ﴿and had feared God﴾ from disbelief, ﴿We would have removed from them their misdeeds and admitted them to Gardens of Bliss﴾.

﴿And if they had upheld the Torah and the Gospel﴾, meaning: had upheld their rulings and limits and acted upon what is in them, ﴿and what was sent down to them from their Lord﴾, meaning: the Qur'an. It was also said: the books of the prophets of the Children of Israel. ﴿They would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet﴾. It was said: "from above them" is the rain, and "from beneath their feet" is the produce of the earth.

Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: "We would have sent down rain upon them and brought forth for them the produce of the earth."

Al-Farra' said: He intended by this abundance in provision, as one says, "So-and-so is in prosperity from his head to his feet." A parallel to this is the words of the Exalted: ﴿And if the people of the towns had believed and feared God, We would have opened for them blessings from the heaven and the earth﴾ (al-A'raf, 96).

﴿Among them is a moderate community﴾, meaning: the believers among the People of the Scripture, such as 'Abd Allah ibn Salam and his companions. *Muqtasidah* means just, not extreme, nor negligent and harsh. The meaning of *al-iqtisad* (moderation) in the language is balance in action, without excess and without deficiency.

﴿And many of them﴾, such as Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf and his companions, ﴿evil is what they do﴾: how wretched is what they do. Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: "They did evil while denying the Prophet ﷺ."

The words of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿O Messenger, convey what has been sent down to you from your Lord﴾ to the end of the verse. It was narrated from Masruq who said: 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "Whoever tells you that Muhammad ﷺ concealed anything of what Allah sent down has lied," and she recited: "O Messenger, convey what has been sent down to you from your Lord" to the end of the verse.[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Tafsir, chapter "O Messenger, convey..." of Surah al-Ma'idah: 8/275, and Muslim in Iman, chapter on the meaning of Allah's words "And he had certainly seen Him in another descent" no. (177): 1/159.]] Al-Hasan narrated: When Allah sent His Messenger, he became distressed and knew that there were people who would deny him, so this verse was revealed.[[Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi, pp. 232–233; al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/116–117.]]

It was also said: it was revealed concerning the defects of the Jews. The Prophet ﷺ invited them to Islam, and they said, "We submitted before you," and they began to mock him, saying to him, "Do you want us to take you as a *hannan* (a beloved one) as the Christians took 'Isa son of Maryam as a *hannan*?" When the Prophet ﷺ saw this, he fell silent, and this verse was revealed, and He commanded him to say to them: "O People of the Scripture, you are not upon anything" to the end of the verse.

It was also said: "Convey what has been sent down to you" concerning stoning and retaliation; it was revealed concerning the affair of the Jews.

It was also said: it was revealed concerning the matter of Zaynab bint Jahsh and her marriage.

It was also said: it concerns jihad, because the hypocrites disliked it, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So when a decisive surah is revealed and fighting is mentioned therein, you see those in whose hearts is disease looking at you with the look of one fainting before death﴾ (Muhammad, 20). And some of the believers disliked it. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Have you not seen those who were told, "Restrain your hands"?﴾ to the end of the verse (an-Nisa', 77). So the Prophet ﷺ would at times refrain from urging jihad because of what he knew of some people's aversion, and Allah sent down this verse.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message﴾. The people of Madinah read *risalatihi* in the plural (*risalatihi* as *risalatihi*), and the rest read *risalatahu* in the singular.

The meaning of the verse: if you do not convey all of it and leave out some of it, then you have conveyed nothing; that is, your sin in leaving off conveying part of it is like your sin in leaving off conveying all of it, as in His words: ﴿And they say, "We believe in some and disbelieve in others," and they intend to adopt a way between that. Those are the disbelievers, truly﴾ (an-Nisa', 150–151). He informed that their disbelief in part nullifies their belief in part.

It was also said: "Convey what has been sent down to you" means: make its conveyance manifest, as in His words: ﴿So declare what you are commanded﴾ (al-Hijr, 94). And "if you do not": if you do not make its conveyance manifest, then you have not conveyed His message. He commanded him to convey what was sent down to him openly, seeking reward, patient, not fearful. If you conceal any of it out of fear of harm that may befall you, then you have not conveyed His message.

﴿And Allah will protect you from the people﴾, that is, will guard you and prevent you from the people. If it is said: Was not his head wounded, his front tooth broken, and was he not harmed in various ways?

It is answered: its meaning is that He protects you from being killed, so they cannot reach to kill you.

It was also said: this verse was revealed after his head had been wounded, because Surah al-Ma'idah is among the last of what was revealed of the Qur'an.

It was also said: "And Allah will single you out with protection from among the people," because the Prophet ﷺ is protected (*ma'sum*).

﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide the disbelieving people﴾. 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us, who said: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, who said: Abu al-Yaman informed us, who said: Shu'ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Sinan ibn Abi Sinan al-Dili and Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman informed me that Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah informed him that he went on a military expedition with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ toward Najd. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned, he returned with him, and the midday rest overtook them in a valley thick with thorny trees. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ dismounted, and the people dispersed, seeking shade under the trees. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ dismounted under a tree and hung his sword upon it, and we slept a sleep. Then suddenly the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was calling us, and with him there was a Bedouin. He said: "This man drew my sword while I was sleeping. I woke up and he had it in his hand, unsheathed. He said: 'Who will protect you from me?' I said: 'Allah'" three times. And he did not punish him, and he sat down.[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Jihad, chapter on hanging one's sword on a tree during travel at midday rest: 6/96, and in al-Maghazi; and Muslim in Salat al-Musafirin, chapter on the prayer of fear, no. (843): 1/576. The wording is al-Bukhari's.]]

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi narrated from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Bedouin drew his sword and said: "Who will protect you from me, O Muhammad?" He said: "Allah." So the Bedouin's hand trembled, the sword fell from his hand, and he began striking his head against the tree until his brain was scattered. Then Allah the Exalted sent down this verse.

'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us, who said: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, who said: Isma'il ibn Khalil informed us, who said: 'Ali ibn Mushir informed us, who said: Yahya ibn Sa'id informed us, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amir ibn Rabi'ah informed us, who said: I heard 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her) say: The Prophet ﷺ had stayed awake, and when he arrived at Madinah he said: "I wish a righteous man from among my companions would guard me tonight." Suddenly we heard the sound of weapons. He said: "Who is this?" The man said: "I am Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas; I have come to guard you." So the Prophet ﷺ slept.[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Jihad, chapter on guarding in the way of Allah: 6/81, and Muslim in Fada'il al-Sahabah, chapter on the virtue of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, no. (2410): 4/1875.]]

'Abd Allah ibn Shaqiq said, on the authority of 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her): She said: The Prophet ﷺ used to be guarded until this verse was revealed: ﴿And Allah will protect you from the people﴾. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ put his head out of the tent and said to them: "O people, disperse, for Allah the Glorified and Exalted has protected me."[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in Tafsir, Surah al-Ma'idah: 8/411, and he said: "This is a gharib hadith. Some narrated this hadith from al-Juraybiri, from 'Abd Allah ibn Shaqiq, who said: The Prophet ... and they did not mention in it: from 'A'ishah." It was authenticated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak: 2/313, and al-Dhahabi concurred; and by al-Tabari in his Tafsir: 6/308. Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in Fath al-Bari: "Its isnad is hasan, and they differed regarding its connection and its being mursal." al-Suyuti added its attribution to: 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, and al-Bayhaqi (both in al-Dala'il), and Ibn Mardawayh. See al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/118.]]

And "if you do not": if you do not make its conveyance manifest, then you have not conveyed His message. He commanded him to convey what was sent down to him openly, seeking reward, patient, not fearful. If you conceal any of it out of fear of harm that may befall you, then you have not conveyed His message.

﴿And Allah will protect you from the people﴾, that is, will guard you and prevent you from the people. If it is said: Was not his head wounded, his front tooth broken, and was he not harmed in various ways?

It is answered: its meaning is that He protects you from being killed, so they cannot reach to kill you.

It was also said: this verse was revealed after his head had been wounded, because Surah al-Ma'idah is among the last of what was revealed of the Qur'an.

It was also said: "And Allah will single you out with protection from among the people," because the Prophet ﷺ is protected (*ma'sum*).

﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide the disbelieving people﴾. 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us, who said: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, who said: Abu al-Yaman informed us, who said: Shu'ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Sinan ibn Abi Sinan al-Dili and Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman informed me that Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah informed him that he went on a military expedition with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ toward Najd. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned, he returned with him, and the midday rest overtook them in a valley thick with thorny trees. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ dismounted, and the people dispersed, seeking shade under the trees. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ dismounted under a tree and hung his sword upon it, and we slept a sleep. Then suddenly the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was calling us, and with him there was a Bedouin. He said: "This man drew my sword while I was sleeping. I woke up and he had it in his hand, unsheathed. He said: 'Who will protect you from me?' I said: 'Allah'" three times. And he did not punish him, and he sat down.[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Jihad, chapter on hanging one's sword on a tree during travel at midday rest: 6/96, and in al-Maghazi; and Muslim in Salat al-Musafirin, chapter on the prayer of fear, no. (843): 1/576. The wording is al-Bukhari's.]]

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi narrated from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Bedouin drew his sword and said: "Who will protect you from me, O Muhammad?" He said: "Allah." So the Bedouin's hand trembled, the sword fell from his hand, and he began striking his head against the tree until his brain was scattered. Then Allah the Exalted sent down this verse.

'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us, who said: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, who said: Isma'il ibn Khalil informed us, who said: 'Ali ibn Mushir informed us, who said: Yahya ibn Sa'id informed us, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amir ibn Rabi'ah informed us, who said: I heard 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her) say: The Prophet ﷺ had stayed awake, and when he arrived at Madinah he said: "I wish a righteous man from among my companions would guard me tonight." Suddenly we heard the sound of weapons. He said: "Who is this?" The man said: "I am Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas; I have come to guard you." So the Prophet ﷺ slept.[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Jihad, chapter on guarding in the way of Allah: 6/81, and Muslim in Fada'il al-Sahabah, chapter on the virtue of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, no. (2410): 4/1875.]]

'Abd Allah ibn Shaqiq said, on the authority of 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her): She said: The Prophet ﷺ used to be guarded until this verse was revealed: ﴿And Allah will protect you from the people﴾. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ put his head out of the tent and said to them: "O people, disperse, for Allah the Glorified and Exalted has protected me."[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in Tafsir, Surah al-Ma'idah: 8/411, and he said: "This is a gharib hadith. Some narrated this hadith from al-Juraybiri, from 'Abd Allah ibn Shaqiq, who said: The Prophet ... and they did not mention in it: from 'A'ishah." It was authenticated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak: 2/313, and al-Dhahabi concurred; and by al-Tabari in his Tafsir: 6/308. Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in Fath al-Bari: "Its isnad is hasan, and they differed regarding its connection and its being mursal." al-Suyuti added its attribution to: 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, and al-Bayhaqi (both in al-Dala'il), and Ibn Mardawayh. See al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/118.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 5, verses 68–71:

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿Say: O People of the Scripture, you have not based yourselves on anything until you establish the Torah and the Gospel and what has been revealed to you from your Lord.﴾

Meaning: establish their rulings and what is obligatory upon you in them. ﴿And that which has been revealed to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in transgression and disbelief. So do not grieve﴾, i.e., do not be sad, ﴿over the disbelieving people.﴾

﴿Indeed, those who believed and those who were Jews and the Sabeans and the Christians﴾. The correct form would be ﴿wal-Sabi'in﴾. We have already discussed the reason for its nominative case in Surah al-Baqarah. (See the earlier explanation of verse 62 of Surah al-Baqarah, in the first volume.) Sibawayh said: there is an inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in it, its estimated meaning being: "Indeed, those who believed, and those who were Jews, and the Christians, whoever believed in God..." up to the end of the verse, and the Sabeans likewise. His saying ﴿those who believed﴾ means outwardly, with the tongue. His saying ﴿whoever believed in God﴾ means inwardly, with the heart. It is also said: ﴿those who believed﴾ refers to true faith, and ﴿whoever believed in God﴾ means remained steadfast in faith, ﴿and the Last Day and did righteous deeds, there will be no fear for them, nor will they grieve.﴾

His exalted saying: ﴿We had already taken the covenant of the Children of Israel﴾ concerning monotheism and prophethood, ﴿and We sent to them messengers. Every time a messenger came to them with what their souls did not desire, a group they denied, and a group they killed.﴾ The denied ones were Jesus and Muhammad, may the blessings and peace of God be upon them both, and the killed ones were Yahya and Zakariyya.

﴿And they thought﴾, i.e., they supposed, ﴿that there would be no trial﴾, i.e., punishment and killing. It is also said: a test and examination; i.e., they supposed that they would not be tested and that God would not punish them. The people of Basra, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read ﴿takun﴾ with a raised nun, on the meaning that it would not occur. The others read it in the accusative, as if the word "la" (not) did not precede it. ﴿So they became blind﴾ to the truth, so they did not see it, ﴿and deaf﴾ to it, so they did not hear it; meaning they became blind and deaf after Moses, may the blessings and peace of God be upon him. ﴿Then God relented toward them﴾ by sending Jesus, peace be upon him. ﴿Then many of them became blind and deaf again﴾ by disbelieving in Muhammad ﷺ. ﴿And God is Seeing of what they do.﴾

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (*Ma'alim al-Tanzil*) on Surah 5, verses 72–74:**

﴿Certainly those who said, "Indeed, Allah is the Messiah, the son of Mary," have disbelieved﴾. They are the Malkaniyya (Melkites) and the Ya'qubiyya (Jacobites) among them. ﴿And the Messiah said, "O Children of Israel, worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord. Indeed, whoever associates others with Allah, Allah has forbidden him Paradise, and his refuge is the Fire. And for the wrongdoers there are no helpers."﴾

﴿Certainly those who said, "Indeed, Allah is the third of three"﴾ means the Murqusiyya (Marcusians). There is an *idmar* (an implied omission) in it, meaning: "the third of three gods," because they say: divinity is shared between Allah, the Exalted, Mary, and Jesus, and each of these is a god, so they are three gods. This is clarified by the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to the Messiah: "Did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah'?" (al-Ma'idah, 116). Whoever says "Allah is the third of three" without intending divinity is not a disbeliever, for Allah says: "There is no secret conference of three but that He is their fourth" (al-Mujadila, 7). The Prophet ﷺ also said to Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him): "What do you think of two whom Allah is the third of?" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Tafsir, Surat al-Tawbah, chapter "The second of two when they were in the cave..." 8/325.]]. Then He said, refuting them: ﴿There is no god except One God. And if they do not desist from what they say, a painful punishment will surely befall those of them who disbelieve﴾. He specified "those who disbelieved" because He knew that some of them would believe.

﴿Will they not repent to Allah and seek His forgiveness?﴾ Al-Farra' said: this is a command in the form of a question, like His saying: ﴿So will you not desist?﴾ (al-Ma'idah, 91), meaning: "Desist!" The meaning is that Allah commands them to repent and seek forgiveness for this great sin. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving, Merciful﴾.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The Messiah, the son of Mary, was not but a messenger; messengers had passed on before him﴾ [[in (b): "passed away" (madat)]] ﴿and his mother was a truthful woman﴾. That is: he is not a god; rather, he is like the messengers who passed on before him, who were not gods. ﴿And his mother was a *siddiqah*﴾ meaning: abundantly truthful.

It was also said: she was called *siddiqah* because she affirmed the signs of Allah, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said in describing her: "She affirmed the words of her Lord" (al-Tahrim, 12). ﴿They both used to eat food﴾ meaning: they both lived on food and sustenance like the rest of the children of Adam. So how could one be a god when his existence depends only on eating food?

It was also said: this is an allusion to bodily excretion, since whoever eats and drinks must necessarily urinate and defecate. How could one with such a characteristic be a god?

Then He said: ﴿Look how We make the signs clear to them; then look how they are turned away﴾, meaning: they are turned away from the truth.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 5, verses 75–78:

﴿Say: "O People of the Scripture (Ahl al-Kitab), do not exceed the limits in your religion beyond the truth."﴾ That is: do not go beyond the limit. Both exaggeration (ghuluww) and negligence (taqsir) are blameworthy in religion. His words ﴿beyond the truth﴾ mean: in your religion, which contradicts the truth. They opposed the truth in their religion, then exaggerated in it by persisting in it. ﴿And do not follow the desires (ahwa') of a people﴾. The ahwa' is the plural of hawa, which is what the appetite of the soul calls for. ﴿Who had gone astray before﴾ means: the leaders of misguidance from the two groups, the Jews and the Christians. The address is to those in the time of the Prophet (ﷺ), who were forbidden to follow their predecessors in what they had innovated according to their own desires. [110a] ﴿And had led many astray﴾ means: those who followed them in their desires. ﴿And [they] strayed from the sound way﴾ means: from the straight path. That is, by misleading others. So the first straying is their own misguidance, and the second is by misleading those who followed them.

His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿Cursed were those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel by the tongue of David﴾ means: the people of Ayla when they transgressed on the Sabbath. David, peace be upon him, said: "O Allah, curse them and make them a sign," and so they were transformed into apes. ﴿And Jesus, the son of Mary﴾ means: by the tongue of Jesus, peace be upon him, that is, the disbelievers among the companions of the table (al-Ma'idah), when they did not believe. Jesus said: "O Allah, curse them and make them a sign," and so they were transformed into swine. ﴿That was because they disobeyed and were transgressing.﴾

Al-Baghawi, *Ma'alim al-Tanzil*, on Surah al-Ma'idah, verses 79–81:

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿You see many of them﴾. It was said: among the Jews, Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf and his companions, ﴿turning in friendship to those who disbelieve﴾,

the polytheists of Makkah, when they went out to them to gather an army against the Prophet ﷺ. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and al-Hasan said: "Among them," meaning among the hypocrites, ﴿turning in friendship to the Jews﴾. ﴿Evil is what their souls have sent ahead for them﴾: evil is what they had sent ahead of deeds for their return in the Hereafter, ﴿that Allah has become angry with them﴾: Allah became wrathful with them, ﴿and in punishment they will abide forever﴾.

﴿And if they had believed in Allah and the Prophet﴾ Muhammad ﷺ, ﴿and in what was revealed to him﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿they would not have taken them as allies﴾, meaning the disbelievers, ﴿but many of them are defiantly disobedient﴾, that is, they depart from the command of Allah, glorified and exalted is He.

Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿You will surely find the most intense of people in enmity toward the believers to be the Jews and those who associate others with Allah﴾, meaning the polytheists of the Arabs, ﴿and you will find the nearest of them in affection to the believers those who say, "We are Christians"﴾. It does not mean all Christians, because in their enmity toward the Muslims they are like the Jews in killing the Muslims, taking them captive, ruining their lands, demolishing their mosques and burning their copies of the Qur'an. There is no loyalty or honour for them. Rather, the verse refers to those among them who embraced Islam, such as the Negus (al-Najashi) and his companions. [And it was said: it was revealed concerning all Jews and all Christians, because the Jews are harder of heart and the Christians are softer of heart than them, and they were less inclined to back the polytheists than the Jews.]

The people of exegesis said: Quraysh conspired to seduce the believers away from their religion, so every tribe rose up against those among them who were Muslims, harming and torturing them. Some were seduced, and Allah protected whom He willed. Allah protected His Messenger through his uncle Abu Talib. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw what his companions were suffering, and he could not protect them, and he had not yet been commanded to fight, he ordered them to emigrate to the land of Abyssinia, saying: "There is in it a righteous king who does not wrong anyone, and no one is wronged in his presence. So go out to him until Allah grants the Muslims relief." By this he meant the Negus. His name was Ashamah, and in Abyssinian his name is 'Ativah. "Negus" is the title of the king, like the terms Caesar and Khosrow. So eleven men and four women secretly went out to them, namely: 'Uthman ibn 'Affan and his wife Ruqayyah, daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam; 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud; [and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf]; Abu Hudhayfah ibn 'Utbah and his wife Sahlah bint Suhayl ibn 'Amr; Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr; Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Asad and his wife Umm Salamah bint Abi Umayyah; 'Uthman ibn Maz'un; 'Amir ibn Rabi'ah and his wife Layla bint Abi [Hathmah] [in the original, "Khaythamah", corrected from the Sirah]; Hatib ibn 'Amr; and [Suhayl] ibn Bayda'. May Allah be pleased with them all. They went down to the sea and took a ship to the land of Abyssinia for half a dinar. That was in Rajab of the fifth year after the Prophethood of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and this is the First Emigration. Then Ja'far ibn Abi Talib went out, and Muslims followed one after another to it. The total number of Muslims who emigrated to Abyssinia was eighty-two men, apart from the women and children.

When Quraysh learned of this, they sent 'Amr ibn al-'As and his companion with gifts to the Negus and his patriarchs, so that they might return the emigrants to them. But Allah protected them. The story is mentioned in Surah Al 'Imran.

When the two returned disappointed, the Muslims remained there in the best dwelling and the finest neighbourhood until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ emigrated and his affair rose high. That was in the sixth year after the Hijrah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote to the Negus through 'Amr ibn Umayyah al-Damri, asking him to marry him to Umm Habibah bint Abi Sufyan, who had emigrated there with her husband, and her husband had died, and to send to him those Muslims who were with him. The Negus sent to Umm Habibah a slave-girl called Abrahah, to inform her of the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ proposal to her. She gave her silver anklets out of joy at that. She authorised Khalid ibn Sa'id ibn al-'As to marry her to him, for a dowry of four hundred dinars. The Negus, may Allah have mercy on him, was the one who proposed on behalf of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Negus sent four hundred dinars to her by means of Abrahah. When she came to her with them, Umm Habibah gave her fifty dinars, but she refused it and said: "The king commanded me not to take anything from you." She said: "I am in charge of the king's oils and garments. I have affirmed Muhammad ﷺ and believed in him. My request of you is that you convey my greetings to him." She said: "Yes." The king had also commanded his wives to send to her whatever aloes-wood and ambergris they had. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would see it upon her and he would not object.

Umm Habibah said: "We went out to Madinah while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was at Khaybar. Those who were to go out to him went out, and I remained in Madinah until the Prophet ﷺ arrived. I entered upon him, and he used to ask me about the Negus. I conveyed to him Abrahah's greetings, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned greetings to both of them." And Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: "It may be that Allah will bring about affection between you and those of them with whom you have enmity," meaning Abu Sufyan, affection, meaning through the marriage to Umm Habibah. When the marriage of Umm Habibah reached Abu Sufyan, he said: "That is the stallion whose nose is not rubbed in the dust." [That is, a noble equal who is not rejected.]

After the arrival of Ja'far, the Negus sent to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ his son Azha ibn Ashamah ibn Abjar with sixty men from Abyssinia, and he wrote to him: "O Messenger of Allah, I bear witness that you are the Messenger of Allah, truthful and confirmed. I have pledged allegiance to you and pledged allegiance to your cousin, and I have submitted to Allah, Lord of the worlds. I have sent to you my son Azha. If you wish that I come to you myself, I will do so. Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah." They boarded a ship following Ja'far and his companions, but when they were in the middle of the sea they drowned. Ja'far and his companions came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with seventy men wearing woollen garments, of whom sixty-two were from Abyssinia and eight from [the people of] Syria. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited Surah Ya-Sin to them to the end. They wept when they heard the Qur'an and believed. He said: "Believe." They said: "This resembles what was revealed to 'Isa, peace be upon him." So Allah, glorified and exalted, revealed this verse: ﴿And you will surely find the nearest of them in affection to the believers those who say, "We are Christians"﴾. It refers to the delegation of the Negus who came with Ja'far, and they were seventy, and they were the people of the monasteries.

Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: they were forty men, thirty-two from Abyssinia and eight Byzantines from Syria.

[Ata' said: they were eighty men, forty from the people of Najran from the Banu al-Harith ibn Ka'b, thirty-two from Abyssinia and eight Byzantines from Syria.]

Qatadah said: it was revealed concerning some People of the Book who were upon a path of truth from what 'Isa, peace be upon him, had brought. When Allah sent Muhammad ﷺ, they affirmed him and believed in him, and so Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, praised them for that.

﴿That is because among them are priests﴾, that is, scholars. Qutrub said: "Qass" and "qissis" mean a scholar in the language of the Romans. ﴿And monks﴾: the monks are the devotees, the people of the monasteries; the singular is rahib, like faris and fursan, and rakib and rukban. It may also be used as a singular, with the plural rahabin, like qurban and qarabin. ﴿And that they are not arrogant﴾: they do not exalt themselves so as to refuse faith and submission to the truth.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote to the Negus through 'Amr ibn Umayyah al-Damri, asking him to marry him to Umm Habibah bint Abi Sufyan, who had emigrated there with her husband, and her husband had died, and to send to him those Muslims who were with him. The Negus sent to Umm Habibah a slave-girl called Abrahah, to inform her of the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ proposal to her. She gave her silver anklets out of joy at that. She authorised Khalid ibn Sa'id ibn al-'As to marry her to him, for a dowry of four hundred dinars. The Negus, may Allah have mercy on him, was the one who proposed on behalf of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Negus sent four hundred dinars to her by means of Abrahah. When she came to her with them, Umm Habibah gave her fifty dinars, but she refused it and said: "The king commanded me not to take anything from you." She said: "I am in charge of the king's oils and garments. I have affirmed Muhammad ﷺ and believed in him. My request of you is that you convey my greetings to him." She said: "Yes." The king had also commanded his wives to send to her whatever aloes-wood and ambergris they had. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would see it upon her and he would not object.

Umm Habibah said: "We went out to Madinah while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was at Khaybar. Those who were to go out to him went out, and I remained in Madinah until the Prophet ﷺ arrived. When the marriage of Umm Habibah reached Abu Sufyan, he said: "That is the stallion whose nose is not rubbed in the dust." [That is, a noble equal who is not rejected.]

After the arrival of Ja'far, the Negus sent to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ his son Azha ibn Ashamah ibn Abjar with sixty men from Abyssinia, and he wrote to him: "O Messenger of Allah, I bear witness that you are the Messenger of Allah, truthful and confirmed. Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: they were forty men, thirty-two from Abyssinia and eight Byzantines from Syria.

[Ata' said: they were eighty men, forty from the people of Najran from the Banu al-Harith ibn Ka'b, thirty-two from Abyssinia and eight Byzantines from Syria.]

Qatadah said: it was revealed concerning some People of the Book who were upon a path of truth from what 'Isa, peace be upon him, had brought. When Allah sent Muhammad ﷺ, they affirmed him and believed in him, and so Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, praised them for that.

the polytheists of Makkah, when they went out to them to gather an army against the Prophet ﷺ. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and al-Hasan said: "Among them," meaning among the hypocrites, ﴿turning in friendship to the Jews﴾. ﴿Evil is what their souls have sent ahead for them﴾: evil is what they had sent ahead of deeds for their return in the Hereafter, ﴿that Allah has become angry with them﴾: Allah became wrathful with them, ﴿and in punishment they will abide forever﴾.

﴿And if they had believed in Allah and the Prophet﴾ Muhammad ﷺ, ﴿and in what was revealed to him﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿they would not have taken them as allies﴾, meaning the disbelievers, ﴿but many of them are defiantly disobedient﴾, that is, they depart from the command of Allah, glorified and exalted is He.

Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿You will surely find the most intense of people in enmity toward the believers to be the Jews and those who associate others with Allah﴾, meaning the polytheists of the Arabs, ﴿and you will find the nearest of them in affection to the believers those who say, "We are Christians"﴾. It does not mean all Christians, because in their enmity toward the Muslims they are like the Jews in killing the Muslims, taking them captive, ruining their lands, demolishing their mosques and burning their copies of the Qur'an. [And it was said: it was revealed concerning all Jews and all Christians, because the Jews are harder of heart and the Christians are softer of heart than them, and they were less inclined to back the polytheists than the Jews.]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 5, verses 82–83:

﴿And when they hear what has been sent down to the Messenger﴾ Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿you see their eyes overflowing﴾ flowing, ﴿with tears because of what they have recognized of the truth﴾. Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said, in the narration of 'Ata': "He means the Negus (al-Najashi) and his companions. Ja'far recited to them in Abyssinia: Kaf, Ha, Ya, 'Ayn, Sad (Kaf-Ha-Ya-'Ayn-Sad), and they did not stop weeping until Ja'far finished the recitation."

﴿They say, "Our Lord, we have believed, so register us among the witnesses."﴾

That is, the community of Muhammad (ﷺ). The evidence for this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That you may be witnesses over the people﴾ (al-Baqarah, 143).

﴿And why should we not believe in Allah and what has come to us of the truth?﴾ This is because the Jews reproached them and said to them, "Why have you believed?" So they answered them with this. ﴿And we hope that our Lord will admit us along with the righteous people﴾, meaning: among the community of Muhammad (ﷺ). Its explanation is (His saying): ﴿That the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants﴾ (al-Anbiya', 105).

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 5, verses 82–83:

﴿And when they hear what has been sent down to the Messenger﴾ Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿you see their eyes overflowing﴾ flowing, ﴿with tears because of what they have recognized of the truth﴾. ﴿فَأَثَابَهُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ Allah gave them ﴿بِمَا قَالُوا جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا﴾ *(in return for what they said: gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein)*. Allah made their statement effective, and He tied the reward to the statement because it was accompanied by sincerity (ikhlas). The evidence is His saying: ﴿وَذَلِكَ جَزَاءُ الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾ *(and that is the recompense of the doers of good)*, meaning the monotheists, the believers. His earlier saying: "Their eyes overflow with tears because of the truth they have recognized" indicates that sincerity and knowledge in the heart, together with the spoken word, constitute faith (iman).

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تُحَرِّمُوا طَيِّبَاتِ مَا أَحَلَّ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ﴾ *(O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things which Allah has made lawful for you)*, the verse. The people of tafsir (ahl al-tafsir) said: The Prophet (ﷺ) once reminded the people and described the Resurrection, and the people were moved and wept. Ten of his Companions gathered in the house of Uthman ibn Maz'un al-Jumahi. They were Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him; Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him; Abdullah ibn Mas'ud; Abdullah ibn Umar; Abu Dharr al-Ghifari; Salim, the freed slave of Abu Hudhayfah; al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad; Salman al-Farisi; and Ma'qil ibn Muqarrin, may Allah be pleased with them all. They consulted together and agreed to practise monasticism (tarahhub), to wear hair shirts (al-musuh), to castrate themselves (yajubbu madhakirahum), to fast continually, to stand in prayer through the night without sleeping on beds, to abstain from eating meat and fat (al-wadak), to abstain from women and perfume, and to wander through the earth (yasihu fi al-ard). This reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so he went to the house of Uthman ibn Maz'un but did not find him. He said to his wife Umm Hakim bint Abi Umayyah, whose name was al-Khawla and who was a perfume seller: "Is it true what has reached me about your husband and his companions?" She disliked to lie to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and she disliked to expose her husband, so she said: "O Messenger of Allah, if Uthman has told you something, then he has told you the truth." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then left. When Uthman entered, she informed him of this, so he and his companions came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "Was I not told that you agreed upon such and such?" They said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah, and we intended only good." He (ﷺ) said: "I was not commanded to do that." Then he said: "Indeed your souls have a right over you, so fast and break your fast, stand in prayer and sleep, for I stand in prayer and sleep, I fast and break my fast, I eat meat and fat, and I approach women. Whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not of me." Then he gathered the people and addressed them, saying: "What is the matter with people who forbid women, food, perfume, sleep, and the desires of [women] [[In "B": (the world).]]? As for me, I do not order you to become priests (qissisin) and monks (ruhban). There is no abandoning meat and women in my religion, nor taking up monastic cells (sawami'). The wandering (siyahah) of my community is fasting, and their monasticism is jihad. Worship Allah and do not associate anything with Him; perform Hajj and Umrah, establish the prayer, give zakah, fast Ramadan, and be upright, and you will be made upright. Those before you were destroyed only through severity: they were severe upon themselves, so Allah was severe upon them, and their remnants are in the dwellings and the monastic cells." Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed this verse [[See: Tafsir al-Tabari: 7/8-11; al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/141-142; Asbab al-Nuzul (236-237).]].

Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Tawbah al-Kushmihani informed us: Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Harith informed us: Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kisai informed us: Abdullah ibn Mahmud informed us: Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Khallal informed us: Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Rishdin ibn Sa'd, who said: Ibn An'um narrated to me, from Sa'd ibn Mas'ud, that Uthman ibn Maz'un, may Allah be pleased with him, came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "Permit us to castrate ourselves (al-ikhtisa')." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "He is not of us who castrates or who has himself castrated; the castration of my community is fasting." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, permit us to wander (al-siyahah)." He said: "The wandering of my community is jihad in the way of Allah." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, permit us to practise monasticism (al-tarahhub)." He said: "The monasticism of my community is sitting in the mosques and waiting for the prayer" [[Recorded by the author (al-Musannif) in Sharh al-Sunnah: 2/270-271, and in Masabih al-Sunnah: 1/225 (Mishkat al-Masabih). The hadith is weak, due to the weakness of Rishdin ibn Sa'd and Ziyad ibn An'um al-Ifriqi. The second part of the hadith, "The wandering of my community...", has a witness in Abu Dawud, from the hadith of Abu Umamah, in the Book of Jihad, chapter on the prohibition of wandering: 3/357. See also: al-Silsilah al-Da'ifah: 3/479-480; Mishkat al-Masabih: 1/225; Majma' al-Zawa'id: 4/254.]].

It is narrated from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have eaten meat and become excited and overcome by desire, so I have forbidden meat," and Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تُحَرِّمُوا طَيِّبَاتِ مَا أَحَلَّ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ﴾ [[Recorded by al-Tirmidhi in Tafsir, Surah al-Ma'idah: 8/415, and he said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith. Some of them narrated it as mursal, without mention of Ibn Abbas. Khalid al-Hadhdha' narrated it from Ikrimah as mursal." al-Wahidi recorded it with its chain in Asbab al-Nuzul: p. 236. al-Tabari recorded in Tafsir: 7/8 the narration to which al-Tirmidhi alluded. al-Suyuti also attributed it to Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh. See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/139; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 6/260.]]

﴿فَأَثَابَهُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ Allah gave them ﴿بِمَا قَالُوا جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا﴾ *(in return for what they said: gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein)*. Allah made their statement effective, and He tied the reward to the statement because it was accompanied by sincerity (ikhlas). The evidence is His saying: ﴿وَذَلِكَ جَزَاءُ الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾ *(and that is the recompense of the doers of good)*, meaning the monotheists, the believers. His earlier saying: "Their eyes overflow with tears because of the truth they have recognized" indicates that sincerity and knowledge in the heart, together with the spoken word, constitute faith (iman).

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تُحَرِّمُوا طَيِّبَاتِ مَا أَحَلَّ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ﴾ *(O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things which Allah has made lawful for you)*, the verse. The people of tafsir (ahl al-tafsir) said: The Prophet (ﷺ) once reminded the people and described the Resurrection, and the people were moved and wept. Ten of his Companions gathered in the house of Uthman ibn Maz'un al-Jumahi. They were Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him; Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him; Abdullah ibn Mas'ud; Abdullah ibn Umar; Abu Dharr al-Ghifari; Salim, the freed slave of Abu Hudhayfah; al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad; Salman al-Farisi; and Ma'qil ibn Muqarrin, may Allah be pleased with them all. They consulted together and agreed to practise monasticism (tarahhub), to wear hair shirts (al-musuh), to castrate themselves (yajubbu madhakirahum), to fast continually, to stand in prayer through the night without sleeping on beds, to abstain from eating meat and fat (al-wadak), to abstain from women and perfume, and to wander through the earth (yasihu fi al-ard). This reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so he went to the house of Uthman ibn Maz'un but did not find him. He said to his wife Umm Hakim bint Abi Umayyah, whose name was al-Khawla and who was a perfume seller: "Is it true what has reached me about your husband and his companions?" She disliked to lie to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and she disliked to expose her husband, so she said: "O Messenger of Allah, if Uthman has told you something, then he has told you the truth." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then left. When Uthman entered, she informed him of this, so he and his companions came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "Was I not told that you agreed upon such and such?" They said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah, and we intended only good." He (ﷺ) said: "I was not commanded to do that." Then he said: "Indeed your souls have a right over you, so fast and break your fast, stand in prayer and sleep, for I stand in prayer and sleep, I fast and break my fast, I eat meat and fat, and I approach women. Whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not of me." Then he gathered the people and addressed them, saying: "What is the matter with people who forbid women, food, perfume, sleep, and the desires of [women] [[In "B": (the world).]]? As for me, I do not order you to become priests (qissisin) and monks (ruhban). There is no abandoning meat and women in my religion, nor taking up monastic cells (sawami'). The wandering (siyahah) of my community is fasting, and their monasticism is jihad. Worship Allah and do not associate anything with Him; perform Hajj and Umrah, establish the prayer, give zakah, fast Ramadan, and be upright, and you will be made upright. Those before you were destroyed only through severity: they were severe upon themselves, so Allah was severe upon them, and their remnants are in the dwellings and the monastic cells." Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed this verse [[See: Tafsir al-Tabari: 7/8-11; al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/141-142; Asbab al-Nuzul (236-237).]].

The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 5, verse 88:

That is: the pleasures that souls desire, of what has been made lawful for you among the good foods and the delicious drinks. ﴿And do not transgress﴾, meaning: do not go beyond the lawful to the unlawful. It was also said: it refers to castration (jabb al-madhakir). ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love the transgressors.﴾

﴿And eat of what Allah has provided for you, lawful and good.﴾ ʿAbdullah ibn al-Mubarak said: "The lawful (halal) is what you take from its proper source, and the good (tayyib) is what nourishes and makes grow. As for solid things such as clay and dust, and whatever does not nourish, they are disliked, except for the purpose of treatment."

﴿And fear Allah, in whom you are believers.﴾ Abu Muhammad ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAbd al-Samad al-Jawzajani informed us: Abu al-Qasim ʿAli ibn Ahmad al-Khuzaʿi informed us: Abu Saʿid al-Haytham ibn Kulayb informed us: Abu ʿIsa al-Tirmidhi informed us: Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Dawraqi, Salama ibn Shabib and Mahmud ibn Ghaylan informed us, saying: Abu Usama informed us, from Hisham ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, from ʿA'isha (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) used to love sweets (al-halwa') and honey." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Ashriba, chapter on al-Baadhiq and on whoever forbade every intoxicant among drinks: 10/62; and the author in Sharh al-Sunna: 11/308.]

(﴿Allah will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths, but He will hold you accountable for what you have intended in the oaths. Its expiation is feeding ten needy people from the average of what you feed your families, or clothing them, or freeing a slave. But whoever cannot find [means], then fasting for three days. That is the expiation of your oaths when you have sworn. And guard your oaths. Thus Allah makes clear to you His verses that you may be grateful.﴾ (89))

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Allah will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: When the verse ﴿Do not forbid the good things that Allah has made lawful for you﴾ was revealed, they said: "O Messenger of Allah, how shall we deal with our oaths that we have sworn?" They had sworn to what they had agreed upon. So Allah revealed: ﴿Allah will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths﴾. [Narrated by al-Tabari: 7/13. See also Asbab al-Nuzul (237).] ﴿But He will hold you accountable for what you have intended in the oaths﴾. Hamza, al-Kisa'i and [Abu Bakr] [Omitted from "b".] read ʿaqqadtum (ʿaqqadtum) with a light pronunciation (taskhif)... Ibn ʿAmir read ʿaqqadtum with an alif (ʿaqadtum), and the rest read ʿaqqadtum with shadda (tashdid), meaning: confirmed (wakkadtum). The meaning of the verse is: you intended and deliberately resolved. ﴿Its expiation﴾, meaning: the expiation for what you have bound by oaths when you break them. ﴿Feeding ten needy people﴾. The scholars differed concerning its measure. Some held that one feeds each needy person a mudd of food by the mudd of the Prophet (ﷺ), which is a ratl and a third of the staple food of the land. The same applies to all expiations. This is the view of Zayd ibn Thabit, Ibn ʿAbbas and Ibn ʿUmar, and Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab, al-Qasim, Sulayman ibn al-Yasar, ʿAta' and al-Hasan also said so.

The people of Iraq said: for each needy person there are two mudds, which is half a sa', and this is related from ʿUmar and ʿAli (may Allah be pleased with them both).

Abu Hanifa said: if he feeds [them] from wheat, then half a sa'; and if from other than wheat, then a sa'. This is the view of al-Shaʿbi, al-Nakhaʿi, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Mujahid and al-Hakam.

If he gives them lunch and dinner, it is not permissible; Abu Hanifa permitted it, and this is related from ʿAli (may Allah be pleased with him).

Dirhams and dinars are not permissible, nor is bread or flour; rather it is obligatory to give grain to them. Abu Hanifa (may Allah be pleased with him) permitted all of that.

If he gives the whole [amount] to one needy person [it is not permissible]. [Omitted from "b".] Abu Hanifa permitted giving the food of ten to one needy person over ten days. It is not permissible to give it except to a free Muslim who is needy. If it is given to a dhimmi, a slave or a wealthy person, it is not permissible. Abu Hanifa permitted giving it to the people of the dhimma. They agreed that giving zakat to the people of the dhimma is not permissible.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿from the average of what you feed your families﴾, meaning: from the best of the staple food of your dependents. ʿUbayda al-Salmani said: "The average is bread and vinegar; the best is bread and meat; and the lowest is plain bread with [something]; and all of it suffices." [In "b": (mujziʾ).]

The words of the Exalted: ﴿or clothing them﴾. Everyone who is obligated to the expiation of an oath has a choice in it: if he wishes he feeds ten of the needy, and if he wishes he clothes them, and if he wishes he frees a slave. If he chooses clothing, they differed concerning its measure.

Some held that he clothes each needy person with one garment of what falls under the name of clothing: a waist-wrap (izar), a cloak (rida'), a shirt (qamis), trousers (sarawil), a turban (ʿimama), a cloak (kisa') or the like. This is the view of Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Hasan, Mujahid, ʿAta' and Tawus, and al-Shafiʿi (may Allah have mercy on him) went to it.

Malik said: it is obligatory for each person what makes his prayer valid, so he clothes the men with one garment and the women with two: a dir' (long shirt) and a khimar (headcover).

Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab said: for each needy person, two garments.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿or freeing a slave﴾. If he chooses manumission, it is obligatory to free a believing slave. Likewise, all expiations, such as the expiation for killing, for zihar and for intercourse during the day in Ramadan, require freeing a believing slave. Abu Hanifa (may Allah be pleased with him) and al-Thawri (may Allah be pleased with him) permitted freeing a disbelieving slave in all of these except the expiation for killing, because Allah restricted the slave there by faith. We say: the unrestricted (mutlaq) is understood in light of the restricted (muqayyad) [just as Allah restricted testimony by justice in one place, saying: "And call to witness two just men from among you" (al-Talaq, 2), and left it unrestricted in another place, saying: "And call to witness two men from among your men" (al-Baqara, 282). Then justice is a condition in all of them, by understanding the unrestricted in light of the restricted]. [What is between the brackets is omitted from "b".] So it is likewise here. And it is not permissible, by consensus, to free an apostate for the expiation.

It is required that the slave be free of slavery's encumbrances. So if he frees, for his expiation, a mukatab (a slave contracted to buy his freedom), or an umm walad (a slave-mother), or a slave he bought with the condition of manumission, or a relative who becomes free upon him (by ownership), intending it as expiation, he does free them, but it is not valid for the expiation. The people of opinion (ashab al-ra'y) permitted freeing a mukatab if he had paid nothing of the installments, and freeing a relative for the expiation.

It is required that the slave be sound from every defect that harms work with clear harm, so a person with one hand cut off or one foot cut off is not permissible, nor is a blind person, nor a chronically disabled person, nor a person permanently insane. One-eyed, deaf, or one whose two ears or nose are cut off is permissible, because these defects do not harm work with clear harm.

According to Abu Hanifa (may Allah be pleased with him), every defect that eliminates a kind of benefit [in full] prevents validity. So he permitted one whose one hand is cut off, but did not permit one whose two ears are cut off.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿So whoever does not find [means], then fasting three days﴾. If the one obligated for the expiation of an oath is unable to feed, clothe, or free a slave, it is obligatory on him to fast three days. Inability means that he does not have in his wealth beyond his sustenance, the sustenance of his dependents and his needs, enough to feed, clothe or free; then he fasts three days.

Some said: if he owns what enables him to feed, even if it is not beyond his sufficiency, then he may not fast. This is the view of al-Hasan and Saʿid ibn Jubayr.

They differed concerning the obligation of consecutiveness (tatabuʿ) in this fast. A group held that consecutiveness is not obligatory in it; rather, if he wishes he makes it consecutive and if he wishes he separates it; consecutiveness is better, and this is one of al-Shafiʿi's two opinions. Some held that consecutiveness is obligatory in it, by analogy with the expiation for killing and zihar, and this is the view of al-Thawri and Abu Hanifa. It is supported by the reading of Ibn Masʿud (may Allah be pleased with him): "fasting three days, consecutive" (muttabiʿat).

﴿That﴾, meaning: that which I have mentioned, ﴿is the expiation of your oaths when you have sworn﴾ and broken them, for the expiation is obligatory only after breaking the oath.

They differed concerning advancing the expiation before breaking the oath. Some held that it is permissible, based on what we have related: that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever swears an oath and then sees something other than it to be better, let him expiate for his oath and let him do what is better." [Narrated by Muslim in al-Aymān, chapter on urging one who swears an oath and sees something else better to do what is better..., no. (1650): 3/1272; and the author in Sharh al-Sunna: 10/17.] This is the view of ʿUmar [and Ibn ʿUmar] [Omitted from "b".], Ibn ʿAbbas and ʿA'isha, and al-Hasan and Ibn Sirin said so, and Malik, al-Awza'i and al-Shafiʿi went to it, except that al-Shafiʿi says: if he expiates by fasting before breaking the oath, it is not permissible, because it is a bodily act; it is permissible only with feeding, clothing or freeing, just as advancing zakat before the year is permissible, but advancing the fasting of Ramadan before its time is not. Some held that advancing the expiation before breaking the oath is not permissible, and Abu Hanifa (may Allah be pleased with him) said so.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And guard your oaths﴾. It was said: he intends by it leaving off swearing, i.e., do not swear. It was also said, and this is the more correct: he intends by it: when you swear, do not break them. So what is meant by it is guarding the oath against breaking. This applies when the oath was not on abandoning what is recommended (mandub) or doing what is disliked (makruh). If he swears to do what is disliked or to abandon what is recommended, then it is better that he breaks his oath himself and expiates, because of what ʿAbd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us: Ahmad ibn ʿAbdullah al-Nuʿaymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Hajjaj ibn Minhal informed us: Jarir ibn Hazim informed us, from al-Hasan, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Samura, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Samura, do not ask for leadership, for if you are given it because you asked, you will be left to it; and if it is given to you without asking, you will be helped in it. And when you swear an oath and then see something else better than it, expiate for your oath and do what is better." [Narrated by Imam Muslim in al-Aymān, in the previous place, no. (1652): 3/1273-1274; and in al-Imara: 3/1456; and the author in Sharh al-Sunna 10/56, except for his saying "And when you swear an oath..."]

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Thus Allah makes clear to you His verses that you may be grateful.﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 5, verse 89:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, indeed, intoxicants, gambling, [sacrificial] stones, and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it that you may be successful.﴾ "Al-maysir" means al-qimar (gambling). ﴿Al-ansab﴾ means the idols; they were so called because they used to set them up (yansibunaha). Its singular is nasb, with a fatha on the nun and a sukun on the sad, and nusb, with a damma on the nun, both lightened and emphasized. ﴿Al-azlam﴾ means the arrows with which they used to seek decisions (yastaqsimuna), its singular being zalam. ﴿Rijs﴾ means filthy, loathsome, repugnant. ﴿From the work of Satan﴾ means from his adornment of it. ﴿So avoid it﴾: the pronoun refers back to rijs. ﴿That you may be successful﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 5, verses 90–91:

As for the enmity caused by intoxicants, when drinkers become intoxicated they become rowdy and quarrel, as the Ansari man did when he struck Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas with a jawbone at the Battle of the Camel. As for the enmity caused by gambling, Qatadah said: "A man would gamble away his family and his wealth, and then he would remain grieved, deprived of his family and his wealth, and enraged at his [ḥurafa'] [[In "B" (ḥu'fanah).]]."

﴿And it prevents you from the remembrance of Allah and from prayer.﴾ This is because whoever occupies himself with drinking intoxicants or gambling is diverted by it from the remembrance of Allah, and it disrupts his prayer, as happened with the guests of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf. A man stepped forward to lead them in the maghrib prayer after they had drunk, and he recited "Say: O you disbelievers, I worship what you worship," omitting the negative particle [lā] [[See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/164.]].

﴿So will you not desist?﴾ That is, "Desist!" The interrogative form carries the meaning of a command, as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿So will you not be grateful?﴾ (Surat al-Anbiya', 80).

﴿And obey Allah and obey the Messenger and beware﴾ of the prohibited things and the forbidden acts. ﴿But if you turn away, then know that upon Our Messenger is only the clear delivery.﴾

Regarding the threat against the drinker of intoxicants, Abu al-Qasim 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Furani informed us: Abu al-Hasan 'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah al-Taysafuni informed us: Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Mahmud al-Mahmudi informed us: Abu al-'Abbas al-Masarjisi informed us at Nishapur: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali informed us: Salih ibn Qudamah informed us: my brother 'Abd al-Malik ibn Qudamah narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Dinar, from Ibn 'Umar, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "Every intoxicant is forbidden. And whoever drinks it in this world without repenting, Allah will give him to drink from the clay of al-Khabal on the Day of Resurrection." They asked: "Do you know what the clay of al-Khabal is?" He said: "It is the sweat of the people of the Fire." [[Reported by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 11/356. In its chain is 'Abd al-Malik ibn Qudamah, who is weak. It is supported by several authentic hadiths from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah and others, including the hadith of Jabir in Muslim, no. (2002), in the book of drinks, and the hadith of Ibn 'Umar in Muslim, no. (2003), which follows.]]

And Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Nafi', from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever drinks wine in this world and does not repent of it, will be deprived of it in the Hereafter." [[Reported by Muslim in the book of drinks, chapter on the punishment of one who drinks wine and does not repent..., no. (2003): 3/1588, and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 11/355.]]

And Abu Sa'id al-Shurayhi informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us: Ahmad ibn Ubayy informed us: Abu al-'Abbas al-Asamm informed us: Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Saghani narrated to us: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Abd Allah al-Ghafiqi, of the people of Egypt, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, that he said: "I bear witness that I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Allah has cursed wine, its drinker, its server, its seller, its buyer, its presser, the one for whom it is pressed, its carrier, the one to whom it is carried, and the one who consumes its price.'" [[Reported by Abu Dawud in the book of drinks, chapter on grape-pressing for wine: 5/260; Ibn Majah in the book of drinks, chapter on the curse upon wine in ten aspects, no. (3380): 2/1121; and Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 2/97. In it is 'Abd al-Rahman al-Ghafiqi. Al-Mundhiri said: Ibn Ma'in was asked about him and said, "I do not know him." Ibn Yunus mentioned him in his History and said: he narrated from Ibn 'Umar. Abu Tu'mah: Makhul accused him of lying. The hadith has supporting reports which strengthen it. Therefore, al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in Talkhis al-Habir (4/73): "Ibn al-Sakan authenticated it. On this subject there is also a report from Anas ibn Malik, narrated by al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah, whose narrators are trustworthy; and from Ibn 'Abbas, narrated by Ahmad, Ibn Hibban and al-Hakim; and from Ibn Mas'ud, mentioned by Ibn Abi Hatim in al-'Ilal; and from Abu Hurayrah, raised to the Prophet: 'Allah has forbidden wine and its price, and has forbidden carrion and its price, and has forbidden swine and its price.' Abu Dawud narrated it; and from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As."]]
