The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 5, verses 92–93:

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten﴾. The occasion of revelation of this verse is that the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, said when the prohibition of wine was revealed: "O Messenger of Allah, what about our brothers who"

The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 5, verses 92–93:

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten﴾. The occasion of revelation of this verse is that the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, said when the prohibition of wine was revealed: "O Messenger of Allah, what about our brothers who"

They died while drinking wine [and eating] [[In MS "b": "and they ate"]] from the proceeds of gambling (maysir)?" So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have consumed﴾ of wine and eaten from the proceeds of gambling, ﴿if they fear Allah﴾ by avoiding shirk, ﴿and believe﴾ and affirm, ﴿and do righteous deeds, then fear Allah﴾ by avoiding wine and gambling after they were forbidden, ﴿and believe, then fear Allah﴾ by avoiding what Allah has forbidden them to eat and drink, ﴿and do good, for Allah loves the doers of good﴾. It was also said: the meaning of the first is "if they avoided shirk and believed and affirmed, then feared Allah," meaning they persisted in that taqwa (God-consciousness). ﴿And believe﴾ means they increased in faith, then they avoided all sins and did good. It was also said: the meaning is "they feared Allah through doing good, and every doer of good is God-conscious," ﴿and Allah loves the doers of good﴾.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿O you who believe, Allah will surely test you with something of the game﴾, to the end of the verse. It was revealed in the year of al-Hudaybiyah, when they were in the state of ihram (ritual sanctity for pilgrimage). Allah tested them with game, and the wild animals would come right up to their camps because of their great number, so they intended to take them. Then this was revealed. ﴿Allah will surely test you﴾ means Allah will examine you. The purpose of the test is to make apparent the obedient from the disobedient, since Allah has no need of testing by means of game. He said "with something" (bi-shay'in) as a partial reference because He tested them only with land game.

﴿Your hands can reach﴾ means the young birds, the eggs, and the young game that cannot flee. ﴿And your spears﴾ means the large game. ﴿That Allah may know﴾ means that Allah may see, since He already knows. ﴿Who fears Him unseen﴾ means who fears Allah while not seeing Him, as in His saying: ﴿those who fear their Lord unseen﴾ (al-Anbiya', 49), meaning he fears Him and so does not hunt while in ihram. ﴿So whoever transgresses after that﴾ means whoever hunts after it has been forbidden, ﴿for him is a painful punishment﴾. It is narrated from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, that he said: his back and his belly are struck with lashes until he is in pain, and his garments are taken.

(O you who believe, do not kill game while you are in the state of ihram. Whoever of you kills it intentionally, its compensation is an equivalent of what he killed from the livestock, judged by two just men among you, as an offering reaching the Ka'bah, or an expiation of feeding the needy, or its equivalent in fasting, that he may taste the consequence of his deed. Allah has pardoned what has passed. But whoever returns, Allah will take retribution from him, and Allah is Exalted in Might, the Possessor of Retribution (95).)

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿O you who believe, do not kill game while you are in the state of ihram﴾, meaning while you are in the state of ihram for hajj and 'umrah. The word is the plural of ḥarām (sacred/in a state of prohibition). It is said: a man is ḥarām and a woman is ḥarām. It can also mean entering the Sacred Precinct (al-ḥaram). It is said: aḥrama al-rajul when he tied the ihram, and aḥrama when he entered the Ḥaram. It was revealed concerning a man called Abu al-Yusr who rushed at a wild ass while in ihram and killed it.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And whoever of you kills it intentionally﴾. They differed concerning this intention. One group said: it is intentional killing of game while forgetting the ihram. But if he kills it intentionally while remembering his ihram, there is no ruling upon him, and his matter is left to Allah, since it is too grave for there to be an expiation for it. This is the view of Mujahid and al-Hasan.

Others said: it is that the muhrim deliberately sets out to kill game while remembering his ihram, and then the expiation is upon him.

They differed regarding if he killed it by mistake. Most jurists held that intentional and unintentional killing are equal in requiring expiation. Al-Zuhri said: for the intentional one it is from the Book, and for the mistaken one it is from the Sunnah. Sa'id ibn Jubayr [MS "b": al-Musayyib] said: the expiation for game is not required for killing by mistake; it applies only to the intentional.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Then the compensation is an equivalent﴾. The people of Kufa and Ya'qub read fa-jazā'un (with tanwīn, indefinite), and mithlu is raised as a substitution (badal) for jazā'. The others read it with the genitive construction: fa-jazā'u mithli (the compensation of the equivalent) ﴿of what he killed from the livestock﴾. Its meaning is that it is required of him to offer an equivalent of that game from the livestock. He meant by this the animal closest to the game killed in resemblance in terms of form, not in terms of value.

﴿Judged by two just men among you﴾ means the compensation is judged by two just men, who should be jurists who look at the animal among livestock most similar to the game and judge by it. Among those who held that the equivalent from livestock is required were Umar, Uthman, Ali, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, Ibn Umar, Ibn Abbas, and other Companions, may Allah be pleased with them all. In different regions and various times they judged by an equivalent from livestock. A judge would rule for an ostrich with a camel, though it is not worth a camel; for a wild ass with a cow, though it is not worth a cow; and for a hyena with a ram, though it is not worth a ram. This shows that they looked at what is close to the game in resemblance of form [not in value]. For pigeons a sheep is required. This refers to every bird that coos and cries, such as the fakhitah and the qumri (dove).

It is narrated from Umar, Uthman and Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them, that they ruled for a pigeon of Makkah a sheep. Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Mus'ab, from Malik, from Abu al-Zubayr al-Makki, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, that Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, ruled concerning the hyena with a ram, for the gazelle with a she-goat, for the hare with a young goat (anaq), and for the jerboa with a jafrah [[Narrated by Malik in al-Muwatta', Kitab al-Hajj, Bab fidyat ma usiba min al-tayr wa al-wahsh: 1/414; al-Shafi'i in al-Musnad: 1/330-331; al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan: 5/183; authenticated by al-Albani in Irwa' al-Ghalil: 4/245; see also Talkhis al-Habir: 2/278.]].

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿as an offering reaching the Ka'bah﴾ means he brings that expiation as an offering to the Ka'bah, slaughtering it in Makkah and giving its meat in charity to the needy of the Sacred Precinct. ﴿Or an expiation of feeding the needy, or its equivalent in fasting﴾. Al-Farra', may Allah have mercy on him, said: al-'adl with a kasra (ʿidl) is the equivalent of the same kind, and al-'adl with a fatḥa (ʿadl) is the equivalent of a different kind. He meant by this: in the compensation for game one has the choice between slaughtering the equivalent from livestock and giving its meat in charity to the needy of the Sacred Precinct, or valuing the equivalent in dirhams, and using the dirhams for food, giving the food in charity to the needy of the Sacred Precinct, or fasting one day for each mudd (measure) of food. He may fast wherever he wishes, since there is no benefit in it for the needy.

Malik said: if he does not give the equivalent, he values the game, then makes the value into food and gives it in charity, or he fasts.

Abu Hanifah, may Allah be pleased with him, said: the equivalent from livestock is not required; rather, one values the game. If he wishes, he spends that value on some livestock; if he wishes, on food, which he gives in charity; and if he wishes, he fasts one day for every half sa' of wheat or one sa' of other food.

Al-Sha'bi and al-Nakha'i said: the compensation for game is in the order (tartib) [that is, in sequence]. The verse is evidence for those who hold to the option (takhyir).

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿that he may taste the consequence of his deed﴾ means the requital of his disobedience. ﴿Allah has pardoned what has passed﴾ means before the prohibition and the revelation of the verse. Al-Suddi said: Allah has pardoned what passed in the Jahiliyyah. ﴿But whoever returns, Allah will take retribution from him﴾ in the Hereafter.

﴿And Allah is Exalted in Might, the Possessor of Retribution﴾. If the muhrim repeatedly kills game, the compensation is multiplied upon him according to the majority of scholars. Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, said: if the muhrim kills game intentionally, he is asked: "Have you killed any game before it?" If he says yes, no ruling is passed on him, and he is told: "Go, Allah will take retribution from you." If he says he has not killed any before it, a ruling is passed on him. If he returns after that, no ruling is passed on him, but his back and chest are filled with painful beating. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ruled likewise concerning Wajj, a valley in al-Ta'if [[Part of a hadith narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Manasik, Bab fi mal al-Ka'bah: 2/441-442, with the wording "... If the game of Wajj and its thorny trees are sacred, consecrated to Allah..."; and by Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad, no. (1416), ed. al-Halabi, authenticated by Ahmad Shakir. Al-Mundhiri said: its isnad includes Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Insan al-Ta'ifi and his father. As for Muhammad, al-Razi was asked about him and said: "not strong, and his hadith is questionable." Al-Bukhari mentioned him in al-Tarikh al-Kabir 1/1/140 and mentioned this hadith for him, saying: "no one followed him in it." He also mentioned his father and pointed to this hadith, saying: "his hadith is not authentic." Al-Busti said: Abd Allah ibn Insan, whose son Muhammad narrated from him, and his hadith is not authentic. Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in Talkhis al-Habir 2/280: "Abu Dawud was silent on it, al-Tirmidhi graded it hasan, 'Abd al-Haqq was silent on it, al-Dhahabi mentioned that al-Shafi'i authenticated it, and al-Khallal mentioned that Ahmad weakened it." Al-Nawawi said in al-Majmu' 7/449: "Al-Bayhaqi narrated it and its isnad is weak."]].

They differed concerning the muhrim: is it permissible for him to eat the meat of game or not? A group held that it is not lawful for him in any case, and this is narrated from Ibn Abbas. It is also the view of Tawus, and Sufyan al-Thawri said the same. They argued with what Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Mus'ab, from Malik, from Ibn Shihab, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah ibn Utbah ibn Mas'ud, from Abd Allah ibn Abbas, from al-Sa'b ibn Jaththamah al-Laythi, that he gifted the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) a wild ass, while he was at al-Abwa' or Waddan, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned it to him. He said: when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw what was in my face, he said: "We only returned it to you because we are in the state of ihram" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Jaza' al-Sayd, Bab idha uhdiya lil-muhrim himaran wahshiyyan lam yuqbal: 4/31, and in al-Hibah; and by Muslim in al-Hajj, Bab tahrim al-sayd lil-muhrim, no. (1193): 2/850; and by al-Musannif in Sharh al-Sunnah: 7/260.]].

Most scholars held that it is permissible for the muhrim to eat it if he did not hunt it himself, nor was it hunted for his sake, or by his signal. This is the view of Umar, Uthman and Abu Hurayrah, and Ata', Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said the same. It is the position of Malik, al-Shafi'i, Ahmad, Ishaq and the Ashab al-Ra'y (the jurists of opinion). The Prophet (ﷺ) returned it to al-Sa'b ibn Jaththamah only because he thought it had been hunted for his sake.

The evidence for its permissibility is what Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Mus'ab, from Malik, from Abu al-Nadr, mawla of Umar ibn Ubayd Allah al-Taymi, from Nafi', mawla of Abu Qatadah, from Abu Qatadah ibn Rib'i al-Ansari, may Allah be pleased with him, that he was with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) until, when they were on part of the road to Makkah, he fell behind with companions of his who were in ihram, while he was not in ihram. He saw a wild ass, mounted his horse, and asked his companions to pass him his whip, but they refused. He asked them for his spear, but they refused. So he took it himself and charged at the ass and killed it. Some of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ate from it, and some of them refused. When they reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), they asked him about that, and he said: "It is only a provision (ṭu'mah) which Allah the Exalted has fed you" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Dhaba'ih wa al-Sayd, Bab ma ja'a fi al-tasayyud: 9/613, and by Muslim in al-Hajj, Bab tahrim al-sayd lil-muhrim, no. (1196): 2/852.]].

Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib informed us: Abd al-Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal informed us: Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm informed us: al-Rabi' informed us: al-Shafi'i informed us: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad informed us, from Amr ibn Abi Amr, from al-Muttalib ibn Hantab, from

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 5, verse 95:

On the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The flesh of game is lawful for you while in the state of ihram, so long as you do not hunt it yourselves or have it hunted for you" [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Manasik, chapter on the flesh of game for the muhrim: 2/362, with the wording "The game of the land is lawful for you..", and al-Tirmidhi in al-Hajj, chapter on what has come concerning eating the flesh of game for the muhrim: 3/584, and al-Nasa'i in al-Hajj, chapter on if the muhrim gestures to game and it is killed: 5/187. Ibn Hibban authenticated it, p. (243) of al-Mawarid, and al-Hakim: 1/452, and al-Shafi'i: 1/322-323 (Tartib al-Musnad), and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 7/263-264. Al-Muttalib ibn Hanzab al-Makhzumi: truthful, but he frequently practised tadlis (concealing defects in a chain) and irsal (omitting a narrator). And Amr ibn Abi Amr: disputed, although he is among the narrators of the Two Sahihs. See: Talkhis al-Habir: 2/26.]] Abu Isa (al-Tirmidhi) said: We do not know of al-Muttalib having heard from Jabir ibn Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with him.

If the muhrim destroys some game for which there is no equivalent among livestock, such as an egg or a bird other than the pigeon, then he must pay its value, which is spent on food, and he gives it in charity or fasts one day for each mudd. They differed concerning locusts: a group permitted them for the muhrim, saying that they are from the game of the sea, and this is reported from Ka'b al-Ahbar. Most scholars hold that they are not lawful, so if he kills one, he must give charity. Umar said: for a locust, a date. It is also reported from him and from Ibn Abbas: a handful of food.

﴿Lawful for you is the game of the sea and its food, as a provision for you and for the travellers; but forbidden to you is the game of the land as long as you are in the state of ihram. And fear Allah, to whom you will be gathered.﴾ (5:96)

The words of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Lawful for you is the game of the sea and its food, as a provision for you and for the travellers﴾. By "the sea" is meant all waters. Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Its game is what is caught, and its food is what is cast up by it." And from Ibn Abbas, Ibn Umar and Abu Hurairah: its food is what the water casts up on the shore dead.

Others said: it is its salted [food], and this is the view of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Qatadah and al-Nakha'i.

Mujahid said: its game is its fresh [catch], and its food is its salted [catch]; "a provision for you" means a benefit for you; "and for the travellers" means those passing by.

The totality of sea creatures is of two kinds: fish and other than fish. As for fish, its carrion is lawful, with the variety of its types. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Two carrions and two bloods have been made lawful for us: the two carrions are the fish and the locust, and the two bloods are the liver and the spleen" [[What is between the brackets is from "Sharh al-Sunnah" and from copy "B", and the hadith was narrated by al-Shafi'i in Tartib al-Musnad: 2/173, and Ibn Majah in al-At'imah, chapter on the liver and spleen, no. (3314): 2/1102, and al-Daraqutni in al-Sayd wa al-Dhaba'ih: 4/271-272, and Imam Ahmad: 2/97 from Ibn Umar, traced to the Prophet. Al-Bayhaqi narrated it as a statement of a Companion and said: this is a sound chain, and it is in the sense of the marfu' (traced) report, al-Sunan: 1/254. Al-Zaylai also attributed it to Abd ibn Humayd, and Ibn Hibban in al-Du'afa', and he faulted it by Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, saying: he used to reverse reports without knowing it, until this became frequent in his narrations, raising statements of Companions and attaching broken chains, so he deserved to be abandoned. See: Nasb al-Rayah: 4/201-202. Ibn Hajar also attributed it to Ibn Mardawayh in his Tafsir from Abu Sa'id, traced to the Prophet, and said: al-Daraqutni mentioned it in al-Ilal ... The report as a statement of a Companion, which Abu Hatim and others authenticated, has the force of the traced report, because the statement of a Companion, "it was made lawful for us, and forbidden to us such-and-such," is like his saying "we were commanded such-and-such, and forbidden such-and-such," so this report may be used as evidence, since it has the sense of the traced report. Talkhis al-Habir: 1/26. And the author also narrated it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 11/244.]] There is no difference between its dying from a cause or without a cause. According to Abu Hanifah, it is not lawful unless it dies from a cause, such as striking a rock, or the water receding from it, and the like.

As for other than fish, there are two kinds: one that lives on land, such as the frog and the crab, whose eating is not lawful; and one that lives in the water and lives on land only as one slaughtered. Opinion differs regarding it. A group held that none of them is lawful except fish, and this is the meaning of the view of Abu Hanifah, may Allah be pleased with him. Another group held that all of the carrion of the water is lawful, because all of it is fish, even though their forms differ, such as the jirri, which is called the water-snake and is shaped like a snake; its eating is permissible by consensus. This is the view of Abu Bakr, Umar, Ibn Umar, Ibn Abbas, Zayd ibn Thabit and Abu Hurairah, and Shurayh, al-Hasan and Ata said the same, and it is the view of Malik and the apparent school of al-Shafi'i.

Another group held that whatever has a counterpart on land is eaten, so its carrion from sea animals is lawful, such as the water-cow and the like; and whatever has no eaten counterpart on land, its carrion from sea animals is not lawful, such as the water-dog, the pig, the donkey and the like.

Al-Awza'i said: everything whose life is in the water is lawful. It was said to him: what of the crocodile? He said: yes.

Al-Sha'bi said: If my family ate frogs, I would feed them. Sufyan al-Thawri said: I hope there is no harm in crab.

The apparent meaning of the verse is evidence for those who permit all sea animals, and likewise the hadith. Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Mus'ab related to us from Malik, from Safwan ibn [Salman] [[In "B": (Sulaym).]], from Sa'id ibn Salamah of the family of Banu al-Azraq, that al-Mughirah ibn Abi Burdah, who was of Banu Abd al-Dar, informed him that he heard Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, say: A man asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, we sail in the sea and carry with us a little water; if we perform wudu with it we become thirsty, so may we perform wudu with sea water?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Its water is pure and its carrion is lawful" [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Tahara, chapter on performing wudu with sea water: 1/81, and al-Tirmidhi in al-Tahara, chapter on what has come concerning sea water being pure: 1/225, and said: this is a hasan sahih hadith; and al-Nasa'i in al-Tahara, chapter on sea water: 1/50, and Ibn Majah in al-Tahara, chapter on performing wudu with sea water: 1/50, and Malik in al-Muwatta: 1/22, and al-Hakim authenticated it: 1/140-141, and Ibn Hibban no. (119), and al-Shafi'i: 1/23 (Tartib al-Musnad) and al-Daraqutni: 1/34-35, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 2/55. See Talkhis al-Habir: 1/9-12.]].

Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Musaddad informed us: Yahya related to us from Ibn Juraij: Umar informed me that he heard Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, say: "We went on the expedition of the Army of Khabt, and Abu Ubaydah was appointed commander. We suffered severe hunger, and the sea cast up a dead fish the like of which we had never seen, called al-Anbar. We ate from it for half a month. Abu Ubaydah took one of its bones, and a rider passed beneath it." And Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir say: Abu Ubaydah said: "Eat." When we came to Madinah we mentioned that to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "Eat the provision Allah brought out for you; feed us if you have any of it." Then some of them brought him some of it and he ate it [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Maghazi, chapter on the expedition of Sayf al-Bahr: 8/78, the wording being his, and Muslim in al-Sayd wa al-Dhaba'ih, chapter on the permissibility of the carrion of the sea, no. (1935): 3/1535, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 11/246. Some people may be astonished at the enormity of this creature, and some may suppose there is exaggeration in it, and this may drive them to deny the report. Here we are before an authentic text and a truthful testimony: the hadith is sound in its chain, as al-Bukhari and Muslim agreed upon its narration, and both are at the highest degree of authenticity; and the hadith is sound in its text, and here is a nearby example from the wonders of Allah's creation that shows this, mentioned by the late Muhammad Fu'ad Abd al-Baqi in Sahih Muslim, in the volume he devoted to the indexes: 5/586: (1) Al-Ahram, the Cairo newspaper, in issue (24419), dated 27/9/1953, page two, column 7, under the heading "Jonah's whale": yesterday a transport vehicle thirty metres long, said to be the longest transport vehicle in the world, passed through the streets of Paris, carrying "Jonah," a huge whale eighteen months old, twenty metres long and weighing eight thousand kilograms. Its owners had it embalmed and exhibited it to spectators in Norway, Sweden, Denmark, Austria and Germany, and it will be displayed in Paris this week for a known fee. Its interior was lit with electric lamps so that spectators could see its belly. (2) The newspaper "al-Akhbar al-Jadidah," issue (396), dated 27/9/1953, page two, columns 1 and 2, under the heading: "A whale twenty metres long and weighing eight tons: people enter its belly, (10) at a time: Paris: this morning 'Una' entered Paris like conquerors, guarded by dozens of police, mounted and on foot. As for this 'Una': it is a huge Norwegian whale..." Then it continued describing the whale, saying: people are allowed to enter its lit stomach, and ten persons can enter its belly at once... etc.]].

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And forbidden to you is the game of the land as long as you are in the state of ihram, and fear Allah, to whom you will be gathered﴾ 112/b. The game of the sea is lawful for the muhrim, as it is lawful for one who is not in ihram. As for the game of the land, it is forbidden for the muhrim and within the Sacred Precinct (al-Haram). Game (sayd) is the wild animal whose flesh is lawful to eat. As for what is not lawful to eat, it is not forbidden because of ihram; the muhrim may take it and kill it, and there is no compensation for killing it, except the hybrid between an animal whose flesh is not eaten and one that is eaten, such as the hybrid between a wolf and a gazelle, which is not lawful to eat, and for which the muhrim who kills it must pay compensation, because it contains a part of game.

Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Mus'ab related to us from Malik, from Nafi', from Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Five of the creatures, there is no sin upon the muhrim for killing them: the crow, the kite, the scorpion, the rat and the rabid dog" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Jaza' al-Sayd, chapter on what the muhrim may kill of creatures: 4/34, and in Bad' al-Khalq, and Muslim in al-Hajj, chapter on what is recommended for the muhrim and others to kill of creatures in the lawful and sacred areas, no. (1199): 2/857. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 7/266.]].

It is also reported from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "The muhrim may kill the hostile predator" [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Manasik, chapter on what the muhrim may kill of creatures: 2/360, in full, and al-Tirmidhi in al-Hajj, chapter on what the muhrim may kill of creatures: 3/577, and said: this is a hasan hadith; and Ibn Majah in al-Manasik, chapter on what the muhrim may kill: 2/1032, and Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 3/3, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 7/267. Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in Talkhis al-Habir: 2/274: "Its chain contains Zayd ibn Abi Ziyad, and he is weak."]]. And from Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Five whose killing is lawful within the Sacred Precinct: the snake, the scorpion, the kite, the rat and the rabid dog" [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in the same place, and al-Tirmidhi in the same place from Aisha, and said: a hasan sahih hadith; and in the chain of Abu Dawud is Ibn Ajlan. It is strengthened by the previous hadith and others.]].

Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said: the rabid dog is every predator that wounds. Malik said the same. The people of opinion (ashab al-ra'y) held that compensation is obligatory for killing what is not eaten, such as the leopard, the panther, the pig and the like, except the specific creatures mentioned in the report; and they analogised the wolf to them, so they did not require expiation for it. Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, analogised to them all that is not eaten, because the hadith includes specific creatures, some of which are harmful predators, some are deadly vermin, and some are birds that do not fall within the meaning of predators, nor are they among the vermin, but are animals whose flesh is considered repugnant; and the prohibition of eating encompasses all of them, so he took this as the basis and attached the ruling to it.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿God made the Ka'bah, the Sacred House﴾. Mujahid said: "It was named Ka'bah because of its squareness (tarbi'), and the Arabs call every square building a ka'bah." Muqatil said: "It was named Ka'bah because it stands apart (infirad) from other buildings." It was also said: "It was named Ka'bah because of its height above the ground." Its root meaning is emergence and elevation. The ankle (ka'b) is called ka'b because it protrudes, emerging from the sides of the foot. And it is said of a girl when she nears puberty and her breasts emerge: taka''abat (she has developed ankle-like breasts).

It was named the Sacred House (al-Bayt al-Haram) because God, exalted is He, made it sacred (harramahu) and magnified its sanctity. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Indeed God, exalted is He, made Makkah sacred on the day He created the heavens and the earth." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Maghazi, chapter 35: 8/26, and Muslim with similar wording in al-Hajj, chapter on the prohibition of Makkah and hunting in it, no. 1353: 2/986, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 7/294.]]

﴿A means of standing for the people﴾. Ibn Amir read (qiyaman) as "qiyaman" without an alif, while the others read "qiyaman" with an alif. The meaning is: a support (qiwaman) for them in the affairs of their religion and their worldly life. As for religion, the Hajj and the rites are established through it. As for worldly life, it is the place to which fruits are brought, and they were safe there from plunder and raids, for no one would attack them within the Sanctuary (al-Haram). God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Do they not see that We have made a secure sanctuary while people are being snatched away from around them?﴾ (al-'Ankabut: 67).

﴿And the sacred month﴾: by this he means the sacred months (al-ashhur al-hurum), which are Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah, al-Muharram and Rajab. He means that He made the sacred months a means of standing for the people, by which they are safe from fighting during them. ﴿And the sacrificial animals (al-hadi) and the garlands (al-qala'id)﴾: he means that they used to feel secure through the garlanding of the sacrificial animals, and that is the support (al-qiwam) in it.

﴿That you may know that God knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth, and that God is Knowing of everything﴾. If it is asked: what connection does this statement have with what precedes it? It is answered: He means that God, may He be exalted, made the Ka'bah a means of standing for the people because He knows the welfare of His servants, just as He knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth. Al-Zajjaj said: "Earlier in this surah there has already been information about the unseen and disclosure of secrets, such as His saying (they are listeners to falsehood, listeners to other people) and His information about their distorting the Books and the like. So His saying ﴿That you may know that God knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth﴾ refers back to that."

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 5, verse 98–100:

﴿Nothing is incumbent upon the Messenger except the conveying (al-tabligh)﴾ [al-Tabligh] [[Omitted from "b".]] ﴿And Allah knows what you reveal and what you conceal.﴾

﴿Say: The evil and the good are not equal﴾, i.e., the lawful and the unlawful, ﴿even if the abundance of the evil pleases you﴾, i.e., gladdens you.

It was revealed concerning Shurayh ibn [Dubay'ah] [[In "a": (Dub'ah), which is an error.]] al-Bakri and Hajjaj ibn Bakr ibn Wa'il [[See above, the occasion of revelation of the second verse of the surah, pp. (7-8).]] ﴿So fear Allah﴾, and do not molest the pilgrims, even if they are polytheists. The story has already passed at the beginning of the surah. ﴿O you who possess understanding, that you may succeed.﴾

﴿O you who believe, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would distress you. And if you ask about them while the Qur'an is being revealed, they will be disclosed to you. Allah has pardoned them, and Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing.﴾ (5:101)

The saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿O you who believe, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would distress you﴾, to the end of the verse. Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Hafs ibn Umar informed us: Hisham, from Qatadah, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: They questioned the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) until they pressed him with questions, so he became angry and ascended the pulpit and said: "Do not ask me today about anything except that I will make it clear to you." So I began looking to the right and left, and there was a man with his head wrapped in his garment, weeping. And there was a man who, when men quarrelled, was called by other than his father's name. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, who is my father?" He said: "Hudhafah." Then Umar began, saying: "We are pleased with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion, and with Muhammad (ﷺ) as Messenger. We seek refuge in Allah from the trials." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have never seen anything in good and evil like today. Paradise and Hell were displayed to me until I saw them behind the wall." Qatadah, when mentioning this hadith, would recite this verse: ﴿O you who believe, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would distress you﴾ [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Fitan, chapter on seeking refuge from trials: 13/43, and Muslim in al-Fada'il, chapter on honouring him (ﷺ) and abstaining from excessive questioning about what is not necessary, no. (2359): 4/1833-1834. The meaning of "ahfawhu": they pressed him insistently and excessively regarding it. It is said: ahfa, alhafa and alahha, with the same meaning. "Lahа": from al-mulahat, which is disputation and argument. "Ansha'a": i.e., began.]].

Yunus narrated from Ibn Shihab: Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah informed me, saying: The mother of Abd Allah ibn Hudhafah said to Abd Allah ibn Hudhafah: "I have never heard of a son more disobedient than you. Are you not afraid that your mother may have committed some of the acts that the women of the Jahiliyyah used to commit, so that she would be disgraced before people?" Abd Allah ibn Hudhafah said: "By Allah, if he had attributed me to a black slave, I would have been attached to him." [[See: Sahih Muslim, in the previous place.]] It is also narrated from Umar that he said: "O Messenger of Allah, we are people recently come from the Jahiliyyah, so pardon us, and Allah, glorified and exalted, will pardon you," and his anger subsided.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 5, verse 98–100:

﴿Nothing is incumbent upon the Messenger except the conveying (al-tabligh)﴾ [al-Tabligh] [[Omitted from "b".]] ﴿And Allah knows what you reveal and what you conceal.﴾

﴿Say: The evil and the good are not equal﴾, i.e., the lawful and the unlawful, ﴿even if the abundance of the evil pleases you﴾, i.e., gladdens you.

It was revealed concerning Shurayh ibn [Dubay'ah] [[In "a": (Dub'ah), which is an error.]] al-Bakri and Hajjaj ibn Bakr ibn Wa'il [[See above, the occasion of revelation of the second verse of the surah, pp. (7-8).]] ﴿So fear Allah﴾, and do not molest the pilgrims, even if they are polytheists. The story has already passed at the beginning of the surah. ﴿O you who possess understanding, that you may succeed.﴾

﴿O you who believe, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would distress you. And if you ask about them while the Qur'an is being revealed, they will be disclosed to you. Allah has pardoned them, and Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing.﴾ (5:101)

The saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿O you who believe, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would distress you﴾, to the end of the verse. Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Hafs ibn Umar informed us: Hisham, from Qatadah, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: They questioned the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) until they pressed him with questions, so he became angry and ascended the pulpit and said: "Do not ask me today about anything except that I will make it clear to you." So I began looking to the right and left, and there was a man with his head wrapped in his garment, weeping. And there was a man who, when men quarrelled, was called by other than his father's name. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, who is my father?" He said: "Hudhafah." Then Umar began, saying: "We are pleased with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion, and with Muhammad (ﷺ) as Messenger. We seek refuge in Allah from the trials." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have never seen anything in good and evil like today. Paradise and Hell were displayed to me until I saw them behind the wall." Qatadah, when mentioning this hadith, would recite this verse: ﴿O you who believe, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would distress you﴾ [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Fitan, chapter on seeking refuge from trials: 13/43, and Muslim in al-Fada'il, chapter on honouring him (ﷺ) and abstaining from excessive questioning about what is not necessary, no. (2359): 4/1833-1834. The meaning of "ahfawhu": they pressed him insistently and excessively regarding it. It is said: ahfa, alhafa and alahha, with the same meaning. "Lahа": from al-mulahat, which is disputation and argument. "Ansha'a": i.e., began.]].

Yunus narrated from Ibn Shihab: Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah informed me, saying: The mother of Abd Allah ibn Hudhafah said to Abd Allah ibn Hudhafah: "I have never heard of a son more disobedient than you. Are you not afraid that your mother may have committed some of the acts that the women of the Jahiliyyah used to commit, so that she would be disgraced before people?" Abd Allah ibn Hudhafah said: "By Allah, if he had attributed me to a black slave, I would have been attached to him." [[See: Sahih Muslim, in the previous place.]] It is also narrated from Umar that he said: "O Messenger of Allah, we are people recently come from the Jahiliyyah, so pardon us, and Allah, glorified and exalted, will pardon you," and his anger subsided.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 5, verses 101–102:

A people used to ask the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) mockingly. A man would say, "Who is my father?" And a man whose she-camel had strayed would say, "Where is my she-camel?" So Allah revealed concerning them this verse: ﴿O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they are disclosed to you, will distress you﴾, until He finished the whole verse [[Recorded by al-Bukhari in the Tafsir of Surat al-Ma'ida, chapter "Do not ask about things which, if they are disclosed to you, will distress you": 8/280.]].

It is also narrated from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: When the verse ﴿And for Allah is the pilgrimage to the House upon mankind﴾ was revealed, a man said, "O Messenger of Allah, is it every year?" He turned away from him until the man asked twice or three times. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "What would make you feel secure that I would not say yes? By Allah, if I had said yes, it would have become obligatory, and if it had become obligatory, you would not have been able to do it. Leave me as I have left you, for those before you were destroyed by their excessive questioning and their disputing with their prophets. So when I command you with something, do of it what you are able, and when I forbid you from something, avoid it." Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they are disclosed to you, will distress you﴾ [[Recorded by al-Tirmidhi from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, in the Tafsir of Surat al-Ma'ida: 8/420, and he said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith from the hadith of Ali." Also Ibn Majah in al-Manasik, no. (2884): 2/963; in Tuhfat al-Ahwadhi he said: "It is munqati' (has a break in its chain)." The original hadith is in Sahih Muslim from the narration of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, in the Book of Hajj, chapter "The obligation of Hajj is once in a lifetime", no. (1337): 2/975; and in the author's Sharh al-Sunnah: 7/3. See also al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/206.]]. That is: if it is made manifest to you, it will distress you; that is, if you are commanded to act upon it. For one who asks about the Hajj cannot feel secure that he will be commanded to perform it every year, and that would distress him. And one who asks about his lineage cannot feel secure that he will be attributed to someone other than his father, and thus be disgraced.

Mujahid said: [The verse] was revealed when they asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the bahira (a she-camel dedicated and left unridden), the sa'iba (a freed animal), the wasila (a she-camel or ewe that bears twins), and the ham (a stallion left free). Do you not see that He mentioned them after that? ﴿And if you ask about them when the Qur'an is being revealed, they will be disclosed to you﴾ [113]. Its meaning: you should be patient until the Qur'an is revealed with a ruling of obligation, prohibition, or judgment, while its apparent meaning does not explain what you need or what your need requires of you. So if you ask about them at that time, they will be made clear to you. ﴿Allah has pardoned that; and Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing﴾.

﴿A people before you asked about them, then they became disbelievers because of them﴾ (102).

﴿A people before you asked about them﴾, as Thamud asked Salih for the she-camel, and the people of Isa asked for the table spread [with food]. ﴿Then they became disbelievers because of them﴾, so they were destroyed. Abu Tha'laba al-Khushani said: "Allah has ordained obligations, so do not neglect them; He has forbidden things, so do not violate them; He has set limits, so do not transgress them; and He has pardoned things without forgetfulness, so do not search for them" [[Recorded by al-Daraqutni as a marfu' report from Abu Tha'laba, and in his Sunan, Kitab al-Radã'a: 4/184; al-Nawawi graded it hasan in al-Arba'in. He also recorded it from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: 4/298, in which there is a story whose chain includes Nahshal al-Khurasani. Ishaq ibn Rahawayh said: "He was a liar." Abu Hatim said: "Matruk (abandoned)." The Hafiz Ibn Rajab said: "This hadith is from the narration of Makhul from Abu Tha'laba. It has two defects: first, that Makhul's hearing from Abu Tha'laba is not authentically established; second, that there is disagreement over whether it is marfu' or mawquf (stopping at Abu Tha'laba). The meaning of the hadith has been related as marfu' through other routes. Al-Bazzar recorded it in his Musnad, and al-Hakim from the hadith of Abu al-Darda', may Allah be pleased with him. Al-Haythami said: al-Tabarani recorded it in al-Kabir from Abu al-Darda', and al-Bazzar, and said: 'Its chain is hasan and its narrators are trustworthy.' He attributed the hadith of Abu Tha'laba to al-Tabarani in al-Kabir and said: 'Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih.' See: Jami' al-Ulum wal-Hikam, pp. 260–261; Majma' al-Zawa'id: 1/171.]].

(﴿Allah has not instituted any bahira, sa'iba, wasila, or ham. But those who disbelieve invent falsehood against Allah, and most of them do not reason﴾ (103).)

His saying, Exalted and Majestic is He: ﴿Allah has not instituted any bahira﴾, that is: Allah did not send it down nor command it. ﴿Nor sa'iba, nor wasila, nor ham﴾. Ibn Abbas said, explaining these practices: The bahira is the she-camel which, when she had borne five offspring, they slit her ear, that is, they split it, and left her from being burdened or ridden, and did not shear her wool, nor prevent her from water or pasture. Then they looked at the fifth offspring: if it was male, they slaughtered it and men and women ate it; if it was female, they slit her ear, that is, they split it and left her, and her milk and her benefits were forbidden to women, and her benefits were exclusively for men. When she died, they became lawful for men and women alike.

It was also said: When a she-camel had given birth to twelve females in succession, she was set free (sa'iba); no one rode her back, her wool was not sheared, and no one drank her milk except a guest. Whatever she bore after that of a female had its ear slit, then it was let loose with its mother among the camels; it was not ridden, its wool was not sheared, and no one drank its milk except a guest, just as had been done to its mother. So it was the bahira, the daughter of the sa'iba.

Abu Ubayd said: The sa'iba is the camel that is set free (yusayyab). This is because a man from the people of the Jahiliyya, when he fell ill or a relative of his was absent, would make a vow saying: "If Allah the Exalted heals me, or heals my sick one, or returns my absent one, then this my she-camel is a sa'iba." Then he would set her free, so she would not be restrained from pasture or water, and no one would ride her. Thus she was in the position of the bahira.

Alqama said: It is the slave who is set free on the condition that he has no wala' (patronage), no 'aql (blood money), and no inheritance. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Wala' belongs only to the one who frees" [[Recorded by al-Bukhari in al-Fara'id, chapter "Wala' belongs to the one who frees": 12/39, and in al-Itq; Muslim in al-Itq, chapter "Wala' belongs only to the one who frees", no. (1504): 2/1141; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 8/348.]].

The sa'iba here is a form with the sense of the passive (maf'ula), meaning the one that is set free (musayyaba), like His saying, ﴿from a gushing fluid﴾ (daafiq, meaning madfuq), and ﴿a pleasing life﴾ (radiya, meaning mardiya).

As for the wasila: among sheep, the ewe, when she had borne seven offspring, and if the seventh was male, they slaughtered it, and men and women ate from it. If it was female, they left it among the sheep. If it was male and female together, they spared the male for the sake of the female, and said, "She has joined her brother (wasalat akhahaa)," so they did not slaughter him. The milk of the female was forbidden to women. If any of them died, men and women ate it together.

As for the ham: it is the stallion camel when his offspring's offspring is ridden. It is said: when ten offspring have been born from his loins, they said, "his back has been protected (huma zahruhu)," so he is not ridden, nor carried upon, nor prevented from pasture or water. When he died, men and women ate him.

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us, that Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, that Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, that Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, that Ibrahim ibn Sa'd informed us, from Salih ibn Kaysan, from Ibn Shihab, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: The bahira is the one whose milk is given to the taghut (idols), so no one among the people milks her. As for the sa'iba, they used to set them free for their gods, and nothing was carried upon them.

Abu Hurayrah said: [The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I saw Amr ibn Amir al-Khuza'i dragging his intestines in the Fire, and he was the first to set free the sawa'ib"] [[Recorded by al-Bukhari in the Tafsir, chapter "Allah has not instituted any bahira, sa'iba, wasila, or ham": 8/283, and Muslim in al-Jannah wa Sifat Na'imiha, chapter "The Fire will be entered by the tyrants", no. (2856): 4/2191.]].

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Taymi, from Abu Salih al-Sammān, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Aktham ibn Jawn al-Khuza'i: "O Aktham, you have seen Amr ibn Luhayy ibn Qam'a [ibn Khandaq] dragging his intestines in the Fire, and I have seen no man more resembling a man than you resemble him, nor he more than you resemble him." That is because he was the first to change the religion of Isma'il, set up the idols, slit the ears of the bahira, set free the sa'iba, bound the wasila, and protected the ham. "I saw him in the Fire harming the people of the Fire with the smell of his intestines." Aktham said: "Will his resemblance harm me, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "No, for you are a believer and he is a disbeliever" [[Recorded by al-Tabari in his Tafsir: 11/118; and Ibn Ishaq in al-Sira: 1/76. Ibn Hajar also attributed it to Ibn Abi Urwa and Ibn Mandah through the route of Ibn Ishaq, then said: "The hadith is recorded in Muslim through the route of Suhayl ibn Salih from his father, more briefly than this, without the story of Aktham" (and he refers to the previous hadith). See: al-Isaba: 1/107; Usd al-Ghaba: 1/133; Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 2/108; al-Bidaya wal-Nihaya: 2/187–189.]].

His saying, Exalted and Majestic is He: ﴿But those who disbelieve invent falsehood against Allah﴾ in their saying, "Allah has commanded us with them," ﴿and most of them do not reason﴾.

﴿When it is said to them, "Come to what Allah has revealed and to the Messenger,"﴾ concerning the permissibility of tillage and livestock and the explanation of the laws and rulings, ﴿they say, "Sufficient for us is what we found our fathers upon,"﴾ of religion. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Even though their fathers knew nothing and were not guided?﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 5, verse 104:

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿O you who believe, take care of your own selves; he who strays cannot harm you if you are guided﴾. It has been related to us from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "O people, you recite this verse: ﴿O you who believe, take care of your own selves; he who strays cannot harm you if you are guided﴾ and you put it in other than its proper place, and you do not understand what it is. I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'When people see an evil and do not change it, Allah the Exalted is about to encompass them with His punishment.'" [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Malahim, Bab al-Amr wa'l-Nahy: 6/187; al-Mundhiri attributed it to al-Nasa'i. Also narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Fitan, Bab ma ja'a fi nuzul al-'adhab idha lam yughayyar al-munkar: 6/388, and he said: hasan sahih; he also narrated it in al-Tafsir. Ibn Majah narrated it in al-Fitan, Bab al-Amr bi'l-ma'ruf wa'l-nahy 'an al-munkar (4005): 2/1327, and Ibn Hibban authenticated it (1837) p. 455. Also Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 1/5, 7; Abu Bakr al-Marwazi in Musnad al-Siddiq pp. 128-131; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/344.]].

And in another narration: "You must enjoin what is good and forbid what is evil, or else Allah, glorified and exalted, will set over you your worst among you, and they will inflict on you the worst torment. Then your best will supplicate Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, but their supplication will not be answered [for you]." [[The words in parentheses are omitted in "B".]] [[Narrated by al-Khatib in Tarikh Baghdad: 13/92; al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Awsat, and al-Bazzar in his Musnad. Al-Haythami said: in it is Hibban ibn 'Ali, who is abandoned (matruk), and Ibn Ma'in declared him trustworthy in one narration and weak in others. Al-'Iraqi said: both of its chains are weak. See: Majma' al-Zawa'id: 7/266; Fayd al-Qadir: 5/261.]].

Abu 'Ubayd said: al-Siddiq feared that people would interpret the verse in a way other than its intended meaning, which would lead them to abandon enjoining good and forbidding evil [and forbidding evil]. [[The words in parentheses are omitted in "B".]] So he informed them that it is not so, and that what is permitted to be left unchanged of evil is the shirk that the covenant-bound (mu'ahadun) utter, because they adhere to it as their religion and have been reconciled upon it. As for wickedness (fusuq), disobedience (usyan), and doubt among the people of Islam, these do not fall under it.

Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: the verse refers to the Jews and Christians, meaning: ﴿take care of your own selves; he who strays among the People of the Book cannot harm you﴾, so take the jizyah from them and leave them.

From Ibn Mas'ud, he said regarding this verse: "Enjoin good and forbid evil as long as it is accepted from you; if it is rejected from you, then take care of your own selves." Then he said: "Some verses of the Qur'an have been revealed whose interpretation had already passed before they were revealed; some whose interpretation occurred in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ); some whose interpretation will occur shortly after the Messenger of Allah; some whose interpretation will occur at the end of time; and some whose interpretation will occur on the Day of Resurrection, namely what is mentioned of the reckoning, Paradise and Hellfire. So long as your hearts and desires are united, and you do not become divided into factions, and some of you do not taste the violence of others, then enjoin and forbid. But when hearts and desires diverge, you are made to wear factions, and some of you taste the violence of others, then each man must look to himself. At that point comes the interpretation of this verse."

Akhbaranā 'Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi told us: Abu Ja'far Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-'Anzi told us: 'Isa ibn Nasr told us: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak told us: 'Utbah ibn Abi Hakim told me: 'Amr ibn Jariyah al-Lakhmi told us: Abu Umayyah al-Sha'bani told us, saying: I came to Abu Tha'labah al-Khushani and said: "O Abu Tha'labah, how do you act regarding this verse?" He said: "Which verse?" I said: "The saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿take care of your own selves; he who strays cannot harm you if you are guided﴾." He said: "By Allah, you have asked about it one who knows. I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about it, and he said: 'Rather, enjoin one another to good and forbid one another from evil, until you see stinginess obeyed, desire followed, the world preferred, and every person pleased with his own opinion; and you see a matter for which you have no choice but to act, then take care of yourself and leave the affairs of the common people. For behind you are days of patience; whoever endures in them is like one who grasps a live coal. For the one who acts in them is like the reward of fifty men who do the same deeds as his.'" Ibn al-Mubarak said: "Someone else added to me: they said, 'O Messenger of Allah, the reward of fifty of them?' He said: 'The reward of fifty of you.'" [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Malahim, Bab al-Amr wa'l-Nahy: 6/188-189; al-Tirmidhi in the Tafsir of Surat al-Ma'idah: 8/423-426, and he said: hasan gharib; Ibn Majah in al-Fitan, Bab qawlihi ta'ala "ya ayyuha alladhina amanu 'alaykum anfusakum" (4014): 2/1330-1331; Ibn Hibban (1850) p. 457, and al-Hakim authenticated it: 4/322, and al-Dhahabi agreed. It has supporting reports by which it is strengthened. The author also narrated it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/347.]].

It was also said: it was revealed concerning the people of desires (ahl al-ahwa'). Abu Ja'far al-Razi said: a young man from among the people of desires came to Safwan ibn Muhriz and mentioned some of his affair, so Safwan said: "Shall I not direct you to the special favor of Allah which He has bestowed upon His friends: ﴿O you who believe, take care of your own selves; he who strays cannot harm you if you are guided﴾."

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿To Allah is your return, all of you﴾, the one who strayed and the one who was guided, ﴿then He will inform you of what you used to do﴾.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 5, verse 105:**

﴿O you who have believed, let there be [a witness] among you when death approaches one of you at the time of bequest: two just men of your own [community], or two others from outside your [community], if you are travelling through the land and the calamity of death befalls you.﴾ [Mentioned in its complete form below.]

God the Exalted said: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا شَهَادَةُ بَيْنِكُمْ﴾ (O you who have believed, let there be testimony among you). The cause of the revelation of this verse is what is narrated: that Tamim ibn Aws al-Dari and Adi ibn [Badda] [[In the two manuscripts it reads "Zayd", which is an error. The correction is from al-Tirmidhi and others.]] left Medina for trade towards the land of Syria. They were both Christians, and with them was Budayl, the freedman of Amr ibn al-As, who was a Muslim. When his illness grew severe, he made a bequest to Tamim and Adi, and instructed them to deliver his goods to his family when they returned. Budayl died, and they searched his goods and took from them a silver vessel decorated with gold, which weighed three hundred mithqals of silver. They concealed it, then completed their business and returned to Medina, and delivered the goods to the household. They searched the goods and found the list in which was recorded what Budayl had with him. They came to Tamim and Adi and said: "Did our companion sell any of his goods?" They said: "No." They said: "Did he engage in trade?" They said: "No." They said: "Was his illness prolonged so that he spent on himself?" They said: "No." They said: "We have found in his goods a list in which is recorded what he had with him, and we have lost from it a silver vessel overlaid with gold, weighing three hundred mithqals of silver." They said: "We do not know. He only bequeathed to us something, and he instructed us to deliver it to you, and we delivered it, and we have no knowledge of the vessel." They brought the dispute before the Prophet ﷺ, but they insisted on their denial and swore oaths. Then God the Exalted revealed this verse: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا شَهَادَةُ بَيْنِكُمْ إِذَا حَضَرَ أَحَدَكُمُ الْمَوْتُ حِينَ الْوَصِيَّةِ اثْنَانِ﴾ (O you who have believed, let there be testimony among you when death approaches one of you at the time of bequest: two [witnesses]). [[See al-Tirmidhi, Tafsir Surat al-Ma'idah: 8/426-431, where he narrates the report and says: "This is a strange hadith, and its chain is not sound." The Abu al-Nadr from whom Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated this hadith is, in my view, Muhammad ibn al-Sa'ib al-Kalbi, whom the scholars of hadith abandoned. Something of this has been narrated from Ibn Abbas in summary by another route. See also: al-Tabari: 11/185; al-Wahidi, Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 245; Ibn al-Arabi, Ahkam al-Qur'an, 2/713-717. Al-Suyuti also attributed it to Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Nahhas in al-Nasikh wa al-Mansukh, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, and Abu Nu'aym in al-Ma'rifah. See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/220-221.]] That is: let two witness, the phrasing being that of a report but its meaning being a command.

It was also said: the meaning is that the testimony among you concerning the bequest at the time of death is two [persons]. They differed about who these two are. Some said: they are the two witnesses who testify to the bequest of the testator.

Others said: they are the two executors (wasiyyan), because the verse was revealed concerning them, and because He said: ﴿تَحْبِسُونَهُمَا مِنْ بَعْدِ الصَّلَاةِ فَيُقْسِمَانِ﴾ (you shall detain them after the prayer, and they shall swear), and an oath is not required of a witness. The executor is made two for emphasis. According to this view, the word "shahadah" (testimony) carries the meaning of presence, as in your saying: "I witnessed the bequest of so-and-so," meaning "I was present." God the Exalted said: ﴿وَلْيَشْهَدْ عَذَابَهُمَا طَائِفَةٌ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ (and let a group of the believers witness their punishment) [al-Nur: 2], meaning presence.

﴿ذَوَا عَدْلٍ﴾ (two just men): that is, trustworthy and sound of mind. ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾ (of your own): that is, of the people of your religion, O assembly of believers. ﴿أَوْ آخَرَانِ مِنْ غَيْرِكُمْ﴾ (or two others from outside your [community]): that is, from outside your religion and your community, according to the view of most commentators. This was said by Ibn Abbas and Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, and it is the view of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid and Ubaydah.

Then these scholars differed concerning the ruling of the verse. [[For a detailed treatment see: Ahkam al-Qur'an of al-Jassas: 4/163 ff.; Ahkam al-Qur'an of al-Tabari, edited by al-Harras, 3/310-314; Ahkam al-Qur'an of al-Shafi'i, collected by al-Bayhaqi: 2/147-155.]] Al-Nakha'i and a group said: it is abrogated (mansukhah, "naskh" meaning abrogation of an earlier ruling by a later one), and the testimony of the People of the Book (ahl al-kitab) was accepted at the beginning and then abrogated.

Others held that it is still in force, and they said: if we do not find two Muslims, we call upon two disbelievers.

Shurayh said: whoever is in a land of exile and does not find a Muslim to witness his bequest, and calls upon two disbelievers, of whatever religion they are, whether of the People of the Book or idol-worshippers, their testimony is permitted. The testimony of a disbeliever against a Muslim is not permitted, except for a bequest made during travel.

It is narrated from al-Sha'bi that a man from among the Muslims was approaching death at Daquqa, and he did not find a Muslim to witness his bequest, so he called upon two men from the People of the Book. They came to Kufa with his estate and came to al-Ash'ari. Al-Ash'ari said: "This is a matter that did not occur after the time of the Prophet ﷺ." He then had them swear oaths, and he approved their testimony.

Others said: the statement ﴿ذَوَا عَدْلٍ مِنْكُمْ﴾ (two just men of your own) means: from the tribe of the testator; ﴿أَوْ آخَرَانِ مِنْ غَيْرِ حَيِّكُمْ وَعَشِيرَتِكُمْ﴾ (or two others from outside your tribe and clan). This is the view of al-Hasan, al-Zuhri and Ikrimah. They said: the testimony of a disbeliever is not permitted in any of the rulings.

﴿إِنْ أَنْتُمْ ضَرَبْتُمْ﴾ (if you travel): that is, if you journey and go on a journey, ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ فَأَصَابَتْكُمْ مُصِيبَةُ الْمَوْتِ﴾ (through the land, and the calamity of death befalls you). Then you make a bequest to the two and entrust your property to them, and some of the heirs suspect them and claim against them treachery. The ruling in that case is that ﴿تَحْبِسُونَهُمَا﴾ (you shall detain them), that is, you shall hold them back, ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ الصَّلَاةِ﴾ (after the prayer), that is, after the prayer. The word ﴿مِنْ﴾ here is superfluous (silah); it means "after the prayer of the afternoon." This is

The opinion of al-Sha'bi, al-Nakha'i, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Qatadah and the majority of exegetes (mufassirun) is that this is because all the people of the religions revere that time and avoid false oaths during it. Al-Hasan said: he meant after the afternoon prayer (salat al-'asr). Al-Suddi said: after the prayer of their own religion and community, because they do not care about the afternoon prayer. ﴿Then they will swear﴾ means they will take an oath, ﴿by God, if you doubt﴾, meaning if you become suspicious and feel doubt about the testimony of the two witnesses and their truthfulness, that is, about the words of the two who are not from your religious community. If they are Muslims, then no oath is required of them. ﴿We will not sell it for any price﴾ means: we will not swear falsely by God in exchange for any gain we take, any wealth we carry off, or any right we deny. ﴿Even if it were a near relative﴾ means: even if the one in whose favor the testimony is given is a relative of ours. ﴿Nor will we conceal the testimony of God﴾: he attributed the testimony to God because He commanded its establishment and forbade its concealment. Ya'qub read "shahadatan" with tanwin, "Allah" elongated, and made the interrogative (istifham, question particle) a substitute for the oath particle (harf al-qasam). It is narrated from Abu Ja'far that he read "shahadatan" with tanwin and "Allah" with a cut alif and a kasra on the ha', without an interrogative, as the beginning of an oath, meaning: "By God." ﴿Indeed, we would then be among the sinners﴾, meaning: if we concealed it, we would be among the sinners.

When this verse was revealed, the Messenger of God ﷺ prayed the afternoon prayer, called Tamim and 'Adi, and had them swear at the pulpit (minbar) by God, besides whom there is no god, that they had not betrayed anything of what had been entrusted to them. They swore to that, and the Messenger of God ﷺ let them go.

Then the vessel appeared, and they differed about how it appeared [[See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/222.]]. Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that it was found in Makkah, and they said: "We bought it from Tamim and 'Adi." Others said: when the period was long, they (the two executors) displayed it, and this reached the Banu Sahm, who came to them about it. The two said: "We had bought it from him." They said to them: "Did you not claim that our companion had not sold any of his goods?" They replied: "We had no evidence, and we disliked admitting it to you, so we concealed it for that reason." So they brought the two of them before the Messenger of God ﷺ, and God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Then if it is discovered﴾.

﴿Then if it is discovered﴾ means: if their betrayal is discovered. The root of 'uthur (discovery) is coming upon something. ﴿That they both﴾, meaning the two executors (al-wasiyyayn), ﴿deserved﴾, meaning became liable, ﴿sin﴾, by their betrayal and their false oaths. ﴿Then two others﴾ from the heirs of the deceased ﴿will stand in their place﴾, meaning in place of the two executors, ﴿from among those who have been wronged﴾. The verb is read with a damma on the ta' in the passive; this is the reading of the majority, meaning "those who have been wronged" (istahagga). ﴿Against them﴾ means: concerning them and on their account, the sin, and they are the heirs of the deceased, whose sake the two swearers deserved the sin on account of. "'Ala" here means "fi" (in), as God says: ﴿over the kingdom of Solomon﴾ (al-Baqarah 2:102), meaning in the kingdom of Solomon. Hafs read "istahagga" with a fatha on the ta' and the ha', and this is the reading of 'Ali and al-Hasan, meaning: the sin became due and binding upon them. It is said that haqqa and istahagga have the same meaning. ﴿The two nearest﴾ is an attribute (na't) of "two others", meaning: two others, the two nearest. This is permissible even though "the two nearest" is definite and "two others" is indefinite, because when he described "two others" by saying ﴿from among those who﴾, it became like a definite noun. "Al-awlayan" is the dual of "al-uwla", and "al-uwla" means "the nearest". Hamzah, Abu Bakr from 'Asim, and Ya'qub read "al-awlayn" in the plural, so it becomes a substitute (badal) for "those who". The intended meaning of them is also the heirs of the deceased.

The meaning of the verse is: when the betrayal of the two swearers is revealed, two others from the relatives of the deceased will stand up, ﴿and they will swear by God: "Our testimony is more worthy than their testimony"﴾, meaning our oath is more worthy than their oath. A parallel is God's statement regarding li'an (mutual oath-cursing): ﴿the testimony of one of them is four testimonies by God﴾ (al-Nur 24:6). What is meant by testimony there is oaths, so it is like the saying of one who says: "I bear witness by God," meaning: "I swear by God." ﴿And we have not transgressed﴾ in our oaths and in our claim that our testimony is more worthy than theirs, ﴿for indeed we would then be among the wrongdoers﴾.

When this verse was revealed, 'Amr ibn al-'As and al-Muttalib ibn Abi Wada'ah al-Sahmiyyan stood up, and they swore by God after the afternoon prayer, and they handed over the vessel to them and to the heirs of the deceased. Tamim al-Dari, after he had embraced Islam, used to say: "God and His Messenger spoke the truth. I took the vessel. So I repent to God and seek His forgiveness." The oath was transferred to the heirs because the two executors claimed that they had purchased it.

When an executor takes something from the property of the deceased and says: "He bequeathed it to me," the heir swears if he denies that. Likewise, if a man claims a commodity in the possession of another man, and he admits it, then claims that he bought it from the claimant, the claimant swears that he did not sell it to him.

It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas [[In the earlier narration of al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan: 8/426-431.]], may God be pleased with them both, from Tamim al-Dari, that he said: "We had sold the vessel for a thousand dirhams, and I and 'Adi divided it. When I embraced Islam, I felt guilty, so I went to the clients (mawali) of the deceased and informed them that my companion had a similar amount. They brought it to the Messenger of God ﷺ, and 'Amr and al-Muttalib swore. So five hundred was taken from 'Adi, and I returned the five hundred."

That is His saying, exalted be He: ﴿That is more likely that they will give testimony in its true form﴾

﴿That is more likely that they will give testimony in its true form﴾ meaning: that ruling which We have passed, namely the return of the oath, is more fitting and more appropriate that the two executors will bring the testimony in its true form, and so will the rest of the people like them; i.e., it is closer to bringing the testimony as it was. ﴿Or they would fear that oaths would be returned after their oaths﴾ meaning: it is closer to their fearing that the oath will be returned after their oath to the claimant (in "B": "the claimants"), so that they swear to their treachery and their lying and are exposed and made to pay, and so they do not swear falsely when they fear this ruling. ﴿And fear Allah﴾ that you swear false oaths or betray a trust. ﴿And listen﴾ to the admonition. ﴿And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 5, verse 109:

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿On the day when Allah will gather the Messengers﴾, and it is the Day of Resurrection, ﴿and He will say: "What was your answer?"﴾ That is: What did your nations answer you? And what did your people reply to you when you called them to My Oneness and My obedience? ﴿They will say﴾, that is, they will say: ﴿"We have no knowledge."﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: its meaning is, "We have no knowledge except that knowledge which You know better than we do." It was also said: "We have no knowledge of the wisdom behind Your asking us about a matter of which You know better than we do." Ibn Jurayj said: "We have no knowledge of the final outcome of their affairs or of what they innovated after us." The proof for this is that He said: ﴿Indeed, You are the Knower of the unseen⁠﴾, that is: You are the One who knows what is hidden, while we know only what we witness.

'Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi informed us, (who said): Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, (who said): Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, (who said): Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, (who said): Muslim ibn Ibrahim informed us, (who said): Wuhayb informed us, (who said): 'Abd al-'Aziz informed us, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Some people from among my companions will come to me at the Basin, and when I recognize them, they will be pulled away from me. So I will say: 'My companions!' And it will be said:

*Ma'alim al-Tanzil* of al-Baghawi, on surah 5, verses 110–111:

"I do not know what they introduced after you" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Riqaq, chapter on the Basin (al-Hawd)... 11/464, and by Muslim in al-Fada'il, chapter on affirming the Basin of our Prophet (ﷺ) and its attributes, no. (2304): 4/1800.]].

Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan, Mujahid and al-Suddi said: Indeed, the Day of Resurrection has terrors and convulsions, in which hearts will leave their places. They will be frightened by the horror of that day and will be stunned, unable to answer. Then, after their minds have returned to them, they will bear witness against their nations.

His Exalted saying: ﴿When Allah said: "O Jesus, son of Mary, remember My favour upon you"﴾. Al-Hasan said: Remembering a favour is giving thanks for it. By His saying ﴿My favour﴾ He means "My favours." The word is singular but its meaning is plural, as in His saying: ﴿And if you count Allah's favours, you cannot enumerate them﴾. ﴿And upon your mother﴾, Mary. Then He mentioned the favours, saying: ﴿When I strengthened you﴾, I supported you, ﴿with the Holy Spirit﴾, meaning Jibril (peace be upon him), ﴿you spoke to people﴾, meaning: and you spoke to people, ﴿in the cradle﴾ as an infant, ﴿and in maturity﴾ as a prophet. Ibn 'Abbas said: He was sent when he was thirty years old, and he remained in his mission for thirty months, then Allah raised him to Himself. ﴿And when I taught you the Book﴾, meaning writing, ﴿and wisdom﴾, meaning knowledge and understanding, ﴿and the Torah and the Gospel. And when you shaped﴾, you made and formed, ﴿out of clay what was like the form of a bird﴾, like the shape of a bird, ﴿by My permission, and you breathed into it and it became a bird﴾, living and flying, ﴿by My permission. And you healed﴾, and cured, ﴿the blind and the leper by My permission. And when you brought forth the dead﴾ from their graves alive, ﴿by My permission. And when I restrained﴾, I held back and turned away, ﴿the Children of Israel﴾, meaning the Jews, ﴿from you﴾, when they intended to kill you, ﴿when you came to them with clear proofs﴾, meaning the evidences and miracles, which we have mentioned.

﴿Those who disbelieved among them said: "This is nothing but clear magic."﴾ That is: what he brought them of clear proofs. Hamza and al-Kisa'i read ﴿sahirun mubin﴾ ("a clear magician") here and in Surah Hud and as-Saff. In that case it refers back to 'Isa (peace be upon him). In Hud it refers back to Muhammad (ﷺ).

﴿And when I inspired the disciples﴾, I cast into their hearts and put into their minds. Abu 'Ubayda said: it means "I commanded," and ﴿ila﴾ (to) is a *silah* (a superfluous particle). The Hawariyyun (the closest disciples) were the special companions of 'Isa (peace be upon him). ﴿That you believe in Me and in My Messenger﴾ ([Isa]) ﴿They said﴾, when I agreed with them, ﴿"We believe, and bear witness that we are Muslims."﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 5, verses 112–113:

إِذْ قَالَ الْحَوَارِيُّونَ يَا عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ هَلْ يَسْتَطِيعُ رَبُّكَ (115)

al-Kisa'i recited "هَلْ تَسْتَطِيعُ" with a ta' and "رَبَّكَ" with a fatha on the ba'. This is the recitation (qira'ah) of Ali, Aishah, Ibn Abbas and Mujahid. The meaning is: "Can you ask and beseech your Lord?" Others recited "هَلْ يَسْتَطِيعُ" with a ya' and "رَبُّكَ" with a damma on the ba'. They did not say this out of doubt about the power of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, but its meaning is: "Will your Lord send down (a table) or not?" This is like a man saying to his companion, "Can you stand up with me?" while he knows that he is able to, and he only means, "Will you do that or not?" It is also said that "yastati'" means "yuti'" (obey). It is said that "ata'a" and "istata'a" have one meaning, like their saying "ajaba" and "istajaba". The meaning is: "Will your Lord obey you by answering your request?" In the narrations it is said: "Whoever obeys Allah, Allah obeys him." Some of them kept the apparent meaning and said: "The people erred." They said this before the knowledge was firmly established, and they were human. So Jesus, peace be upon him, when they erred, said to them, glorifying their statement: ﴿Fear Allah, if you are believers﴾, meaning: do not doubt His power.

[114/b]

﴿That He send down upon us a table from heaven﴾. The "ma'idah" is the spread on which the food is placed. It is a form (fa'ilah) from "mada, yamiduhu", when he gives and feeds someone, like their saying "mara, yamiruhu". "Imtad" is its reflexive form (ifta'ala). The "ma'idah" is that which feeds those who eat the food. The food is also called "ma'idah" by extension, because it is eaten upon the table. The people of Kufa said: it was named "ma'idah" because it sways (tamid) with those who eat, that is, it inclines. The people of Basra said: it is a "fa'ilah" in the sense of "maf'ulah", that is, it sways with those who eat towards it, like the verse "a pleasing life" (ʿīshatin rāḍiyah), meaning "a pleased-with life."

﴿He said﴾: Jesus, peace be upon him, replying to them: ﴿Fear Allah, if you are believers﴾, so do not doubt His power. It is also said: "Fear Allah" means that you should not ask Him for anything that the nations before you did not ask of their prophets. So he forbade them from demanding signs after faith.
