The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 5, verse 114:

It means: we only asked because we want ﴿to eat from it﴾, eating for blessing (tabarruk), not eating out of need, so that ﴿we may be assured of His power, and our hearts may be at rest﴾, and be calm and tranquil, ﴿and know that you have indeed told us the truth﴾ that you are the Messenger of Allah. That is: we may increase in faith and certainty. It was also said: Jesus, son of Mary, commanded them to fast thirty days, and that when they broke their fast they would ask Allah for nothing without being given it. So they did this and asked for the table (al-Ma'idah), and they said: ﴿and know that you have indeed told us the truth﴾ in your saying that when we fast thirty days, we ask Allah the Exalted for nothing without Him giving it to us. ﴿And we will be among the witnesses to it﴾, witnessing for Allah with His oneness and power, and for you with prophethood and messengership. It was also said: ﴿and we will be among the witnesses for you﴾ before the Children of Israel when we return to them.

﴿Jesus, son of Mary, said﴾ at that point: ﴿O Allah, our Lord, send down to us a table from heaven﴾. It was said that he performed ritual washing, put on a woollen garment, prayed two rak'ahs, bowed his head, lowered his gaze and wept. Then he said: O Allah, our Lord, send down to us a table from heaven, ﴿that it may be a festival for us, for the first of us and the last of us﴾, that is: a favour from You to us and a proof and evidence. The word ʿīd (festival) means a day of joy. It is named so because it returns (yaʿūd) from sorrow to joy. It is also a name for what you are accustomed to and what returns to you. The day of al-Fitr and al-Adha are called festivals because they return every year. As-Suddi said: its meaning is that we take the day on which it was sent down as a festival, for the first of us and the last of us, that is, we and those after us honour it. Sufyan said: we pray on it. His saying ﴿for the first of us﴾ means for the people of our time, ﴿and the last of us﴾ means for those who come after us. Ibn ʿAbbas said: the last of the people will eat from it just as the first of them ate. ﴿And a sign from You﴾, a proof and evidence. ﴿Provide for us, for You are the best of providers.﴾

﴿Allah said﴾, the Exalted, responding to Jesus, peace be upon him: ﴿Indeed, I will send it down to you﴾, meaning: the table. The people of Medina, Ibn ʿAmir and ʿAsim read munazziluhā with the doubled letter (tashdid), because it was sent down repeatedly, and the form with tafʿīl indicates repetition, one time after another. The others read it without doubling (takhfif), in line with His saying: "send down to us". ﴿But whoever among you disbelieves after that﴾, that is, after the table is sent down, ﴿I will surely punish him with a punishment﴾, that is, a punishment of a kind, ﴿that I will not inflict upon anyone among the worlds﴾, meaning: the worlds of his time. The people denied and disbelieved after the table was sent down, so they were transformed into apes and swine. ʿAbdullah ibn ʿUmar said: The people who will suffer the most severe punishment on the Day of Resurrection are the hypocrites, those among the people of the table who disbelieved, and the family of Pharaoh.[[Narrated by Ibn Jarir al-Tabari as a statement of ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAmr: 11/233. Shaykh Ahmad Shakir authenticated it in ʿUmdat al-Tafsir. As-Suyuti also attributed it to ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Abu ash-Shaykh, likewise as a statement (mawquf). Al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/237.]]

The scholars differed concerning the table: was it sent down or not? Mujahid and al-Hasan said: it was not sent down, because when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, threatened them for their disbelief after the table would be sent down, they feared that some of them would disbelieve, so they sought to be excused and said: "We do not want it." So it was not sent down. His saying ﴿Indeed, I will send it down to you﴾ means: if you ask.[[The view of Mujahid and al-Hasan, may Allah have mercy on them both, is a less preferred opinion, and they did not rely on a sound report. It also contradicts the text of the verse "Indeed, I will send it down to you." Therefore al-Baghawi and others preferred the view of the majority, which is the correct one.]]

The correct view, which most scholars hold, is that it was sent down, based on His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, I will send it down to you﴾. There is no dispute about this report, because the reports about it are widely transmitted from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the Companions and the Successors.

They differed about its description. Khilas ibn ʿAmr related from ʿAmmar ibn Yasir, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that it was sent down as bread and meat, and they were told: "It will remain for you as long as you do not betray [and conceal]"[[Addition from manuscript B.]], but their day had not passed before they betrayed and concealed, and so they were transformed into apes and swine.[[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir from ʿAmmar ibn Yasir, both as a marfuʿ and a mawquf report: 11/228-229. Also by at-Tirmidhi in the chapter on Surah al-Ma'idah: 8/433, who said: "This is a gharib hadith. Abu ʿAsim and others narrated it from Saʿid ibn Abi ʿArubah, from Qatadah, from Khilas, from ʿAmmar, as a mawquf report. We do not know it as marfuʿ except through the hadith of al-Hasan ibn Qazaʿah ... and we do not know any basis for the marfuʿ hadith."]]

Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: Jesus, peace be upon him, said to them: "Fast thirty days, then ask Allah for whatever you wish, and He will give it to you." So they fasted. When they finished, they said: "O Jesus, if we worked for someone and completed his work, he would feed us." They asked Allah for the table, and the angels approached bearing a table, on which were seven loaves and seven fishes, until they placed it before them. The last of the people ate from it just as the first of them ate.[[It should be noted here that the basic account is established by the Noble Qur'an, and understanding it does not depend on the many reports that the commentators cited to describe this table, how it was sent down, and the time of its descent, etc. These reports are transmitted from Wahb ibn Munabbih, Kaʿb al-Ahbar, Salman, Ibn ʿAbbas, Muqatil, al-Kalbi, ʿAta, and others. Their chains are not established, and even where a report's attribution to its speaker is sound, that does not mean it is sound in itself. A report from Wahb, for example, may be transmitted with an established chain, yet be derived from the People of the Book (Israiliyyat). Therefore the books of tafsir should be purified of such reports, including what al-Baghawi cites here. Ibn Kathir, al-Qurtubi, Ibn ʿAtiyyah and others have pointed out the weakness of these Israili reports. And Allah knows best. See also: al-Isra'iliyyat wal-Mawdu'at by Dr. Muhammad Abu Shahbah, pp. 266-277.]]

Kaʿb al-Ahbar said: a table was sent down upside down, flown by the angels between heaven and earth, and on it was every food except meat.

Saʿid ibn Jubayr related from Ibn ʿAbbas: everything was sent down on the table except bread and meat. Qatadah said: on it was fruit from the fruits of Paradise.

ʿAtiyyah al-ʿAwfi said: a fish came down from heaven having the taste of everything.

Al-Kalbi said: on it was bread, rice and herbs.

Wahb ibn Munabbih said: Allah sent down loaves of barley and fish, and a group of people would eat, then leave, and others would come and eat, until they had all eaten and there was some left over.

From al-Kalbi and Muqatil: Allah sent down bread, fish and five loaves. They ate what Allah willed, and the people numbered a thousand and more. When they returned to their villages and spread the news, those who had not witnessed it laughed at them and said: "Woe to you! He has only bewitched your eyes." Whoever Allah wished good for, He kept steadfast in his insight, and whoever He wished to test returned to his disbelief. They were transformed into swine, with no child or woman among them. They remained so for three days, then died. They did not reproduce, did not eat and did not drink, and so is every transformed creature.

Qatadah said: it used to come down to them morning and evening wherever they were, like the manna and quails for the Children of Israel. ʿAta ibn Abi Rabah, from Salman al-Farisi, said: when the disciples (al-Hawariyyun) asked for the table, Jesus, peace be upon him, put on wool and wept, and said: "O Allah, send down to us a table from heaven," and the verse continues. Then a red cloth came down between two clouds, one cloud above it and one cloud below it, while they watched it descending swiftly until it fell before them. Jesus wept and said: "O Allah, make me among the grateful. O Allah, make it a mercy and do not make it a punishment." The Jews looked at a thing the like of which they had never seen, and they had never smelled a fragrance better than its fragrance. Jesus, peace be upon him, said: "Let the best of you in deed stand up, uncover it, and mention the name of Allah, the Exalted." Shamʿun al-Saffar, the leader of the disciples, said: "You are more deserving of that than us." So Jesus, peace be upon him, stood, performed ablution, prayed a long prayer and wept much. Then he uncovered the cloth from it, saying: "In the name of Allah, the best of providers." Behold, it was a roasted fish without its scales and without bones, dripping with fat, with salt by its head and vinegar by its tail, and around it were various kinds of herbs except leeks, and there were five loaves: on one was olives, on the second honey, on the third ghee, on the fourth cheese, and on the fifth dried meat. Shamʿun said: "O Spirit of Allah, is this from the food of this world or from the food of the Hereafter?" He said: "None of what you see is from the food of this world or from the food of the Hereafter, but it is a thing Allah created by overpowering might. Eat of what you asked for, and He will increase you and give you more of His bounty." They said: "O Spirit of Allah, be the first to eat from it." Jesus, peace be upon him, said: "I seek refuge in Allah from eating from it; rather, whoever asked for it will eat from it." They feared to eat from it, so he invited the needy, the sick, the lepers, the elderly, the handicapped and the afflicted, and said: "Eat of the provision of Allah; for you is the ease, and for others is the trial." They ate, and there departed from it one thousand three hundred men and women, poor, sick, disabled and afflicted, all of them satisfied. Behold, the fish was in the same form as when it had descended. Then the table-cloth ascended, rising upward while they looked at it until it disappeared. No disabled person, no sick person and no afflicted person ate from it without being healed, and no poor person without being made rich. Whoever did not eat from it regretted it. It remained for forty mornings, descending at midday, and when it descended the rich and the poor, the young and the old, men and women gathered. It was never taken down, and it was eaten from

...from it, until when the shade declined, it would fly off while they watched its shadow, until it disappeared from them. It used to descend every other day, descending one day and not descending the next, like the she-camel of Thamud. Then God Most High revealed to [Jesus, peace be upon him] [[The text between the brackets is missing from manuscript "B".]]: "Make My table and My provision for the poor, not for the rich." This weighed heavily on the rich, so they raised doubts and cast doubt on it among the people, saying: "Do you think the Table truly descends from heaven?" So God Most High revealed to Jesus, peace be upon him: "I have stipulated that whoever disbelieves after its descent, I will punish him with a punishment that I will not inflict upon anyone among the worlds." Jesus, peace be upon him, said: ﴿If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ Then three hundred and thirty men of them were transformed, having spent the night on their beds with their wives, and by morning they were pigs running about in the roads and the refuse heaps, eating filth in the latrines. When the people saw this, they fled to Jesus, peace be upon him, and wept. When the pigs saw Jesus, peace be upon him, they wept and began circling around Jesus, peace be upon him, and Jesus would call them by their names, and they would nod their heads and weep, but they could not speak. They lived three days and then died.

And when God said: ﴿O Jesus, son of Mary, did you say to the people, "Take me and my mother as two gods besides God?"﴾ He said: ﴿Glory be to You! It is not for me to say what I have no right to say. If I had said it, You would have known it. You know what is in my soul, and I do not know what is in Your soul. Indeed, You are the Knower of the unseen.﴾ ﴿I did not say to them except what You commanded me: "Worship God, my Lord and your Lord." And I was a witness over them while I was among them. But when You caused me to die, You were the Watcher over them, and You are a Witness over everything.﴾ ﴿If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Mighty, the Wise.﴾

Regarding His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And when God said, "O Jesus, son of Mary, did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as two gods besides God?'"﴾ They differed as to when this statement will occur. Al-Suddi said: God Most High said this statement to Jesus, peace be upon him, when He lifted him up to heaven, because the particle "idh" (when) refers to the past. The rest of the commentators said: God will say this to him on the Day of Resurrection, as evidenced by His saying before it, ﴿On the day when God gathers the messengers﴾ (al-Ma'idah 5:109), and His saying after it, ﴿This is a day when the truthful will benefit from their truthfulness﴾ (al-Ma'idah 5:119). By both He meant the Day of Resurrection. The particle "idh" may also come in the sense of "idha" (when), as in His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿If only you could see when they are terrified﴾ (Saba' 34:51), meaning "when they are terrified" [on the Day of Resurrection]. [The text between the brackets is missing from manuscript "B".] The Resurrection, though it has not yet occurred, is as though it has occurred, because it is coming without doubt.

His saying: ﴿Did you say to the people, "Take me and my mother as two gods besides God?"﴾ If it is asked: What is the purpose of this question, given that God, Mighty and Majestic, knows that Jesus did not say it?

It is answered: This question is put to him to rebuke his people and to magnify the gravity of this statement, just as one person says to another: "Did you do such-and-such?"

And likewise? [He asks] about what He knows he did not do, to inform and to magnify the matter, not to inquire or question.

Also: God, Mighty and Majestic, wished to have Jesus (peace be upon him) acknowledge his own servanthood, so that his people would hear it and their lie against him, that he had commanded them to it, would be exposed. Abu Rawq said: When Jesus (peace be upon him) heard this address, his joints trembled, and from the root of every hair on his body a spring of blood gushed forth. Then he replied to God, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿He said: Glory be to You﴾, exalting and magnifying You, ﴿it is not for me to say what I have no right to say. If I had said it, You would have known it. You know what is in my soul, and I do not know what is in Your soul﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: You know what is in my unseen, and I do not know what is in Your unseen. It was also said that its meaning is: You know my secret, and I do not know Your secret. Abu Rawq said: You know what came from me in the life of this world, and I do not know what will come from You in the Hereafter. Al-Zajjaj said: "nafs" (self) is an expression for the whole of a thing and its reality. He means: You know all that I know of the reality of my affair, and I do not know the reality of Your affair. ﴿Indeed, You are the Knower of the unseen things﴾, what has been and what will be.

﴿I did not say to them except what You commanded me: "Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord." And I was a witness over them as long as I remained among them. But when You took me up, You were the Watcher over them, and You are a Witness over all things﴾ (5:117).

﴿Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord﴾: [Affirm His oneness] and do not associate anything with Him. ﴿And I was a witness over them as long as I remained﴾, I stayed, ﴿among them. But when You took me up﴾, You seized me and raised me up to You, ﴿You were the Watcher over them﴾, the Guardian over them, keeping watch over their deeds, ﴿and You are a Witness over all things﴾.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿If You punish them, they are Your servants. And if You forgive them, indeed You are the Almighty, the Wise﴾ (5:118). If it is asked: how could he ask for forgiveness for them when they were disbelievers? And how could he say "if You forgive them, indeed You are the Almighty, the Wise", when this does not suit a request for forgiveness? It is answered: As for the first, its meaning is: if You punish them for persisting in their disbelief, and if You forgive them after faith. This fits the view of al-Suddi, that this request was made before the Day of Resurrection, because faith does not benefit on the Day of Resurrection.

It was also said: this refers to two groups among them: its meaning is, if You punish those among them who disbelieved, and if You forgive those among them who believed.

It was also said: this is not in the form of asking for forgiveness. Had it been so, he would have said: "indeed You are the Forgiving, the Merciful." Rather, it is in the form of submitting the matter and entrusting it to His will.

As for the second question: Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) used to recite ﴿and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Mighty, the Wise﴾ as "*wa-in taghfir lahum fa-innaka anta al-ghafur al-rahim*" [the reading of his codex], and it is so in his codex. As for the well-known recitation (*qira'ah*, a canonical mode of recitation), it has been said that there is an inversion (*taqdim wa-ta'khir*) in it, its intended meaning being: "if You forgive them, indeed they are Your servants, and if You punish them, indeed You are the Almighty, the Wise."

It was also said: its meaning is: if You punish them, indeed they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Almighty in dominion, the Wise in judgment; nothing diminishes from Your might, and nothing goes outside Your rule. And within His wisdom, His forgiveness, and the vastness of His mercy and forgiveness, He may admit the disbelievers. But He has informed that He does not forgive them, and He does not break His report.

Ismail ibn 'Abd al-Qahir informed us: Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad al-Farisi narrated to us: Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Juludi narrated to us: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan narrated to us: Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj narrated to me: Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us: Ibn Wahb informed me: 'Umar ibn al-Harith informed me that Bakr ibn Sawada narrated to him, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, that the Prophet (ﷺ) recited the saying of God, Exalted, concerning Abraham: "My Lord, they have led many people astray. Whoever follows me is of me..." [Qur'an 14:36], to the end of the verse, and the saying of Jesus (peace be upon him): "If You punish them, they are Your servants, and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Almighty, the Wise" [Qur'an 5:118]. Then he raised his hands and said: "O Allah, my community (*ummati*)," and he wept. Then God, Mighty and Majestic, said: "O Gabriel, go to Muhammad, and your Lord knows best; ask him what makes him weep." Gabriel came to him and asked him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) informed him of what God had said. Then God, Exalted, said: "O Gabriel, go to Muhammad and say: Indeed We shall please you regarding your community, and We shall not grieve you."

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 5, verse 118–119:

﴿Allah said: "This is a day when the truthful will benefit from their truthfulness."﴾ 115/b Nafi' read (yawma) with a fatha on the mim, meaning: these things will occur on a day, so the adverb (fi) was elided and the word became accusative (intasaba). The others read it with a damma, as the predicate (khabar) of (hadha), meaning: their truthfulness will benefit the truthful in this world, and in the Hereafter, if they had lied, Allah would have sealed their mouths and their limbs would have spoken, and they would have been disgraced. It is also said that by "the truthful" they meant the Prophets.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 5, verse 118–119:

﴿Allah said: "This is a day when the truthful will benefit from their truthfulness."﴾ 115/b Nafi' read (yawma) with a fatha on the mim, meaning: these things will occur on a day, so the adverb (fi) was elided and the word became accusative (intasaba). The others read it with a damma, as the predicate (khabar) of (hadha), meaning: their truthfulness will benefit the truthful in this world, and in the Hereafter, if they had lied, Allah would have sealed their mouths and their limbs would have spoken, and they would have been disgraced. It is also said that by "the truthful" they meant the Prophets.

Al-Kalbi said: "Their faith benefits the believers."

Qatadah said: "Two speakers who will not err on the Day of Resurrection: Jesus, peace be upon him, concerning whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, related the account, and the enemy of Allah, Iblis. His statement is: 'And Satan will say when the matter has been decided,' [and the rest of the verse]. The enemy of Allah spoke truthfully on that day, though before that he had been lying, so his truthfulness did not benefit him. As for Jesus, peace be upon him, he was truthful in this world and the Hereafter, so his truthfulness benefited him."

Ata said: "This is a day from the days of this world, because the Hereafter is an abode of recompense, not an abode of action." Then He explained their reward, saying: ﴿For them are gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. That is the great attainment.﴾ Then He magnified Himself, saying: ﴿To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them, and He is over all things competent.﴾
